> **Both halves are needed.** The switch is what starts it; making the column
> does not. And after adding any column in Grist, go back to the spreadsheet
> card and pick your table again — we cache the column list when you pin it, so
> a column added since is one the agent has never been told about.

## Things worth knowing

**One row per conversation.** Every answer goes into the same row, so you get one
line per customer rather than one line per thing they said.

**The agent fills in only what it was told.** A field it never heard is left
empty. It will not guess.

**Formula columns are read, not written.** Grist computes those itself. If
*every* column in the table is a formula we say so when you pick it — the agent
can read that table but cannot save anything into it.

**Looking something up is exact and case-sensitive.** `PRIYA` does not match
`Priya`. Use it for order numbers, phone numbers and reference codes, which is
what customers give verbatim anyway.

**It will not search for nothing.** If the agent has no value to match on it asks
the customer for one, rather than returning whatever happens to be at the top of
your table.

**At most five rows come back from a lookup.** More than that read aloud is a
paragraph nobody can follow on a phone.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **If you rename or delete a column in Grist, tell us.** We remember your columns
> from when you picked the table. Rename one and saves start failing. Fixing it
> takes ten seconds: open the card and choose the table again.

**Free Grist has limits, and they are Grist's rather than ours.** A free site
allows **3,000 API calls a month** and **5,000 rows per document**. A busy phone
line can use those, and when they are gone Grist refuses — your card says so.
*Save in the background* handles the smaller bumps for you.

**Disconnecting keeps your data.** Rows already written stay in your spreadsheet;
they are your records, not ours to remove. Anything still queued and not yet
written is discarded, and we tell you how many that is before you are left
wondering.

## If it stops working

The card says **Needs attention** and shows what Grist said.

Usually it is one of three things: the key was removed in Grist, the document is
full or out of monthly calls, or a column was renamed. Create a new key and use
**Replace key** if it is the first — your switches and your chosen table are
remembered.

## Deliberately not included

The agent cannot reach **any other document or table**, even though your API key
could. It cannot **create or delete columns, tables or documents**, and it cannot
**delete rows**. It fills the one table you pointed it at, and reads from it.

Nobody phoning your business has a good reason to reshape your spreadsheet, and
the safest way to guarantee that is not to give the agent the ability at all.


# Website & app agent
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/agent/website-and-app-agent

Let your agent see the screen your customer is on, fill it in, point at the right button and step in when they get stuck.

Switch this on and your agent stops being a chat in the corner. On your website
— and, with the mobile SDKs, inside your app — it can see the screen your
customer is on: the form, which fields are empty, the error under a field, the
buttons. It answers about what is in front of them, fills fields in, points at
the next step, and offers help on its own when someone gets stuck. By chat or by
voice.

## Switch it on

**1. Open the agent**

Go to **Agents**, open the agent on your website, and choose **Website & app**
under **Deploy**.

**2. Turn it on**

Switch on **Let the agent see and use the screen** and **Save**. If your chat
widget is already on your site, there is nothing else to add: it works on the
next page load.

**3. Choose what it may do**

Every action is on until you switch it off: point at a field or button, scroll
to it, put the cursor in a field, type into fields, choose from drop-downs,
tick boxes, press buttons and links, open another page of your site, and run
your own actions.

**4. Add the moments it steps in (optional)**

Under **When it steps in**, add a moment: what happens, on which pages, after
how long, and what the agent says. Set **At most … per visit**.

## What it always does — whatever you switch on

* It **never reads or fills** passwords, card numbers, CVV, OTP, Aadhaar or PAN
  fields.
* It sees **whether** a field is filled, not **what** is in it — unless you mark
  the field readable (below).
* PAN, Aadhaar and card numbers shown on the page are masked before anything
  leaves it, and page addresses leave without their query string.
* A button that **pays, submits or confirms** is pressed only after your customer
  taps **Allow** in the chat. If they tap **Not now**, the agent tells them so and
  leaves it to them.
* It never touches anything you mark off-limits.

## The moments it steps in

| Moment | What it means |
| - | - |
| The person has not done anything for a while | No typing, tapping or scrolling for the time you set |
| A field shows an error | An error stays on screen for the time you set |
| The same field fails twice | They fixed it, and it failed again |
| Clicks the same thing again and again | Three or more clicks on one spot within a second |
| Clicks something that does nothing | Nothing on the page changed after the click |
| Moves to leave the page | Desktop only: the pointer leaves the top of the window |
| Has been on the page for a while | Time on the page passes what you set |

**On pages containing** takes part of the page address (`checkout`, `/kyc`) or
the screen name your site sets (below). Leave it empty for every page. Each
moment shows at most once per page, never while the chat is open, and never more
than your per-visit limit. The message appears beside the chat button; a tap
opens the chat with the agent already talking.

## Tell it more (optional)

Add these after the widget tag:

```html theme={null}
<script>
  // The step the person is on, and facts the agent should know.
  AgentWidget.setScreen("kyc_address", { step: 3, product: "personal loan" });

  // Something that happened. The agent sees the last ten.
  AgentWidget.track("upload_failed");

  // An action of your own the agent may run on this page, with your customer's own session.
  AgentWidget.registerAction(
    "retry_upload",
    {
      description: "Retry uploading the document the customer chose",
      parameters: [{ name: "document", type: "string", description: "Which document", required: true }],
    },
    async ({ document }) => {
      const ok = await myApp.retryUpload(document);
      return { uploaded: ok };
    },
  );
</script>
```

Action names are lowercase with underscores. Whatever your function returns is
what the agent is told. Nothing your function does passes through ThinnestAI.

## Control element by element (optional)

```html theme={null}
<!-- Never read or touched by the agent -->
<div data-ta-mask>…</div>
<!-- Seen, but never typed into or clicked -->
<button data-ta-no-touch>Delete account</button>
<!-- The agent may read this field's value (hidden by default) -->
<input name="city" data-ta-allow />
<!-- Always ask before pressing / never ask -->
<button data-ta-confirm>Renew</button>
<button data-ta-safe>Next</button>
```

## Voice

If the agent takes calls on your website (**Voice → where it answers → Website**),
it can act on the screen during a call too. The call shrinks to a small bar with
the agent's name, a live caption, mute and hang-up, so your customer sees their
details go in while they talk. Anything that pays or submits still waits for
**Allow** in the chat.

## Mobile apps

SDKs for **Android, iOS, React Native and Flutter** are in early access. They show
the same agent — chat, voice, cards and forms — in a sheet over your app. Your app
describes each screen to the agent (its fields, their state and errors) and
carries out the actions in its own code. [Ask us for access](mailto:support@thinnest.ai).

## FAQ

> [accordion] Does it slow my website down?
>
> The extra script loads only when this is switched on for the agent, and it
> reads the page only while the chat is open or a call is on.

> [accordion] Can the agent submit a form by itself?
>
> It can fill the form. Pressing a button that submits, pays or confirms waits
> for your customer to tap Allow. To never let it press a particular button,
> mark it `data-ta-no-touch`.

> [accordion] Why does it say a field is filled but not what is in it?
>
> By design: values stay on your customer's device. Add `data-ta-allow` to a
> field the agent may read, such as a city or plan name — never to anything
> personal.


# Workflows
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/agent/workflows

Call, message and follow up with each contact over days — and let AI read every call and pick what happens next.

A workflow takes one contact at a time through a journey you draw: Agent calls them, AI reads the call and decides
how it went, the workflow waits, sends a WhatsApp or an SMS, calls again — whatever you connect. Each contact goes
through on their own, at their own pace, and you can see where every one of them is.

Open **Workflows** in the sidebar, then **Create workflow**:

* **Describe it, and AI builds it.** Say what should happen in a few sentences — *"When someone gets the tag new-lead,
  Riya calls them. If they're interested, send the brochure on WhatsApp and tell the sales team…"* — and AI draws the
  workflow, choosing your agents and templates by name. It is saved as a draft: look it over, fill what is marked in
  red (a template's blanks, an agent it could not tell apart), then publish. It can start on a date too (*"call
  patients the day before their visit"*) and add an **Extract details** step.
* **Start from a ready-made one**: qualify new leads, call back missed calls, appointment reminders, clinic
  appointment confirmations, payment reminders, document chase, win back old customers.
* **Start from a blank canvas.**

> [!NOTE]
>
> A workflow never changes an agent. A call it places is that agent's call in every way — its instructions, voice,
> steps and actions. The workflow decides only **when** to call or message and **what follows**. If you never use
> Workflows, nothing about your agents changes.

## What starts it

The **Start when** card at the left of the canvas:

| Start when | What happens |
| - | - |
| **Contacts I choose** | Press **Start** and pick a contact group, or everyone with a tag. |
| **A tag is added** | The moment a contact gets the tag, from the Contacts page or a workflow. |
| **A call ends** | After a phone or WhatsApp call — answered, missed, or cut off part-way — on any agent, or one you choose. **Which calls**: calls to your number (the default), calls Agent made (campaigns, callbacks), or both. A campaign call nobody picked up is never a missed call unless you choose it. Website and Playground conversations don't count, and neither does a call where Agent flagged the caller as spam. |
| **A form is sent** | When someone sends one of your WhatsApp forms. |
| **Your system asks** | Your CRM, website or app starts one contact through it — see [below](#start-it-from-your-system). |
| **A date on the contact** | Days before or after a date the contact holds — a visit, a renewal, a birthday — at the time you choose, in the contact's own clock. See [below](#start-on-a-date). |
| **An incoming webhook** | Any tool — a form builder, your shop, Zapier — posts to this workflow's own address. No API key, no fixed format. See [below](#start-from-a-webhook). |
| **On a schedule** | Every day, a weekday each week, or a day each month, at a time in your workspace's clock, for a contact group or everyone with a tag. |

Add **Only if…** to take through only the contacts who match — a tag, their name, email, phone or language, or
one of their own details.

Contacts without a phone number are skipped, and nobody is ever in the same workflow twice at once.

### Start from a webhook

Choose **An incoming webhook** and the card shows the workflow's own address. Paste it into your tool as where to send,
then tell the card where things are in what it sends:

* **Phone** (required), and optionally the **name** and **email**: a path into what the tool posts — `customer.phone`,
  `data.0.mobile`. Send a test from your tool and press **Refresh**: the card then suggests the paths it saw, with
  their values. A form post's field names (`customer.phone`) work as they are.
* **Keep a detail on the contact**: more of what it sends, saved as the contact's details (`visit_date` from
  `booking.date`), for **A date on the contact**, a **Conditional**, or `{{contact.visit_date}}`.

It takes JSON or a form post, up to 64 KB. A number without its country code takes your workspace's country. A new
number becomes a contact; a name or email fills a gap but never overwrites one you have. The address is the key: keep
it secret, and **Make a new address** if it leaks — the old one stops at once. One address starts at most 1,000 runs an
hour. Your tool gets `201` when a run started, `200` when they are already going through it, `202` when the workflow is
not live (what it sent is still kept for the mapping), `422` when there was no phone number where the card looks.

### Start on a date

Choose **A date on the contact**, name the detail that holds the date (`visit_date`), how many days before or after it,
and the time: *1 day before visit_date, at 10:00*. Each contact whose date falls due is started that day, once the
time comes.

* **The contact's own clock.** 10:00 is 10:00 where they are, worked out from their number, as calling hours are. A
  number from a country spanning several time zones (the US) starts once it is 10:00 at the far end; a number that says
  nothing about where it is uses your workspace's clock.
* The detail holds a date written `2026-11-02` (year, month, day). **Extract details** saves dates that way, and
  **importing contacts** turns a column of dates like `02/11/2026` into it: day first, or month first for a file
  imported for US and Canadian numbers, unless a date in the column settles it (25/12 can only be day first). A column
  with anything in it that is not a real date is kept exactly as it was. Through the API, send `2026-11-02`.
* **Once for each date.** A contact is started once per date, whatever **Settings** says about going through again; a
  new date (next month's visit) starts them again. A run still going holds a new one back.
* Only on the day. If a date is changed to one that is already past, nobody is started for it.

## The blocks

Drag a block from the **Blocks** list onto the canvas, or click it. Draw from a block's right-hand dot to the next one.
Everything about a block is set on the block itself. **Tidy up**, at the top right of the canvas, lays every block out
left to right in the order the workflow runs, with a decision's answers top to bottom as you listed them.

| Block | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Call** | Agent calls the contact, from Agent's own number, inside the call window you set, with retries after busy, no answer or failed. Fill Agent's variables from the contact or from earlier blocks. |
| **Send WhatsApp** | Sends an approved template from your WhatsApp number, with its blanks filled. A reply reaches the agent that answers that number. |
| **Send SMS** | Sends a DLT template through your own SMS provider. |
| **AI decides** | AI reads a call and picks one of the answers you name — *Interested*, *Call back later*, *Not interested* — each with its own path. Below the confidence you set, it takes **Unsure**. |
| **Extract details** | AI reads a call and saves what the customer said into the contact's own details — a budget, a visit date, yes or no to a question. Name each detail and say what it is. |
| **Conditional** | Checks a rule — how a call went, an API's answer, a contact's details or tags — and goes **Match** or **No match**. |
| **Await** | Waits for a time (15 minutes, a day…), until a date and time, or for something to happen: they reply on WhatsApp, send a form, call you, get a tag, or your system sends an event. It takes **Arrived** when it happens and **Timeout** if it does not within the time you give it. |
| **Action** | Sends to, or reads from, your CRM or any API. Later blocks can use its answer. It goes **Success** on an answer in the 200s and **Failed** on any other answer or none; leave Failed unconnected and the run carries on down Success. |
| **Send to CRM** | Saves the contact in the CRM one of your agents has connected — [Zoho, Bigin or HubSpot](/agent/crm) — filling the fields pinned there from the contact and earlier blocks. It updates their record when one matches, else makes one. **Saved** or **Failed**; Failed left unconnected goes on as Saved. |
| **Book on calendar** | Books a meeting on the calendar one of your agents has connected — [Cal.com or Calendly](/agent/calendar) — at a time the run holds (`{{contact.visit_at}}`, or `2026-11-02 10:30`), in your workspace's clock (the contact sees it in theirs), for the contact's email. **Booked**; **Link instead** when the calendar cannot book directly (Calendly's free plan): the one-time link is `{{block.link}}`, for a WhatsApp after it; **Failed**. A booking's open exits end the run: it never goes on as if booked. |
| **Update contact** | Adds or removes tags, sets one of the contact's details (empty clears it), and can **assign** their conversations to a teammate or a **team** (Settings → Teams: the member with the fewest conversations assigned gets it), as the inbox does — they are told, and it shows under **Mine**. A tag added here starts and stops sequences and workflows just as one added by hand. |
| **Tell the team** | Your owners and admins, or a **team** you choose (Settings → Teams), get a notification, and an email if their notification settings send one. A team with nobody in it tells the owners and admins instead. |
| **Split test** | Sends each contact down one of two to four paths at random, by share — to find out which works better. |

### How sure AI decides should be

**Review decisions** on an **AI decides** block lists its recent answers on real calls — what AI said, how sure it
was, and the call's summary (switch on *Summarise each call* on the agent to see it). Mark the right answer for each,
or *A person should decide* when none fits.
From your marks it finds the lowest bar at which AI was right often enough — pick 90, 95, 98 or 99% — and says what
that means: *at 82% sure, AI settles 400 of 500 on its own, at least 98% right; 100 go to Unsure, for a person*.
**Use** sets it as the block's bar; publish to use it, and wire **Unsure** to a person (**Tell the team**, or
**Update contact** → assign).

The bar is set cautiously: twenty right answers out of twenty do not prove 99%, so a small sample earns a modest bar
and more marks earn a surer one. At least ten marked answers are needed before a bar is offered.

### A contact's own details

Besides a name, email, phone, language and tags, a contact keeps its own details — `budget`, `visit_date`, `doctor`.
They come from:

* **Extract details**, which saves what the customer said on a call;
* **Update contact**, which sets one, filled from anything earlier in the workflow;
* **Importing contacts**: every column of your file besides the number, name, email and language is kept under its
  header (*Appointment Time* becomes `appointment_time`). A blank cell keeps what the contact already had;
* the [contacts API](/api-reference/contacts/update-contact), as `fields`;
* **An incoming webhook**, from what the tool posts.

A later block reads one as `{{contact.budget}}`, and a **Conditional** checks it as a contact field. Calls an agent
places fill its `{{visit_date}}` from the contact too, on any call, not only a workflow's; a caller ringing in is not
given them. Names are written
in lower case with underscores; a contact holds up to 30, each up to 300 characters. They show under the contact's name
in **Contacts**.

When a call starts the workflow, **AI decides**, **Extract details** and **Conditional** can read that call too: choose
*The call that started this run*. Its outcome is *answered*, *no answer*, *busy*, *voicemail* or *failed* (cut off part-way). Agent
answers every call to your number, so a caller who needs ringing back is one whose outcome is anything but
*answered* — the **Call back missed calls** starter checks exactly that.

### Filling blanks

Anywhere you fill a blank or a variable, type text or pick a value: the contact's name, phone or email, an earlier
call's **summary** or **outcome**, or an earlier action's answer.

In an **Action**, values are written safely for where they go: encoded in the address (a `+` in a phone number stays a
`+`), escaped inside a JSON body (a quote in somebody's name can't break it), and kept to one line in a header.

## Settings

**Settings** in the builder's header:

* **Stop a contact's run when** they reply on WhatsApp, or get a tag you name (say, *booked*). Anyone who asks not to be
  contacted, or is on your do-not-call list, is always stopped.
* **Goal** — the AI decides answer that counts as success. The **Workflows** page shows how many runs reached it.
* **A contact can go through it again**: never, after their last run ends, or 30 days after it.
* **Quiet hours** — no calls or messages between these times, in the contact's own time (read from their number;
  for a country with several time zones, it must be outside quiet hours in all of them). A Call block's call window
  is the contact's time too.
* **End a run after** a number of days (up to 30).
* **Start at most** a number of contacts an hour. The rest wait their turn at Start and go in as room opens — for a
  big list, a busy webhook or a schedule over thousands. Test runs are never held back.

## Publish, test and start

* **Publish** saves a new version. Runs already going finish on the version they started on. If something would stop
  the workflow working — a call with no agent, an unapproved template, a blank left empty — it is marked in red under
  **to check**, and Publish waits until it is fixed. Amber items are worth a look but don't stop you.
* **Test** runs the canvas as it is now — saved or not — on your own phone. Tick **Skip waits** to turn a day's wait
  into seconds. Tests make real calls and send real messages. For a workflow that starts when a call ends, choose
  how that call went — missed, answered, cut off or busy — and the test begins as if it had.
* **Start** (for *Contacts I choose*) picks the group or tag and starts them.
* **Runs** shows the latest contacts and, for each, what happened block by block. The download button gives every
  run as a CSV: who, the block they are on or ended on, whether they reached the goal, when, and why it ended.
* **History** lists the published versions. **Restore** brings one back as the draft, canvas and settings; nothing
  changes for contacts until you publish it.
* **Results** puts the last 30 days on the canvas: how many reached each block, and how many took each AI answer.

## Start it from your system

Set **Start when** to **Your system asks** — the card then shows the exact address to call, with this workflow's id
and a copy button — and publish. Then call
[Start a Workflow Run](/api-reference/workflows/start-a-workflow-run) with a full API key:

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/workflows/wf_…/runs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "to": "+91 98765 43210", "name": "Asha", "variables": { "order": "10432" } }'
```

* A number you have never sent before becomes a new contact, so a fresh lead can go straight in.
* `variables` are this run's own values: a blank written `{{contact.order}}` fills from `order`.
* `started: false` (not an error) means they are already going through it, or the workflow's settings don't let them
  go through it again.

### Clinic appointment confirmations

The ready-made **Clinic appointment confirmations** workflow sends a WhatsApp reminder, waits three hours for a reply,
and calls the patient if none comes. AI then sorts the call into **Coming**, **Moved** or **Cancelled**: confirmed and
cancelled patients are tagged, your front desk is told about a moved visit or a freed slot, and a patient who could not
be reached gets a text. For the call, pick the pre-built **Appointment confirmations** agent (**Agents** > **Start from a
pre-built agent**): it checks it is speaking to the patient before it mentions the visit, rebooks from your open times,
and never gives medical advice.

Start it the day before each visit with the visit's time and doctor. Import tomorrow's patients with an
*Appointment Time* and a *Doctor* column and start it for them, or have your clinic system start each one:

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/workflows/wf_…/runs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "to": "+91 98765 43210", "name": "Asha", "variables": { "appointment_time": "tomorrow at 11 am", "doctor": "Dr Menon" } }'
```

* [List Workflows](/api-reference/workflows/list-workflows) gives every workflow's id and what starts it;
  [Get a Workflow](/api-reference/workflows/get-a-workflow) gives its blocks and, for one your system starts, the
  address to send runs to.
* **Tell a waiting run what happened.** An Await set to *Your system sends an event* waits for an event you name, such
  as `payment_received`. Send it with [Send a Workflow Event](/api-reference/workflows/send-a-workflow-event):

  ```bash theme={null}
  curl -X POST https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/workflows/events \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{ "to": "+91 98765 43210", "event": "payment_received" }'
  ```

  Only events sent after the run reached the Await count.
* From an AI assistant, the MCP tools `list_workflows`, `start_workflow_run` and `send_workflow_event` do the same. The SDKs have
  `workflows.list`, `workflows.get`, `workflows.startRun` and `workflows.sendEvent`.

## Good to know

* Calls and messages are billed exactly as any other call or message. AI decides is not charged.
* Calls keep the usual calling hours in the contact's own time, your plan's lines, and your balance. When every line
  is busy, contacts wait their turn rather than fail.
* On a call a workflow places, the agent's own **[After the call](/agent/after-the-call)** messages are not sent — the
  workflow decides what follows, so the contact never gets both.
* **Pause** a workflow from its menu on the Workflows page: contacts wait where they are until you resume it.
  **Delete** stops every run still going.


# Create Action
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/create-action

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/actions
Give the agent a call to your own API, with placeholders it fills from what the customer said. Dotted placeholders are filled by the platform, never the model: `{{call.id}}` (the id `GET /calls` lists), `{{call.from}}`, `{{call.to}}`, `{{call.direction}}` (empty outside a call), `{{conversation.id}}`, `{{contact.id}}`, `{{contact.phone}}`, `{{agent.id}}`, `{{workspace.id}}` and `{{test.chat}}` (`true` during a test chat, empty otherwise) — in the path, query, body or a header value, never the host; an unknown one is refused. Every call also sends `X-Call-Id`, `X-Conversation-Id`, `X-Agent-Id` and `X-Workspace-Id` when known, and `X-Test-Chat: true` during a test chat (`POST /agents/{id}/test-chat`), where the call values are empty and `X-Call-Id` is absent — so your endpoint can answer without writing anything. A new action is always **off**: test it with `POST …/test`, then `PATCH` `enabled: true` — sending `enabled` here is refused. Header values are sealed on arrival and never returned. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Action
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/delete-action

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}/actions/{actionId}
Remove the action and its sealed headers. The agent stops being able to call it at once. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Action
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/get-action

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/actions/{actionId}
One action. Header values never appear; only `headerNames`.

# List Actions
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/list-actions

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/actions
The agent's actions — calls to your own HTTPS API that it may make mid-conversation — newest first. Header values never appear; only `headerNames`.

# Test Action
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/test-action

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/actions/{actionId}/test
Make the call once, for real, through the same address checks and credentials the agent uses — and it works while the action is still off, which is the point. A test has no conversation, so only `{{agent.id}}` and `{{workspace.id}}` fill; the rest are empty. A failed call is still `200`, with `ok: false`. On a `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` action the test **does** the write. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Action
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/actions/update-action

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}/actions/{actionId}
Change any field, or switch it on or off with `enabled`. The action is validated as it will be saved, so a new `url` is checked against the parameters already there. Leaving `headers` out keeps the saved credential; sending any replaces the whole set. `enabled: true` makes it callable from every conversation at once. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Agent
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/create-agent

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents
Makes an agent exactly as the console does: a starter persona when you send no `instructions`, a website widget key, and (where your deployment has voice) a voice channel that answers on the web and WhatsApp. Only `name` is required. The plan's agent allowance, its model list and its voice tiers apply; a refused voice undoes the whole create. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Agent
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/delete-agent

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}
Deletes the agent and everything under it: its conversations, knowledge, actions and channels. It cannot be undone. A **build** key may do this.

Refused with `409` `agent_on_live_call` while the agent is on a call (ringing or connected): deleting it then would lose that call's recording, transcript, analysis and usage. Delete it after the call ends.

# Get Agent
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/get-agent

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}
One agent: its instructions, model, languages, script, widget, call settings and the details it collects from calls. Which engine speaks its voice or runs its model is never part of the answer.

# Get Agent BYOK Model
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/get-agent-byok-model

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/byok-model
On a workspace that brings its own keys: the model this agent runs on your own LLM key. `model` is the agent's own choice (null when it runs the key's model), and `stale` names an earlier choice your key no longer reaches, which the key's model answers in place of. Refused with `409` when the workspace is not using its own keys, or when this agent is set to `byok: "off"` (it then runs on our models, and a choice you set is not available to read until you put it back on the workspace's keys).

# Get Agent BYOK Voice
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/get-agent-byok-voice

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/byok-voice
On a workspace that brings its own keys: the voice this agent speaks with on your own voice provider. `voice` is null for the provider's default voice. A choice belongs to the provider it was made on; after you switch your voice key to another provider, `stale` holds the old choice and calls speak the new provider's default until you choose again. On a Cartesia key the response also holds how the voice sounds: `speed`, `volume`, `emotion`, `agentModel` (this agent's own Sonic model; `model` is always your key's) and `pronunciationDictId`, each null while unset. Refused with `409` when the workspace is not using its own voice key (it brings no keys, or only its language model), or when this agent is set to `byok: "off"` (it then speaks in our voices).

# List Agents
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/list-agents

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents
Every agent in your workspace, newest first, in the same shape Get Agent returns. Page with `limit` and `cursor`.

# Set Agent BYOK Model
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/set-agent-byok-model

/api-reference/openapi.json put /agents/{id}/byok-model
Chooses which model of your own LLM key this agent runs. It must be one the key reaches — listed under `byok.models` by List Models — or `null` to run the key's own model (the one set under Settings → Your keys). The next reply uses it. A **build** key may do this.

# Set Agent BYOK Voice
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/set-agent-byok-voice

/api-reference/openapi.json put /agents/{id}/byok-voice
Chooses the voice this agent speaks with on your own voice provider: an id from List BYOK Voices, checked against the provider's list for your key, or `null` for the provider's default. On Cartesia an id that is not on the list yet, such as a voice cloned a moment ago, is checked with Cartesia directly and accepted if your key owns it. The agent needs a voice channel first. A **build** key may do this.

On a Cartesia key you can also set how this agent's voice sounds: `speed` (0.6 to 1.5), `volume` (0.5 to 2.0), `emotion` (one of Cartesia's values; English only), `model` (`sonic-3.6`, `sonic-3.6-2026-08-27`, `sonic-3.5`, `sonic-3` or `sonic-2` for this agent alone; `sonic-3.6` follows Cartesia's latest stable snapshot, the dated one never changes) and `pronunciationDictId` (a dictionary id from your Cartesia account). Every field is optional and the request only changes what it names: a key left out stays as it is, `null` goes back to the default, a value sets it. So `{ "voice": "…" }` alone changes the voice and keeps the settings; `{ "voice": null }` goes back to the provider's default voice and clears them. The settings belong to a voice of the agent's own: sending one before a voice is chosen, or with `voice: null`, is refused. `speed`, `volume` and `emotion` need a Sonic 3 model, and `speed` does not apply to a Cartesia Professional Voice Clone. A refused field answers `400` with `code: validation_failed` and `field` naming it.

# Test Chat
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/test-chat

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/test-chat
Talks to your real agent through its website chat — the same prompt, model, knowledge, actions, limits and billing as the console's Playground — and answers with its reply and every tool it used. It runs as a sandbox: anything that would phone, message, email or send a code to a person, or change a calendar booking, is switched off and the agent says what it would have done instead; your own actions still run for real, and every request they make carries an `X-Test-Chat: true` header (and `{{test.chat}}` fills as `true`) so your endpoint can answer without writing anything. The conversation appears in your inbox; send `session` back to continue it. It always runs the agent as saved: there is no separate draft, so a change you save is live at once. To try a change first, create a second agent with it (Create Agent) and test that one. A reply costs what a chat reply costs: on an agent using its own language-model key, the flat ₹0.02 own-key reply price. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Agent
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/agents/update-agent

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}
Changes any subset of the fields Create Agent takes and answers with the whole agent. Fields you leave out are untouched, and unknown fields are ignored — but a body that names no field this API knows is refused. A model or voice is checked against your plan only when it changes, and a refused voice refuses the whole patch before anything is written. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Agent Analytics
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/analytics/get-agent-analytics

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/analytics
What the agent's Analytics page shows: totals, conversations/replies/leads per day, conversations by hour and by channel, the questions it could not answer and the questions asked most. Windows are rolling `days`; hours and days are UTC. `resolved` and `escalated` count conversations by their current status. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Get Dashboard
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/analytics/get-dashboard

/api-reference/openapi.json get /dashboard
The console Dashboard's figures for the whole workspace: how many agents, numbers, knowledge documents, campaigns, keys, members, contacts and leads; conversations unread and waiting on a person; calls in the last 30 days; and the balance as the account card shows it. The period charts are `GET /calls/summary` and `GET /whatsapp/summary`. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Authentication
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/authentication

Bearer keys, and the one place they must never go.

```
Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…
```

Create a key in **Settings → API keys**. It is shown **once**, at creation, and
stored only as a hash — nothing can retrieve it afterwards, including us.

## This is not your widget key

> [!WARNING]
>
> Your **public key** (`pk_…`) identifies which agent answers and is meant to be
> visible in your page source.
>
> Your **API key** (`ta_live_…`) can message any of your customers. It belongs in
> a server's environment. Putting it in your HTML hands anybody the ability to
> message your entire contact list.

## Choose what each key can do

When you create a key, you pick one of three access levels. The level applies
everywhere the key is used — your own code calling the API, and the MCP server.
A key's access cannot be changed later — create a new key and revoke the old one.

| Access level | What the key can do |
| - | - |
| **Full access** | Everything, including messaging your customers and placing calls. Keys created before access levels existed have full access. |
| **Build** | See everything, and set up agents, knowledge, actions, contacts, webhooks, sequences and their steps, WhatsApp forms, template and one-time-code drafts, projects, teams, saved replies and notification settings, and connect a Telegram bot. It can also test-chat an agent, resolve, take over and assign conversations, and pause a sequence or pause or cancel a campaign. It **cannot** send messages or codes, place or end calls, reply to a customer, report events, add anyone to a sequence, start a campaign or sequence, publish a form, rent or release a number, clone a voice, or change the workspace, its members or invitations. Test chats and adding knowledge still count towards your usage. |
| **Read-only** | See everything. Change nothing. |

If a key tries something its access level does not allow, the request is
refused with `403` and a message saying what kind of key it is:

```json theme={null}
{ "error": "This API key is a build key: it can set up agents, actions, contacts and webhooks, but not message customers, send codes or place calls. Use a full key for that." }
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Connecting an AI assistant such as Claude Code or Cursor to the
> [ThinnestAI MCP server](/mcp/overview)? The MCP server can do exactly what its
> key can do, so choose **Build** to let it set things up without being able to
> contact a customer, or **Read-only** if it only needs to report. See
> [Connect your assistant to the MCP server](/mcp/connect).

## Acting for one of your customers

If you build your own product on the API, your key reaches each of your
[customers](/api-reference/customers): add their id in a header.

```
Thinnest-Workspace: org_1f2e…
```

The request runs inside that customer, with your key's access level. An id that
is not one of your customers is `404`, whether or not it exists.

## Revoking

Immediate. Revoked keys are kept along with their last-used time, because that
is the first thing anybody wants to know after a leak.

## Rate limits

Per organization, per minute.

```http theme={null}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
```

Honour `Retry-After`. The limit exists because a loop in an integration can
spend a month of WhatsApp budget before anybody looks at a dashboard — and
because Meta rate-limits the number afterwards. The damage is money first and
reputation second.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Idempotency protects you from repeating **one** request. It does nothing about
> a thousand different ones. These are separate problems and both are guarded.

## Storing the key

```bash Environment theme={null}
THINNEST_API_KEY=ta_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```js Node theme={null}
const res = await fetch("https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/messages", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.THINNEST_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload),
});
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os, requests

res = requests.post(
    "https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/messages",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['THINNEST_API_KEY']}"},
    json=payload,
)
```


# Bring your own keys
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys

Run your agents on your own speech-to-text, LLM and voice accounts, on your own voice and language model, on your own voice alone, or on your own language model alone. Each agent can follow the workspace or choose its own.

With **bring your own keys** (BYOK), your workspace uses your own accounts with the providers. The
three jobs are speech-to-text, the LLM and the voice. You pay those providers directly. Depending
on what you bring, we charge a flat platform fee or our usual per-minute voice plan.

You choose what you bring:

* **All three of my keys** (scope `all`). Speech-to-text, the LLM and the voice are all yours.
* **Only my voice** (scope `voice`). Your voice account speaks. Our speech-to-text hears the
  caller, our model answers, and the phone line is ours.
* **My voice and my language model** (scope `llm_voice`). Your voice account speaks and your LLM
  account answers, on any model your key offers. We keep the speech recogniser (our speech-to-text
  hears the caller), and the phone line is ours.
* **Only my language model** (scope `llm`). Your LLM account answers, on any model your key
  offers. We keep the speech recogniser and the voice, and the phone line is ours. You pay the same
  per-minute voice plan as any other call: Standard, Premium or Studio, by the voice the agent
  speaks with.

| | All three of my keys | My voice and my language model | Only my voice | Only my language model |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Call minute | **₹1.00** (\$0.012) a minute, all-in | **₹1.00** (\$0.012) a minute, our speech-to-text and phone line included | **₹1.50** (\$0.02) a minute, our phone line included | Our usual voice plan: Premium or Studio |
| Chat reply | **₹0.02** per reply | **₹0.02** per reply | Our usual price, because the model is ours | **₹0.02** per reply, as with all three |

Calls are billed in 30-second pulses, at the rate set when the call starts. With only your
language model, the model you run never changes the price of the minute: the price follows the
voice alone, however costly your model is on your own account.

With all three, BYOK turns on only when a speech-to-text key, an LLM key and a voice key are all
added and checked. With your voice and your language model, it needs a checked LLM key and a
checked voice key. With only your voice, it needs only a checked voice key. With only your
language model, it needs only a checked LLM key, with a model chosen. Any plan can turn it on.

With all three keys, your voice and language model, or only your language model, each agent can also run its own **model** from your LLM key. On the agent's **Playground**, the
Model list shows every model your key reaches. Leave it on your key's model, which is the one set
in **Settings → Your keys**, or pick another for this agent alone.

Each agent speaks with a voice you choose from your own voice provider. Open the agent's
**Voice** page: it lists every voice your key can use, and **Play** speaks a short line in the
agent's language. The preview runs on your account, so the provider charges you for those few
characters. If a provider hosts its own sample of a voice, that sample plays instead, at no
cost. An agent without a chosen voice speaks with a standard voice from your provider.

On a call with all three, your speech-to-text hears the caller, your LLM answers, and your voice
speaks. With your voice and your language model, our speech-to-text hears the caller, and your LLM
answers and your voice speaks. With only your voice, only the speaking is yours. With only your language model, only the
answering is yours: our speech-to-text hears the caller and our voice speaks. If one of your keys cannot be used when a call starts, the call is not
answered on our providers instead.

### Which models answer calls with only your voice

With only your voice, the call minute includes our model, so a call runs only on a low-cost
model. Today those are:

* Prana
* Prana \[Voice]
* GPT-OSS 120B
* GPT-5 Nano
* GPT-4.1 Nano

The rule is Prana, Prana \[Voice] and GPT-OSS 120B by name, plus any voice model (other than our call-only
Composer, which runs a second model each turn) whose price per token is at or below our reference low-cost voice model on both input and output, so a new
model that is cheap enough joins the list on its own. `GET /api/v1/models` marks each model with
`voiceOnlyByok`.

An agent already set to another model keeps it for chat, which is billed as usual, and runs on
GPT-OSS 120B on calls. The agent's model picker lists only the allowed models while you use only your
voice. Setting another model through `POST` or `PATCH /api/v1/agents` returns a 400 that says
why. With all three of your keys, with your voice and language model, with only your language model, or without BYOK, nothing changes:
with only your language model the model is your key's, so any model your key offers can answer calls. The limit applies only to agents
that use your keys: an agent you have switched off your keys (below) answers on our stack, so it may
use any model.

### Each agent chooses how it uses your keys

BYOK is switched on for the workspace, and the scope you choose in **Settings → Your keys** is the
**default**: every agent follows it until it is told otherwise. A workspace holds its keys once, and
each agent can choose for itself. An agent's `byok` is one of:

* `null` (or `"workspace"`): follow the workspace's default scope. This is how every agent starts.
* `"off"`: never use your keys (below).
* `"all"`, `"voice"`, `"llm"` or `"llm_voice"`: run this agent on that scope's keys, whatever the
  workspace default is. For example, with an LLM key and a voice key saved, one agent can run on
  `"llm"` (your model, our voice) while another runs on `"llm_voice"` (your model and your voice).

Choosing a scope is refused with `409` unless the workspace holds checked keys, each with a model, for
everything the scope needs. The message names the missing key, for example "no verified voice key
(tts)". Switching BYOK off in the workspace is the master switch: with it off, no agent uses a key,
whatever it chose. The workspace default decides which keys turning BYOK on needs; an agent's own
scope needs its keys too, so a key an agent's scope needs cannot be removed while BYOK is on (set the
agent to follow the workspace first, or replace the key).

A call or reply is priced and run under the scope that applies to the agent when it starts, so two
agents in one workspace can bill differently: the price follows the agent's scope. If an agent's
scope can no longer be served when a call starts (a key was removed while BYOK was off), the agent
falls back to the workspace's scope and the call goes ahead; it is never refused for that, and never
billed at a rate that does not match how it ran.

A call can be handed to another agent only when that agent would run on the same stack the call
started on. A hand-off to an agent on a different scope, or switched off your keys, is refused.

#### An agent on ours

Give an agent `byok: "off"` and it never uses your keys, whatever the workspace does:

* calls run on our voices, our speech-to-text and our model, and the minute is billed at our normal
  rate for that voice, not the BYOK rate;
* chat replies are billed as normal replies, not the flat BYOK reply charge. With only your language
  model, the minute is already our normal rate, so what changes for an agent set to `"off"` is the
  model (ours, not yours) and the chat reply price;
* the voice-only model limit does not apply to it;
* the model and voice choices you saved for your own keys are kept and ignored until you switch the
  agent back to `"workspace"`.

The other agents in the workspace keep their own choice and price. A customer of yours
follows the same rule on its own agents. The setting is read once when a call or a reply starts, so a
call is never priced at one rate and run on another stack. A call already ringing keeps the stack it
was started on: if you switch its agent off your keys in those few seconds, the call is refused
rather than moved onto ours.

An agent set to `"off"` is billed at our rate for the voice it uses: the Premium rate, or the
Studio rate with a Studio voice. A new agent starts on a Premium voice.

## In the console

Open **Settings → Your keys** and choose the default: **All three of my keys**, **My voice and my
language model** (we keep the speech recogniser, ₹1/min), **Only my voice** or **Only my language
model**. All three key cards are always shown, so you can save a key for an agent that chooses a
different scope. Keys for jobs your default does not cover are not used by agents that follow it. On
an agent's **Playground** or **Voice** page, **How Agent uses your keys** chooses between following
the workspace, **Off**, and each set your saved keys allow. Each card has:

* **Provider.** Choose who does that job.
* **Model.** Every model the provider offers. Before you add a key, the list shows the models the
  provider offers. Once your key is checked, it shows the models **your** key reaches. Long lists
  are grouped by family, such as Flux, Aura-2 and Aura for Deepgram's voices.
* **API key**, plus any other field the provider needs. Azure, for example, needs a region.

**Verify and save** checks the key with the provider before storing it. A key the provider rejects
is not saved. Keys are stored encrypted, and are only ever shown by their last four characters.

Once the cards you need are filled, switch on **Use my own keys**.

## Providers

| Job | Providers |
| - | - |
| Speech-to-text | Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Soniox, Speechmatics, Gladia, Sarvam, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, Azure Speech |
| LLM | OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Sarvam, DeepSeek, xAI Grok, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible URL |
| Voice | Deepgram, ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI, Sarvam, Soniox, Mistral, Azure Speech, Rime, Inworld, Hume, Murf, Speechify |

**Azure Speech** takes your key and region. If your Azure resource accepts its key only at its own
address, as Azure AI Foundry resources do, also give its **resource endpoint**, such as
`https://my-resource.cognitiveservices.azure.com`.

**Any OpenAI-compatible URL** takes a base URL that starts with `https://`. Azure OpenAI's
`https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1` is one. If the server does not list its models, send
the model id with the key, and we check the two together with a one-token request.

On calls, a Google Gemini 2.5 or 3 model is asked to think less before it speaks, so the
caller is not left waiting (a Pro model cannot switch thinking off, so it is asked for the least
it allows). Chat replies are not changed.

## When a key fails

There is no fallback to our providers for a job that is yours. If your provider refuses a request
(a revoked key, no credit, rate limits), the reply fails, or the voice does not speak. We do not answer on our own models and bill you for it. You get a notification naming
the provider and the reason, at most once a day per provider. With only your voice, speech-to-text
and the LLM are ours, so our usual backups for them stay on. With only your language model, the
speech-to-text and the voice are ours and keep our usual backups, but the model never has one: if your
key fails, the caller hears our apology and the call is flagged, and we do not answer on our model.

To hear about changes to your keys in your own systems, subscribe a webhook to
[`byok.changed`](/api-reference/webhooks#workspace-events): it is sent when a key is added, replaced,
removed or refused by its provider, and when your own keys are switched on or off or set to cover
different jobs. It names the job and the provider, never any part of the key. Each call's
[Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) also says which keys it ran on, in `billing.keys`.

## Customers

If you build on our API with [customers](/api-reference/customers), your customers use **your** keys
while BYOK is on, with your choice of all three, your voice and language model, only the voice or only the language model. A customer can bring a complete
set of its own for that choice (three keys, an LLM and voice key, a voice key or an LLM key), which then overrides yours. Turning BYOK off in your workspace turns it off for every customer that inherits your keys. A customer with its own complete set and its own switch on keeps using its own.

## API

Every request below also works for a customer, with the `Thinnest-Workspace` header.

### Status

```http theme={null}
GET /api/v1/byok
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "enabled": true,
  "scope": "all",
  "usingScope": "all",
  "using": "own",
  "complete": true,
  "credentials": [
    {
      "kind": "stt",
      "provider": "deepgram",
      "label": "Deepgram",
      "key": "…k9z2",
      "fields": { "model": "nova-3-general" },
      "model": "nova-3-general",
      "models": ["flux-general-en", "nova-3-general", "…"],
      "verifiedAt": "2026-10-06T10:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-10-06T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

`scope` is what this workspace brings by default: `all`, `voice`, `llm` or `llm_voice`; each agent may choose its own (below). `usingScope` is the scope that applies
right now (a customer runs on its developer's), or `null`. `complete` says whether the keys for
`scope` are ready. `using` is `own`, `developer` (a customer using its developer's keys) or `none`. `models` is what the
provider offered this key, and `model` is the one it runs.

### Add or replace a key

```http theme={null}
PUT /api/v1/byok/credentials
```

```json theme={null}
{ "kind": "llm", "provider": "openai", "credentials": { "apiKey": "sk-…", "model": "gpt-5.4-mini" } }
```

* **`kind`.** One of `stt`, `llm` or `tts`.
* **`provider`.** One of the provider ids in the table above, in lower case. An error lists the ones
  that do that job.
* **`credentials.model`.** Optional. Without it, a speech key starts on the provider's usual model.
  An LLM key starts on the provider's usual model when it has one; otherwise choose one.
* **Replacing a key.** If you replace a key with one for the same provider, its model is kept.

| Status | Why |
| - | - |
| `400` | The provider rejected the key, or does not offer that model on it. |
| `409` | BYOK is on, and this key would leave a job without a model. |
| `502` | The provider could not be reached to check the key. Try again. |

### Change the model, or refresh the list

```http theme={null}
PATCH /api/v1/byok/credentials/llm
```

```json theme={null}
{ "model": "gpt-5.4-nano" }
```

The key is not sent again. The model must be on the key's `models` list. For a model the provider
launched after you added the key, send `"refreshModels": true`, alone or together with the new
`model`.

### Turn BYOK on or off

```http theme={null}
PATCH /api/v1/byok
```

```json theme={null}
{ "enabled": true, "scope": "voice" }
```

Send `enabled`, `scope`, or both. `scope` is `all`, `voice`, `llm` or `llm_voice`. The request is refused with
`409` until the keys for the scope are added, checked, and each has a model: all three for `all`,
the voice key for `voice`, the LLM key for `llm`, the LLM key and the voice key for `llm_voice`. While BYOK is on, moving to a scope needs that
scope's keys first, for example the other two keys to move from `voice` to `all`.

### Voices

```http theme={null}
GET /api/v1/byok/voices
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "provider": { "id": "elevenlabs", "label": "ElevenLabs" },
  "model": "eleven_flash_v2_5",
  "items": [
    { "id": "EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL", "name": "Sarah", "language": "en", "gender": "female", "sample": "https://…", "own": false }
  ]
}
```

These are the voices your voice provider offers your key. `sample` is a clip the provider hosts,
when it has one. On Deepgram, a voice is a model, such as `aura-2-helena-en` or `flux-alexis-en`.
On Cartesia the list starts with your own cloned voices.

`own` is `true` for a voice that belongs to your own account with the provider — one you cloned or
designed there — and `false` for the provider's library:

| Provider | What `own` means |
| - | - |
| Cartesia | The voices your Cartesia account owns (listed first) |
| ElevenLabs | The voices your account owns: your cloned and designed voices |
| Soniox | Always `true`: Soniox lists only your account's own voices |
| Every other provider | Always `false`: the provider does not say which voices are yours |

### Preview a voice

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/byok/voices/preview
```

```json theme={null}
{ "voice": "EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL", "agentId": "agt_…" }
```

The response is the audio itself: `audio/mpeg`, or `audio/wav` for Sarvam. Without `text`, the
voice speaks a short line of ours in the agent's language, or in `language` if you send it. Any
`text` you send is capped at 200 characters, because your provider charges you for every
character. Soniox has no preview here: it speaks only on a live call.

### Choose an agent's model

`GET /api/v1/models` lists our models in `items`, as before. On a workspace using its own keys
it also returns `byok`:

```json theme={null}
{ "byok": { "provider": { "id": "openai", "label": "OpenAI" }, "workspaceModel": "gpt-5.4-nano", "models": ["gpt-5.4-mini", "gpt-5.4-nano", "…"] } }
```

```http theme={null}
PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/byok-model
```

```json theme={null}
{ "model": "gpt-5.4-mini" }
```

The model must be one your key reaches. Send `null` to go back to your key's model. `GET` on the
same path returns the agent's choice. It also returns `stale`, the agent's earlier choice, if your
key no longer reaches it; until you choose again, the agent runs your key's model.

### Choose an agent's voice

```http theme={null}
PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/byok-voice
```

```json theme={null}
{ "voice": "EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL" }
```

The voice must be one that `GET /byok/voices` lists. Send `null` to go back to the provider's
standard voice. `GET` on the same path returns the agent's current choice.

Your own cloned voices are listed and can be used. On Cartesia, `GET /byok/voices` lists your
account's own voices first, then the whole library (up to 2,000 voices), so a clone is always on the
list however large the library is. If Cartesia is slow to answer, the list can come back short:
the response then says `"complete": false`, is not cached, and you should ask again. A voice you cloned a moment ago is accepted here by its id even before it shows up in the
list.

To use a different voice for a single call, put it in that call's `overrides`, as
`"overrides": { "voice": "EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL" }` on `POST /api/v1/calls` or in a batch.
On a workspace using its own keys, the voice must be one of yours from `GET /byok/voices`. A per-call voice is
checked like an agent's voice: if it is not on the list we ask the provider about that one voice
directly, so a clone made a moment ago is accepted. If the provider cannot be reached to check, the
request fails with `502` and can be retried; only a provider that says it has no such voice gives a refusal.

A choice belongs to the provider it was made on. If you switch your voice key to another provider,
the agent speaks with the new provider's standard voice until you choose again. `GET` shows the old
choice as `stale` until then.

### Tune a Cartesia voice

If your voice key is Cartesia, each agent can also set how its voice sounds. A client who finds
calls quiet or a little fast can fix it for that agent alone, without touching the others.

In the console, open the agent's **Voice** page and choose a voice. A **How it sounds** panel
appears under the list, with a **Hear it** button that speaks a short line with the settings as
they are now (on your account, so Cartesia charges you for those few characters) and a **Save
settings** button. Through the API, send the same fields to the voice call above:

```http theme={null}
PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/byok-voice
```

```json theme={null}
{ "speed": 0.95, "volume": 1.4, "emotion": "calm", "model": "sonic-3.5", "pronunciationDictId": "pdict_123" }
```

| Field | Values | Default |
| - | - | - |
| `speed` | 0.6 to 1.5 | 1, Cartesia's own |
| `volume` | 0.5 to 2.0. Raise it if calls sound quiet. | 1 |
| `emotion` | One of Cartesia's emotions, such as `neutral`, `calm`, `content`, `sad`, `angry`, `scared`, `happy`, `excited`. | the words decide |
| `model` | `sonic-3.6`, `sonic-3.6-2026-08-27`, `sonic-3.5`, `sonic-3` or `sonic-2`, for this agent alone. `sonic-3.6` is Cartesia's own name for its newest 3.6 version; the dated one is a fixed release. | your key's model |
| `pronunciationDictId` | The id Cartesia gave a pronunciation dictionary in your account | none |

Every field is optional, and a request changes only the fields it names. A field you leave out stays
as it is, `null` puts one back to its default, and a value sets it. So `{ "voice": "…" }` alone
changes the voice and keeps the settings. `{ "voice": null }` goes back to the standard voice and
clears them, because the settings belong to a voice of your own: sending one before a voice is
chosen, or together with `"voice": null`, is refused. A setting that is not allowed answers `400`
with `code: validation_failed` and `field` naming it. `GET` on the same path returns the settings,
each `null` while unset. It returns the agent's own model as `agentModel`, because `model` there is
always your key's.

A few things to know:

* `emotion` works in English only. In other languages Cartesia ignores it.
* `speed`, `volume` and `emotion` need a Sonic 3 model. With `sonic-2` they are refused, and if your
  key's model is later changed to `sonic-2` they are simply not sent.
* `speed` does not apply to a Professional Voice Clone, which keeps the pace of its recording. Use
  `volume`, or an Instant Voice Clone, to adjust it.
* Cartesia treats these as guidance, not exact changes. Listen with **Hear it** or the preview below
  before you rely on a value.
* A call that names its own voice in `overrides` keeps the agent's settings.
* Only an agent speaking with your Cartesia voice has them. Other providers are not affected.

To hear a setting without saving it, add the same fields to the preview:

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/byok/voices/preview
```

```json theme={null}
{ "voice": "a0e99841-438c-4a64-b679-ae501e7d6091", "speed": 0.95, "volume": 1.4 }
```

Only the fields you send are spoken; the agent's saved settings are not read.

### Choose how one agent uses your keys

`byok` is a field of the agent, on `POST /api/v1/agents` and `PATCH /api/v1/agents/{id}`, and comes
back on every agent:

```http theme={null}
PATCH /api/v1/agents/{id}
```

```json theme={null}
{ "byok": "llm_voice" }
```

* Leave `byok` out and the agent's choice is unchanged.
* `null` (or `"workspace"`) follows the workspace's default scope. An agent that follows the workspace
  comes back as `"workspace"`.
* `"off"` keeps this agent on our voices, models and pricing.
* `"all"`, `"voice"`, `"llm"` or `"llm_voice"` runs this agent on that scope's keys. It is refused with
  `409` if the workspace has no checked key for something the scope needs, and the error names it.
* Anything else is a 400.

In the console, the same choice is **How Agent uses your keys** on the agent's Playground and Voice
pages, shown only while your workspace uses its own keys.

Changing it needs an API key that can edit agents, as for the agent's model and voice. While an agent
is `"off"`, `GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/byok-model` and `byok-voice` answer `409`, because it uses
neither of your providers. `PUT` still saves a choice for when you switch it back on.

### Remove a key

```http theme={null}
DELETE /api/v1/byok/credentials/tts
```

The request is refused with `409` while BYOK is on and the key is one the scope needs. Under scope
`all` that is every key; under scope `voice` only the voice key is required, under scope `llm`
only the LLM key, and under scope `llm_voice` the LLM key and the voice key, so a leftover key for a
job that is ours can be deleted while BYOK is on. It is also refused while an agent is set to a scope that needs the
key. Replace a needed key instead, set that agent to follow the workspace, or turn BYOK off first.

Changing keys or switching BYOK needs an API key with **full** access. A read-only key can see the
status.


# Add BYOK Key
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/add-byok-key

/api-reference/openapi.json put /byok/credentials
Adds or replaces your key for one job. The key is checked with the provider before anything is stored — a key the provider rejects is not saved — then stored encrypted and only ever shown by its last four characters. The provider's model list is pulled at the same time. Without `credentials.model`, a speech key starts on the provider's usual model and an LLM key on its usual one where it has one; replacing a key with one for the same provider keeps the model already chosen. Needs a **full** key.

# Delete BYOK Key
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/delete-byok-key

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /byok/credentials/{kind}
Removes your key for one job. Refused while BYOK is on, since a workspace on its own keys always has all three — turn BYOK off first, or replace the key with Add BYOK Key. Needs a **full** key.

# Get BYOK Status
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/get-byok-status

/api-reference/openapi.json get /byok
Whether your workspace runs on its own keys, whose keys are in use (`own`, or `developer` for a customer using its developer's), which keys you bring (`scope`: all three, only your voice, only your language model, or your language model and your voice), whether your keys for that scope are complete enough to switch on, and each key, masked to its last four characters.

# List BYOK Keys
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/list-byok-keys

/api-reference/openapi.json get /byok/credentials
Your workspace's own provider keys, one per job, masked to their last four characters, with the model each runs and every model its provider offered it.

# List BYOK Voices
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/list-byok-voices

/api-reference/openapi.json get /byok/voices
The voices your own voice provider offers your key — what Set Agent BYOK Voice accepts. `sample` is a clip the provider hosts, free to play, when it has one. On Cartesia the list starts with your own cloned voices, then the whole library (up to 2,000 voices); if Cartesia is slow to answer the list can come back short: `complete` is then `false`, it is not cached, and you should ask again. A per-call `overrides.voice` is checked the same way as an agent's voice: if it is not on the list we ask the provider about that one voice directly, so a voice missing from a short list is still accepted. Refused with `409` when the workspace is not using its own keys; its voices are then List Voices. These are the voices of the agents that use your keys: an agent set to `byok: "off"` (Update Agent) speaks in our voices from List Voices, at our normal pricing, while your other agents stay on your keys.

# Preview BYOK Voice
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/preview-byok-voice

/api-reference/openapi.json post /byok/voices/preview
Speaks one short line in a voice of your own voice provider, on your key, and answers with the audio itself. Your provider charges you for the characters, so `text` is capped at 200; without it the voice says a short greeting of ours in `language`, or the agent's language when you name an agent. Soniox has no preview: it speaks only on a live call. On a Cartesia key, `speed`, `volume`, `emotion`, `model` and `pronunciationDictId` are spoken too, so a setting is heard before it is saved (they work as in Set Agent BYOK Voice; the agent's saved settings are not read). Needs a **full** key.

# Turn BYOK On or Off
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/turn-byok-on-or-off

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /byok
Switches your workspace onto your own keys, or back onto ours, and/or chooses what you bring (`scope`). Scope `all` needs all three keys — speech-to-text, LLM and voice — added, verified and each with a model chosen; scope `voice` needs only the voice key, and speech-to-text, the LLM and telephony stay ours; scope `llm` needs only the LLM key, and speech-to-text and the voice stay ours (calls are billed on the normal voice plan, whatever your model); scope `llm_voice` needs the LLM key and the voice key, and our speech recogniser stays (a call is a flat ₹1/min like `all`). `scope` is the default for your agents: any agent may follow it, be switched off, or choose another scope your keys allow (Update Agent `byok`). Any plan may turn it on. On a developer's workspace, turning it off turns it off for every customer using your keys, and a customer inherits your scope. Needs a **full** key.

# Update BYOK Key Model
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys/update-byok-key-model

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /byok/credentials/{kind}
Changes the model a stored key runs without sending the key again. `model` must be on the key's `models`; for a model the provider launched after you added the key, send `refreshModels: true` — alone, or with the new `model`, which is then checked against the fresh list. While BYOK is on, a refreshed list that drops the chosen model is refused. Needs a **full** key.

# Cancel Call
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/cancel-call

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /calls/{id}
Calls off a call you placed through the API (`out_…` or `sch_…`). A call still waiting to ring — booked, queued for its hours, or a retry — is cancelled and answers `200` with its report, `status: "cancelled"`. A call ringing or connected is ended on the line and answers `202` with the report as it stands; its ending arrives a moment later with `call.analysed`, and no retry follows. A call that has already ended answers `409`. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Call
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/get-call

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/{id}
One call and everything it learned: status, timings, how it ended, the summary, the collected `fields`, the transcript, a signed `recording` link and the call's `quality` figures (reply times, silences, interruptions, model errors). It is exactly the object `call.analysed` delivers, so a missed delivery can be read back here; `analysedAt` null means the summary and fields are not final yet. Any id List Calls hands out works — `out_…` and `sch_…` for calls you placed, the call reference for any other.

# Get Call Timeline
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/get-call-timeline

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/{id}/timeline
Where the time went in each turn of one call. Every time is in milliseconds from the moment the caller stopped speaking, so a turn reads as a row of steps: the recogniser's wait and the caller's final words, Ear's check, the turn being decided, the model being asked, the first words of the answer leaving the model, the first sound of any kind, and the answer being heard. `split` adds up the pieces a team works on: the wait before the turn was decided, the recogniser, Ear's check, the model's first sentence and the voice.

`answerAudioMs` is the time to the first word of the ACTUAL answer. `quality.responseMs` stops at the first sound of any kind, so a thinking line that plays first ends it; here `firstAudioKind` says what spoke first (`answer`, `filler` or `other`) and `answerAudioEstimated` is true when a filler spoke first and the answer's start is worked out from the audio queued behind it rather than heard directly. A step that did not happen on a turn is null, never zero. A negative `modelAskedMs` is real: with `earlyAnswers` the model is asked before the turn is decided.

`timeline` is null for a call that has none: a call from before this existed, or one on a call type that does not record it. It holds times only, no words, so it stays when a call's content is deleted. Any id List Calls hands out works.

# Get Call Transcript
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/get-call-transcript

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/{id}/transcript
What was said on one call, oldest first: this call's spoken turns only, internal notes left out — the same words `call.analysed` delivers. `?format=txt` returns a plain-text file to save (`call-{id}.txt`, one `[mm:ss] Who: what` line per turn). A turn's `offset` is when it was written down, not where it falls in the audio, so it suits ordering and rough position but not subtitles.

# List Calls
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/list-calls

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls
Every call your workspace made or took — inbound, website, WhatsApp, a campaign's or one you placed — newest first, without transcripts or recordings. Each item's `id` opens the call with Get Call. A call booked for later appears here only once it has rung; read a booked call by the `sch_…` id Place Call gave you.

# Place Batch Calls
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/place-batch-calls

/api-reference/openapi.json post /calls/batch
Rings up to 200 people with one request. Every option Place Call takes may be set once for the batch and again on an entry, the entry winning (an entry's `variables` sit on top of the batch's); `purpose` and `agent` are the batch's. Every entry is queued and paced inside your plan's lines and balance — none rings inline — and each gets its own `sch_…` id that reports through `call.analysed` and Get Call. A bad entry is listed under `refused` and does not stop the rest. Needs a **full** key.

# Place Call
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/calls/place-call

/api-reference/openapi.json post /calls
Your agent rings a customer, opens with your `purpose` (spoken aloud, so 300 characters or fewer), then holds a normal conversation. A number that is not a contact yet becomes one with the `name` and `source` you send; someone who opted out or is on your do-not-call list is refused. Outside the calling hours you set with `callingHours` (any hour of any day when you set none), in the customer's own time, or with `scheduledAt`, the call is queued and answers `status: "scheduled"` with a `sch_…` id; otherwise it rings now with an `out_…` id. Each call is billed from your balance, refused with `402` when it cannot pay, held to your plan's concurrent lines and 60 requests a minute; what it learned arrives as `call.analysed` or from Get Call. Needs a **full** key.

# Cancel Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/cancel-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json post /campaigns/{id}/cancel
Stops a draft, sending or paused campaign for good and sets `finishedAt`. Messages already handed to WhatsApp, and calls already placed, still complete. This cannot be undone, and it is also how you get rid of a draft you do not want: campaigns cannot be edited or deleted, so cancel it and create a new one. A **build** key may do this, since it only ever stops sends.

# Create Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/create-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json post /campaigns
Creates a WhatsApp broadcast (`kind: "whatsapp"`) or a calling campaign (`kind: "voice"`) as a draft, with the same checks as the console's builder: WhatsApp connected and the template approved with every blank filled, or for calls an agent with a number that answers phone calls and is licensed for this kind of call. The audience is built from your contacts right away, by consent; people who asked not to be contacted are always left out. Send `launch: true` to start it at once, or `scheduledAt` to start it later; a launch that is refused (no paid plan, not enough balance) still leaves the draft and says why in `message`, and an audience of nobody is never launched. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/get-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json get /campaigns/{id}
Returns one broadcast or calling campaign with its current state and counts. Poll it while a campaign is sending to follow its progress; `finishedAt` is set when it ends or is cancelled, and `lastError` says why a campaign stopped, when it did.

# Launch Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/launch-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json post /campaigns/{id}/launch
Starts a draft, as the console's Send or Start button does, re-running its checks at the moment they matter: your plan must include campaigns, a calling campaign's agent must still have a number that answers phone calls (and, for promotional calls, is licensed for them), and your balance must cover the send. If the balance covers only part of it, the campaign starts and `message` says how far it goes; the rest stays queued until you top up. Messages go out in the background; calls are paced by your free call lines. A campaign already sending answers `200` and is left alone, and a scheduled draft launched here starts now instead of waiting. Needs a **full** key.

# List Campaigns
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/list-campaigns

/api-reference/openapi.json get /campaigns
Lists your workspace's broadcasts and calling campaigns, newest first, each with its live counts: recipients, sent, delivered, read, replied, failed and skipped. Filter by `status` to watch only the ones that are sending.

# Pause Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/pause-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json post /campaigns/{id}/pause
