Stops a sending campaign from sending any more. Messages already handed to WhatsApp, and calls already placed, still complete. Resume Campaign picks up where it stopped, without messaging anyone twice. Only a `sending` campaign can be paused. A **build** key may do this, since it only ever stops sends.

# Resume Campaign
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/campaigns/resume-campaign

/api-reference/openapi.json post /campaigns/{id}/resume
Sends a paused campaign again, to everyone it has not reached yet; nobody is messaged or called twice. It clears `lastError`, and what it sends is charged as usual. Only a `paused` campaign can be resumed; a draft is started with Launch Campaign. Needs a **full** key.

# Connect Telegram Bot
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/channels/connect-telegram-bot

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/channels/telegram
Connects a Telegram bot to the agent with the token @BotFather gave you: the token is checked with Telegram, stored encrypted and never shown again, and Telegram is told where to deliver messages. Telegram needs a paid plan, and a bot can belong to one agent only. Telegram calls back on the address this request arrived on, so call the public API address. A **build** key may do this.

# Disconnect Telegram Bot
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/channels/disconnect-telegram-bot

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}/channels/telegram
Disconnects the agent's Telegram bot (a 404 when none is connected) and tells Telegram to stop delivering to us. Its conversations stay in your inbox, and the bot itself still exists in Telegram — delete it in @BotFather if you want it gone. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Agent Channels
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/channels/get-agent-channels

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/channels
Where the agent answers, as the Channels page shows it: the widget key, the WhatsApp number and its health, the Telegram bot and the voice line. No token or secret is ever part of the answer. The widget's look and the call settings are changed with Update Agent (`widget`, `voice`).

# Add Contacts To Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/add-contacts-to-group

/api-reference/openapi.json post /contact-groups/{id}/members
Adds up to 1,000 contacts to the group. Contacts already in it are left as they are (`added` counts only the new ones). Every id must be a contact in this workspace, or nothing is added and the answer is `404` naming them. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Contact Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/create-contact-group

/api-reference/openapi.json post /contact-groups
Creates an empty group. Names are unique in the workspace whatever the capitals; a second one answers `409`. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Contact Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/delete-contact-group

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /contact-groups/{id}
Deletes the group and its memberships. Its contacts stay. A campaign not yet sent that was aimed at it no longer reaches anybody through it. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Contact Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/get-contact-group

/api-reference/openapi.json get /contact-groups/{id}
One group and how many contacts are in it.

# List Contact Groups
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/list-contact-groups

/api-reference/openapi.json get /contact-groups
Every group in the workspace, by name, each with how many contacts are in it. Returned whole: `nextCursor` is always null.

# Remove Contacts From Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/remove-contacts-from-group

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /contact-groups/{id}/members
Takes up to 1,000 contacts out of the group. The contacts stay; ids not in the group are ignored (`removed` counts the ones taken out). A **build** key may do this.

# Rename Contact Group
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contact-groups/rename-contact-group

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /contact-groups/{id}
Renames a group. Campaigns aimed at it keep reaching it. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Contact
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contacts/create-contact

/api-reference/openapi.json post /contacts
Creates a contact — or, when someone is already on that number, **updates that person** instead, so a CRM that syncs the same lead twice never doubles your list. Answers `201` for a new contact and `200` for one it updated. Creating a contact is not consent: only `consent.status: "granted"` with a `source` is. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Contact
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contacts/delete-contact

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /contacts/{id}
**Erases** the contact: their conversations and transcripts, their calls, any queued call and their campaign rows go with them, and so does any duplicate that was merged into them. This cannot be undone. Use it for a person's request to be forgotten; to stop messaging someone, set their consent to `withdrawn` instead. A **build** key may do this.

**Recordings are erased too.** The audio of their calls is deleted before the call rows go: a recording we store is deleted right away, the phone provider's copy of a call on a number we rent is deleted through your workspace's own account with them, and any copy made for model training is deleted. A file that cannot be deleted at that moment is queued and retried every night until it is gone; the contact is erased regardless, and the response says how many are still queued in `recordingsPending`.

**Knowing when it is finished.** Subscribe a webhook to `contact.erased`: it is sent once the erasure is complete — straight away when this answers 204, or from the nightly retry once the last queued recording is gone — with only the contact's id and when it was erased.

**What is not erased.** Do-not-call entries are kept deliberately, so the person is not called again. Webhook payloads we already sent are purged on their own schedule after 7 days. Copies in your own systems, and in your vendors', are yours to delete.

# Get Contact
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contacts/get-contact

/api-reference/openapi.json get /contacts/{id}
One contact, by id.

# List Contacts
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contacts/list-contacts

/api-reference/openapi.json get /contacts
Contacts with a phone number, newest first. Filter by tag, by your CRM's id, or by phone to look one person up. Contacts folded into another by a merge are left out.

# Update Contact
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/contacts/update-contact

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /contacts/{id}
Changes any of the fields Create Contact takes, consent included; fields you leave out keep their values, and `null` clears a field. `tags` replaces the whole list. A contact whose consent is `withdrawn` is never sent marketing, enrolled in a sequence or put in a campaign. A **build** key may do this.

# Assign Conversation
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/conversations/assign-conversation

/api-reference/openapi.json post /conversations/{id}/assign
Make a conversation a teammate's job, by their email — or `null` to put it back in the pool. The teammate is notified when it really moves to them. Assigning does **not** silence the agent; taking it over with Update Conversation Status does. List your teammates with `GET /members`. The shared inbox needs a paid plan. A **build** key may do this.

# List Conversation Messages
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/conversations/list-conversation-messages

/api-reference/openapi.json get /conversations/{id}/messages
One conversation's messages, newest first: the customer's, your agent's, and replies a teammate sent from the inbox (`author: "teammate"`). Your team's internal notes are left out. Photos, voice notes, videos and documents a customer sent come back as links valid for **eight hours** — download what you need to keep.

# List Conversations
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/conversations/list-conversations

/api-reference/openapi.json get /conversations
Your workspace's conversations, newest first. `since` keeps only those a customer has written in at or after that moment — the way to find what a missed `message.received` webhook would have told you, including a conversation whose very first message you never heard about. Go back a few minutes from the last event you handled, since messages that arrive together can be delivered out of order.

# Reply to Conversation
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/conversations/reply-to-conversation

/api-reference/openapi.json post /conversations/{id}/reply
Your own agent platform answers a WhatsApp customer — the other half of the `message.received` webhook. Send exactly one of `text`, `media`, `template` or `form`; text, media and forms need the customer's 24-hour window open, a template does not. Only works on a number with **Connect External Agent/CRM** turned on, and not while a teammate has taken the conversation over. Each message is charged like any WhatsApp message from that number. Needs a **full** key.

# Update Conversation Status
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/conversations/update-conversation-status

/api-reference/openapi.json post /conversations/{id}/status
The inbox's three moves: `resolved` marks it done and fires the `conversation.resolved` webhook, `active` hands it back to the agent, and `human_handling` takes it over so the agent stays quiet until it is handed back. An internal note records which API key made the change; the customer never sees it. `changed: false` means it was already in that state, and nothing was written or announced. The shared inbox needs a paid plan. A **build** key may do this.

# Customers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers

Build your own product on the API: a workspace for each of your customers, reached with one key.

A **customer** is a workspace you create for one of your own customers — with its own agents,
contacts, knowledge, phone numbers and WhatsApp. Your one API key reaches any of them by adding a
header. Everything they use is billed to you.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Your first customer makes your workspace a **developer workspace**. A workspace that resells our
> console under its own brand (white label) cannot also have API customers.

## Create a customer

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/customers
Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…
Idempotency-Key: 6f1d2c9a-…
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "name": "Acme Dental",
  "externalId": "acme-42",
  "metadata": { "tier": "gold", "seats": 3 },
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata"
}
```

`201 Created`

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "org_1f2e…",
  "name": "Acme Dental",
  "externalId": "acme-42",
  "metadata": { "tier": "gold", "seats": 3 },
  "timezone": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "allottedCallLines": null,
  "archivedAt": null,
  "eraseAfter": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-06T10:00:00Z"
}
```

| Field | |
| - | - |
| `name` | Required. 1–120 characters. |
| `externalId` | Your own id for this customer: 1–128 letters, digits, `.` `_` `:` or `-`. Unique among your customers. |
| `metadata` | Up to 50 keys (1–40 characters each). Values are strings (up to 500 characters), numbers or booleans — no nested objects or lists. 8 KB in all. |
| `timezone` | An IANA time zone such as `Asia/Kolkata`. |

Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried request returns the same customer instead of making a
second one. Creating a customer needs a key with **full** access.

| Status | Why |
| - | - |
| `400` | A field is wrong — the message names it. |
| `402` | Your plan's customer limit is reached. |
| `409` | Another customer already has that `externalId`, or your workspace uses white label. |

## Work inside a customer

Add `Thinnest-Workspace` with the customer's `id` to **any** request. It runs inside that customer
as if the customer had sent it. `X-Workspace` is the same header under a neutral name; send one or
the other. Both naming different workspaces is refused with `400`.

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/agents
Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…
Thinnest-Workspace: org_1f2e…
```

```json theme={null}
{ "name": "Front desk" }
```

| You send | You get |
| - | - |
| No header, or your own workspace | Your own workspace |
| One of your customers | That customer |
| Someone else's customer, or an id that does not exist | `404 Workspace not found.` |
| A customer you deleted | `410` — with when it was deleted and when it will be erased |
| The header from a workspace with no customers | `400` |

Your key's access level applies inside the customer too: a read-only key can only read there.

## List customers

```http theme={null}
GET /api/v1/customers?limit=50
```

Newest first. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Filters: `externalId`,
`archived=true` (deleted, waiting to be erased), `createdAfter`, `createdBefore` (ISO 8601 times).

Manage customers from your own workspace — **without** `Thinnest-Workspace`.

## Get one customer

```http theme={null}
GET /api/v1/customers/org_1f2e…
```

The customer, plus:

```json theme={null}
{
  "counts": { "agents": 2, "phoneNumbers": 1, "contacts": 418 },
  "spendThisMonthMicro": 1840000
}
```

`spendThisMonthMicro` is what this customer's usage has cost you since the 1st of the month (UTC),
in millionths of your currency — `1840000` is ₹1.84.

## Update a customer

```http theme={null}
PATCH /api/v1/customers/org_1f2e…
```

```json theme={null}
{ "name": "Acme Dental Pvt", "metadata": { "tier": null, "region": "south" } }
```

You can change `name`, `externalId` (`null` clears it), `timezone`, `allottedCallLines` (how many of
your call lines this customer may use at once; `null` for no cap) and `metadata`. Metadata is
**merged**: keys you leave out are kept, and a key set to `null` is removed.

## Delete a customer

```http theme={null}
DELETE /api/v1/customers/org_1f2e…
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Release the customer's phone numbers and disconnect its WhatsApp number first. Deleting is
> refused (`409`, naming them) while it still holds either, because releasing a number cannot be
> undone.

When you delete a customer:

* requests into it answer `410`, and keys made for it stop working;
* its webhooks are switched off, its campaigns cancelled, its sequences and scheduled callbacks stopped;
* a call already in progress finishes;
* **30 days later it is erased**: every conversation, contact, recording and file.

Until then you can bring it back:

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/customers/org_1f2e…/restore
```

Restoring does not restart campaigns or bring back old keys — start those again yourself.

## Keys for one customer

To give a customer its own API access, or to run one customer's integration on a key that cannot
reach the others:

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/customers/org_1f2e…/keys
```

```json theme={null}
{ "name": "Acme's dashboard", "scope": "read" }
```

The key (`ta_live_…`) is in the response **once**. `scope` is `full`, `build` or `read`.

| | |
| - | - |
| `GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/keys` | The customer's keys — name, prefix, access level, last used. Never the key itself. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/customers/{id}/keys/{keyId}` | Revoke it, immediately. |

A key made for one customer works only in that customer.

## Move a phone number between customers

A number one customer rents can be handed to another customer, or to your own workspace, with its
digits kept — for a customer that is splitting in two, or a number you rented for yourself while
setting a customer up.

In the console it is on the **Phone Numbers** page: open the number's menu and choose **Move to
another workspace…**. Through the API:

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/phone-numbers/918041234567/move \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Thinnest-Workspace: org_…from…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "toWorkspace": "org_…to…" }'
```

Send it as the workspace that holds the number (no header when that is your own). It answers with
the number, `from`, `to` and `paidThrough` — the last month already paid, after which the new
workspace's rent begins. The number arrives unassigned; point it with
`PATCH /api/v1/phone-numbers/{number}` as the new workspace. An Indian number needs the new
workspace's own business details approved first (`number_move_needs_business_details`), and nothing
moves during a live call (`number_on_live_call`). See
[Move Phone Number](/api-reference/phone-numbers/move-phone-number) for every refusal.

## Billing

Everything your customers use — calls, messages, replies, phone number rental — is charged to
**your** balance at your plan's prices. Your customers have no balance of their own. When your
balance runs out, your customers stop with you until you top up.

A customer is always on your plan. Your plan decides how many customers you can have:

| Plan | Customers |
| - | - |
| Free and Pay as you go | 3 |
| Pro | 100 |
| Scale | 1,000 |
| Enterprise | 10,000 |

Need more? Write to us. A deleted customer counts until it is erased.

On the Free plan, the included replies, voice minutes and WhatsApp messages are **shared** by you and
all your customers — one trial, not one each.

### What a customer can see

Your balance stays yours. Inside a customer, `GET /api/v1/usage` returns `"billedTo": "developer"` and
no `wallet`, and its console shows no balance and nothing to pay — so a key you give a customer, or a
person you invite into it, never sees what you hold.

### Your cloned voices

Every voice you clone can be used by all your customers' agents, automatically: inside a customer,
[`GET /voices`](/api-reference/voices/list-voices) lists it with `"sharedFromDeveloper": true`. Only you
can rename or delete it, and it counts against your clone limit. Its `id` inside a customer is your
own voice's `id`, the same one you see in your workspace, so you set it as an agent's `voice` the
same way. A customer's own clones are its own; you do not see them. More on the [Voice Clone](/channels/voice-clone#your-customers-can-use-your-voices) page.

### How long a customer's calls are kept

Set `callRetentionDays` on a customer with
[`PATCH /workspace`](/api-reference/workspace/update-workspace) and the `Thinnest-Workspace` header,
the same as any other setting of theirs. See [How long calls are kept](/workspace/data-and-erasure#how-long-calls-are-kept).

### Notifications

Your customers have no members of their own, so anything we would tell them — a webhook switched off,
a template rejected, a campaign in trouble — comes to **you**, with the customer's name in the title,
and is emailed according to your own notification settings. Its **Open** link takes you into that
customer's workspace, to the template or campaign it is about. So does a low-balance warning caused by
your customers' usage.

### Currency

You and your customers use one currency, fixed once you have a customer. If you have not chosen one
when you create your first customer, it is set to rupees — pick dollars before then if you bill in
dollars.


# Create Customer
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/create-customer

/api-reference/openapi.json post /customers
Creates a workspace for one of your customers and answers with its `id` — send that id as `Thinnest-Workspace` to act inside it. Your first customer makes your workspace a developer workspace; everything a customer uses (calls, messages, replies, number rental) is charged to your balance at your plan's prices, and your plan caps how many customers you may have (3 on Free and pay-as-you-go, 100 on Pro, 1,000 on Scale, 10,000 on Enterprise; a deleted customer counts until it is erased). Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry never makes a second workspace. Needs a **full** key.

# Create Customer Key
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/create-customer-key

/api-reference/openapi.json post /customers/{id}/keys
Mints an API key that works in this one customer only — to give your customer its own API access, or to run one customer's integration on a key that cannot reach the others. The full key (`ta_live_…`) is in this response **once**; store it, because it is never shown again. Its usage is still charged to you. Needs a **full** key.

# Delete Customer
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/delete-customer

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /customers/{id}
Deletes a customer: requests into it answer `410` from now on, every key made for it is revoked, its webhooks are switched off, its campaigns cancelled and its sequences and scheduled callbacks stopped (a call already in progress finishes). **30 days later it is erased** — every conversation, contact, recording and file — unless you restore it first. Refused while the customer still holds a rented phone number or a connected WhatsApp number: release those yourself first, because that cannot be undone. Deleting an already-deleted customer answers it as it is. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Customer
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/get-customer

/api-reference/openapi.json get /customers/{id}
One customer, with how many agents, active phone numbers and contacts it has and what its usage has cost you since the 1st of this month (UTC). Deleted customers waiting to be erased are found too.

# List Customer Keys
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/list-customer-keys

/api-reference/openapi.json get /customers/{id}/keys
Every API key made for this customer, newest first, revoked ones included: name, prefix, access level and when it was last used. Never the key itself. Not paged. A deleted customer answers `404`.

# List Customers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/list-customers

/api-reference/openapi.json get /customers
Your customer workspaces, newest first. Deleted customers waiting to be erased are left out unless you ask for them with `archived=true`. Call it from your own workspace: with the `Thinnest-Workspace` header it is refused, because a customer has no customers of its own.

# Restore Customer
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/restore-customer

/api-reference/openapi.json post /customers/{id}/restore
Brings back a deleted customer before its erase date, with everything it held. It does not restart campaigns or revive the keys that were revoked when it was deleted: start those again and mint new keys. Restoring a customer that was never deleted answers it unchanged. Needs a **full** key.

# Revoke Customer Key
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/revoke-customer-key

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /customers/{id}/keys/{keyId}
Revokes one of a customer's keys, immediately: its next request answers `401`. Answers with the key as it now is. A key already revoked is `404`. Needs a **full** key.

# Update Customer
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/customers/update-customer

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /customers/{id}
Changes a customer's `name`, `externalId`, `timezone`, `allottedCallLines` or `metadata`; fields you leave out are kept. `metadata` is merged, not replaced: keys you do not mention stay, and a key set to `null` is removed. A deleted customer must be restored before it can be changed. Needs a **full** key.

# Add Do-Not-Call Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/do-not-call/add-do-not-call-number

/api-reference/openapi.json post /do-not-call
Puts a number on the list; from then on no outbound call rings it. Adding a number already there changes nothing and answers `200` with the entry as it was. A **build** key may do this — it only ever stops calls.

# Get Do-Not-Call Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/do-not-call/get-do-not-call-number

/api-reference/openapi.json get /do-not-call/{phone}
Whether a number is on the list, and how it got there.

# List Do-Not-Call Numbers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/do-not-call/list-do-not-call-numbers

/api-reference/openapi.json get /do-not-call
The workspace's do-not-call list, newest first.

# Remove Do-Not-Call Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/do-not-call/remove-do-not-call-number

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /do-not-call/{phone}
Takes a number off the list, so it can be called again. Needs a **full** key. If the person asked on a call not to be called (`source: call`), be sure they have since agreed before removing it.

# Errors
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/errors

The status, the machine-readable code that tells refusals apart, and whether retrying will help.

Every error answers a JSON body with a sentence for a person and a code for a program:

```json theme={null}
{
  "error": "That customer has asked not to be contacted.",
  "code": "opted_out"
}
```

## Branch on `code`, never on the sentence

The status says what kind of problem it is. The **`code`** says exactly which. A `403` on
`POST /calls` can mean the customer opted out, the number is on your do-not-call list, or the key
is not a full key; those are three different codes, and what you do about each is different (an
opted-out customer is never rung again, a do-not-call number can be taken off the list, a key can
be swapped for a full one).

The sentence in `error` is for showing to a person and **may be reworded in any release**. A
`code` does not change; new ones are only ever added. So match on `code`, and treat a code you do
not recognise as the generic one for its status.

```js theme={null}
const res = await fetch("https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/calls", { method: "POST", headers, body });
if (res.status === 403) {
  const { code } = await res.json();
  if (code === "opted_out" || code === "do_not_call") markUncallable(lead);
  else if (code === "key_scope_build" || code === "key_scope_read") alertOps("use a full key for calls");
}
```

### Which limit a `429` hit

A `429` names the limit in `code` and sizes it in a `limit` object, next to the `Retry-After`
header (seconds to wait):

```json theme={null}
{
  "error": "Over 60 calls a minute. Slow down and retry.",
  "code": "rate_limit_calls",
  "limit": { "name": "calls", "perMinute": 60 }
}
```

`limit.perMinute` is set for the limits counted per minute; `limit.max` (and `limit.windowSeconds`
when it has a window) for the others, such as `concurrent_calls` and the codes one number may be
sent.

### A `402` on `POST /calls`

`code` is `insufficient_balance`. The existing `reason` field says which limit stopped the call:
`no balance`, `trial spent`, `overdrawn`, `too many calls`, `balance unknown` or `retry buffer`.

## Statuses

| Status | Means | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | Malformed request, or a template blank is missing | Fix and resend. Retrying unchanged fails identically |
| `401` | Key missing, wrong or revoked | Check the header. **Do not retry**. The answer is the same whichever it is, so a probe learns nothing about your keys |
| `402` | Money or the plan: the balance cannot pay, or the plan does not include it | Top up or upgrade. `code` says which |
| `403` | The key's level, or a refusal about the person or number | `code` says which. Retrying unchanged fails the same way |
| `404` | No template of that name on your account | Check the name. Names are per account, so another business's template is invisible to you |
| `409` | Template not approved, WhatsApp not connected, contact opted out, or Meta has restricted the account | Look at **Templates** or **Channels**. Retrying makes a restriction worse |
| `409` | The same idempotency key is still in flight | Retry in a moment; the first request will have answered by then |
| `409` | Deleting an agent that is on a live call (`agent_on_live_call`: "The agent is on a live call. Delete it after the call ends.") | Nothing was deleted. Delete it after the call ends. In the console the same refusal reads "This agent is on a call right now. Delete it once the call ends." |
| `429` | Rate limited | Wait for `Retry-After` |
| `503` | WhatsApp is temporarily unavailable | Ours to fix, not yours. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key |

## Every code

Generated from the same list the API uses, so it cannot drift from it. A status with no more
specific code answers its generic one: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthorized` (401),
`payment_required` (402), `forbidden` (403), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `gone` (410),
`unprocessable` (422), `rate_limited` (429), `internal_error` (500) and `service_unavailable`
(502, 503, 504).

**The key and the workspace it acts in**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `unauthorized` | The key is missing, wrong or revoked. The answer is the same whichever it is. |
| `key_scope_read` | The key is read-only and the request changes something. Use a build or full key. |
| `key_scope_build` | The key is a build key and the request needs a full key: messaging customers, sending codes, placing calls, spending money or changing who has access. |
| `workspace_not_found` | The `Thinnest-Workspace` header names a workspace that is unknown, is not one of your customers, or is not an `org_` id. |
| `workspace_deleted` | The customer named in `Thinnest-Workspace` was deleted. Restore it before its erase date. |
| `workspace_not_developer` | `Thinnest-Workspace` was sent from a workspace that is not a developer workspace. |
| `workspace_header_forbidden` | A key that belongs to one customer workspace cannot act as another. |

**Limits: which one was hit (a `limit` object names it)**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `rate_limit_resources` | Over the per-minute limit on ordinary API requests for this workspace. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `rate_limit_family` | Over the per-minute limit across all of a developer's customers. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `rate_limit_calls` | Over the per-minute limit on `POST /calls`. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `rate_limit_messages` | Over the per-minute limit on `POST /messages`. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `rate_limit_codes` | Over the per-minute limit on `POST /codes`. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `rate_limit_code_recipient` | This number has already been sent the most codes allowed in the window. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `concurrent_calls` | Every line the plan allows is already on a call. Retry when one finishes. |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests of another kind. Wait for `Retry-After` when it is given. |

**Placing a call**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `opted_out` | The customer asked not to be contacted. Nothing you change in the request makes it allowed. |
| `do_not_call` | The number is on the workspace's do-not-call list. Remove it from the list to call it. |
| `stop_list_unknown` | The opt-out and do-not-call lists could not be read, so the call was not placed. Safe to retry shortly. |
| `insufficient_balance` | The balance cannot pay for a call. `reason` says which limit stopped it: `no balance`, `trial spent`, `overdrawn`, `too many calls`, `balance unknown` or `retry buffer`. |
| `outside_calling_hours` | It is outside the calling hours you set with `callingHours`, and the request said `ifOutsideHours: refuse`. `nextOpening` says when. With no `callingHours` a call may ring at any hour. |
| `number_never_callable` | The calling hours you set never open for this number on the days given, in its own time zone. |
| `call_in_progress` | The person is on a call right now, with this agent or another in the workspace. |
| `call_already_scheduled` | A call to this number is already scheduled on this agent. Its `id` and `scheduledFor` come back. |
| `calling_not_set_up` | The workspace has no agent that answers the phone, or its phone provider is not connected. |
| `carrier_unavailable` | The phone provider would not place the call. 503 is worth retrying; 502 is this number. |
| `agent_not_found` | No agent of that name or id answers the phone in this workspace. |
| `agent_ambiguous` | More than one agent answers the phone. Name one in `agent`. |
| `from_number_invalid` | `from` is not a number this agent can call from. |

**Agents**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `signing_unavailable` | Requests cannot be signed right now, so a setting that needs a signing secret (the who-is-calling lookup) was not saved. Try again later. |
| `agent_on_live_call` | The agent is on a live call, and deleting it would lose that call's recording, transcript and usage. Delete it after the call ends. |
| `phone_number_required` | `voice.surfaces` includes `phone`, but the agent has no phone number to answer or call from. Attach one first. |

**Numbers**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `invalid_number` | The phone number could not be read. |
| `number_required` | Connect a WhatsApp number first; this needs one. |
| `number_claimed_elsewhere` | That number is already registered here. Get in touch if it is yours. |
| `needs_own_carrier_keys` | The number is on your own carrier account; add that account's API credentials to place calls from it. |
| `number_cannot_forward` | Calls to this number cannot be forwarded: its phone provider does not support it here. |
| `forward_destination_not_allowed` | `forwardTo` is a premium-rate, shared-cost, toll-free, satellite or high-cost international number, which a forward cannot go to. |
| `forward_loop` | `forwardTo` is this number or another number on the platform, which would forward calls in a loop. |
| `number_move_needs_developer` | Moving a number between workspaces needs a developer's key, from its own workspace or acting as one of its customers. |
| `number_move_same_workspace` | `toWorkspace` is the workspace the number is already in. |
| `number_on_live_call` | The number is on a call right now. Move it once the call ends. |
| `number_move_needs_business_details` | An Indian number is held in the name of the business using it: the target workspace's business details must be approved first. |
| `number_move_carrier_account` | A number on your own carrier account moves only when both workspaces have that same account's keys saved. |
| `number_move_in_progress` | That number is already being moved (another request, or a retry still in flight). Wait a few minutes and read it again. |
| `number_move_other_region` | A rented number moves only between workspaces of the same region: United States numbers stay in workspaces billed outside India, Indian numbers in Indian ones. |
| `number_move_legacy_number` | This number was set up before workspace-level phone accounts existed and cannot be moved here. Contact support to move it. |
| `number_move_unavailable` | The phone network did not take the move. The number is still where it was, answered by no agent; safe to retry shortly. |

**Messages and codes**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `template_not_found` | No template of that name in this workspace. |
| `template_not_approved` | The template is not approved yet. |
| `template_language_missing` | The template is not approved in that language. `available` lists the ones it is. |
| `template_unsendable` | The template carries something no send can fill. Edit the template. |
| `code_template_not_found` | There is no approved one-time-code template matching the request. |
| `code_template_ambiguous` | More than one code template is approved; name one with `template` or `language`. |
| `whatsapp_not_connected` | The workspace has no connected WhatsApp number. |
| `whatsapp_blocked` | The WhatsApp account is restricted. Retrying makes a restriction worse. |
| `whatsapp_not_configured` | WhatsApp is not available right now. |
| `free_allowance_used` | The free plan's monthly WhatsApp allowance is used. Pay as you go lifts it. |
| `send_failed` | The message provider would not take the message. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key. |

**Plan and money**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `plan_required` | The plan does not include this. Upgrade to use it. |
| `plan_limit` | The plan's allowance of this is used (for example customers). Upgrade, or remove one. |
| `payment_required` | Another 402: money or a plan upgrade is needed. Read `error`. |

**Idempotency**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `idempotency_in_progress` | That `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed. Retry in a moment for its answer. |

**The generic code for a status that has no specific one**

| `code` | Means |
| - | - |
| `validation_failed` | The request was malformed or a value is out of range. Retrying unchanged fails the same way. |
| `forbidden` | Not allowed, for a reason with no more specific code. |
| `not_found` | No such resource in this workspace. |
| `conflict` | The request clashes with the resource's current state. |
| `gone` | It existed and has been deleted or has expired. |
| `unprocessable` | The request is well formed but cannot be acted on in the state things are in. |
| `internal_error` | Something failed on our side. Safe to retry; if it persists, tell us. |
| `service_unavailable` | A dependency is unavailable. Safe to retry shortly. |

## On 409 in particular

> [!WARNING]
>
> When Meta restricts an account, every refused request is a signal that the
> business has not noticed. **A retry loop against a restriction extends it.**
>
> The console shows the reason and when it lifts. Go and look rather than
> retrying.

`409` also covers the correct-behaviour cases: a **marketing** template
addressed to somebody who opted out is refused. That is not a bug to work
around.

## Retry policy that will not hurt you

```js theme={null}
const RETRYABLE = new Set([429, 500, 502, 503, 504]);

async function send(payload, key, attempt = 0) {
  const res = await post(payload, key);

  if (res.ok) return res.json();

  if (!RETRYABLE.has(res.status) || attempt >= 4) {
    // 400, 401, 404 and 409 never succeed on a retry. Surface them.
    throw new Error(`${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
  }

  const after = Number(res.headers.get("Retry-After") ?? 0);
  const backoff = after > 0 ? after * 1000 : 2 ** attempt * 1000;

  await sleep(backoff);
  // Same idempotency key on every attempt — that is what makes this safe.
  return send(payload, key, attempt + 1);
}
```

The important line is the last one: **the same idempotency key on every
attempt**. Generating a fresh key per retry turns a safe retry into a duplicate
message.

Keys are honoured for 24 hours, so a backoff that runs for minutes is well
inside the window. A job parked overnight and released the next morning is not —
it will send.


# Report Event
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/events/report-event

/api-reference/openapi.json post /events
Tells us something happened to a customer. Every sequence or tag rule subscribed to that event name runs: sequences that stop on it end first, then tags are added or removed, then sequences that start on it enrol the contact (unless they opted out, and only into an active sequence). The contact is created if the number is new. Nothing subscribed is still a `200`, with `matched: false` — you can send events before anyone has set up what they do. Only send events for people who agreed to hear from you: an event that starts a sequence is taken as their opt-in. Needs a **full** key.

# Create Form
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/create-form

/api-reference/openapi.json post /forms
Saves a form, **unpublished** — it cannot be sent until Publish Form succeeds. Up to 8 questions; field names are what each answer comes back under. Without `agent`, the form goes to the agent holding your WhatsApp number, else your oldest agent. No connected number is needed to build one. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Form
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/delete-form

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /forms/{id}
Deletes the form; it can no longer be sent. Answers already collected stay, marked as from a removed form. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Form
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/get-form

/api-reference/openapi.json get /forms/{id}
One form, with its questions and whether it can be sent.

# List Forms
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/list-forms

/api-reference/openapi.json get /forms
Your workspace's WhatsApp forms, newest first, published or not.

# Publish Form
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/publish-form

/api-reference/openapi.json post /forms/{id}/publish
Publishes the form to your workspace's **own** WhatsApp Business Account, which makes it sendable. Needs a connected WhatsApp number whose connection was finished. If WhatsApp refuses (most often because the business is not verified yet), the form stays saved and you can publish again later; a failed republish leaves the live version on the air. Needs a **full** key.

# Update Form
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/forms/update-form

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /forms/{id}
Changes any of `name`, `category` and `form` (`form` is replaced whole). **Any** change unpublishes the form, as saving does in the console — the published copy still asks the old questions — so publish it again before sending it. A **build** key may do this.

# API reference
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/introduction

The transactional API — the messages your systems send, not the ones your marketing does.

This API exists for the messages a **system** sends: an order confirmation, a
delivery update, a one-time password. One customer, one event, right now.

It is not the campaigns API, and the difference is not cosmetic.

| | Broadcasts | This API |
| - | - | - |
| Triggered by | A person, in the console | Your code, on an event |
| Audience | A list computed from consent | One customer |
| Typical category | Marketing | Utility or authentication |
| Reaches an opted-out contact | No | Yes, for utility and authentication |

If you find yourself looping this endpoint over a list of customers, you want
[broadcasts](/whatsapp/broadcasts) instead.

## Base URL

```
https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1
```

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What |
| - | - | - |
| `POST` | `/messages` | [Send a template to one customer](/api-reference/messages/send-message) |
| `POST` | `/codes` | [Send a one-time code](/api-reference/one-time-codes/send-one-time-code) |
| `POST` | `/calls` | [Ring one customer](/api-reference/calls/place-call), and get the results back |
| `GET` | `/calls/{id}` | [A call's results](/api-reference/calls/get-call) — summary, fields, transcript, recording |
| `DELETE` | `/calls/{id}` | [Cancel a waiting call, or end a live one](/api-reference/calls/get-call) |
| `POST` | `/calls/batch` | [Ring up to 200 people](/api-reference/calls/place-batch-calls) |
| `GET` | `/calls` | [List calls](/api-reference/calls/list-calls) |
| `…` | `/agents`, `/agents/{id}` | [Agents](/api-reference/agents/create-agent) — create, read, update, delete |
| `…` | `/agents/{id}/knowledge` | [What an agent knows](/api-reference/knowledge/add-knowledge-document) |
| `…` | `/agents/{id}/actions` | [Actions](/api-reference/actions/create-action) — let the agent call your own API |
| `POST` | `/agents/{id}/test-chat` | [Talk to your own agent](/api-reference/agents/test-chat) and read its reply |
| `GET` | `/templates`, `/sequences` | [The template names and sequence ids](/api-reference/templates/list-templates) the sending endpoints take |
| `…` | `/campaigns`, `/campaigns/{id}` | [Campaigns](/api-reference/campaigns/create-campaign) — results, and pause, resume, cancel |
| `…` | `/conversations/{id}/status`, `/assign`, `/members` | [Resolve, hand back, take over and assign](/api-reference/conversations/list-conversations) |
| `GET` | `/usage`, `/agents/{id}/analytics`, `/calls/summary`, `/whatsapp/summary` | [Usage and analytics](/api-reference/usage/get-usage) — the numbers to build a dashboard on |
| `GET` | `/voices`, `/models`, `/phone-numbers` | [The lists an agent is configured from](/api-reference/voices/list-voices) |
| `…` | `/contacts`, `/contacts/{id}` | [Contacts](/api-reference/contacts/create-contact) |
| `…` | `/webhooks`, `/webhooks/{id}` | [Webhook endpoints](/api-reference/webhooks) |
| `POST` | `/events` | Report an event, which can enrol a contact in a [sequence](/whatsapp/sequences) |
| `POST` | `/sequences/{sequenceId}/enrolments` | Enrol a contact directly |

Every id is prefixed by what it is — `ag_`, `act_`, `cmp_`, `cust_`, `doc_`, `wh_` — and every list
takes `limit` (up to 100) and `cursor`, answering `{ "items": […],
"nextCursor": "…" | null }`. Resource endpoints share a limit of 240 requests a
minute per workspace.

## What it will not do

> [!WARNING]
>
> * **Send an unapproved template.** Meta refuses it, so we refuse it earlier and
>   with a clearer message.
> * **Send marketing to somebody who opted out.** Refused with `409`. Utility and
>   authentication still reach them, and must.
> * **Send free-form text.** Outside the 24-hour window WhatsApp carries only
>   approved templates. Inside it, the conversation belongs to the agent and the
>   inbox.

## Start here

> [card] [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication)
>
> Creating a key, and where it must not go.

> [card] [Send a message](/api-reference/messages/send-message)
>
> The one endpoint most integrations need.


# Create Invitation
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/invitations/create-invitation

/api-reference/openapi.json post /invitations
Invites somebody to the workspace and emails them a link that works for 14 days (the email goes out just after the answer). Inviting an address that already has a pending invitation sends it again with a fresh 14 days and its new role, and answers `200` instead of `201`. Every seat counts — the people in the workspace plus pending invitations. Addresses at reserved test domains (`example.com`, `.test`, …) get the invitation but no email. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Invitation
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/invitations/get-invitation

/api-reference/openapi.json get /invitations/{id}
One invitation, whatever its status — pending, accepted or revoked.

# List Invitations
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/invitations/list-invitations

/api-reference/openapi.json get /invitations
Pending invitations, newest first. The link in each is only ever in the email, never here.

# Revoke Invitation
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/invitations/revoke-invitation

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /invitations/{id}
Revokes a pending invitation: its link stops working and its seat is freed. An invitation that was accepted or already revoked is `404`. Needs a **full** key.

# Add Knowledge Document
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/knowledge/add-knowledge-document

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/knowledge
Adds a web page (`url`) or pasted `text` to what the agent knows. A page is fetched and indexed before this answers, so a slow site is a slow request; `passages` says how much was indexed. A page that cannot be read is answered `422` with the reason and the `failed` document it left behind, which you can delete. Files are uploaded in the console. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Knowledge Document
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/knowledge/delete-knowledge-document

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}/knowledge/{documentId}
Removes the document and every passage indexed from it; the agent stops citing it at once. A **build** key may do this.

# List Knowledge Documents
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/knowledge/list-knowledge-documents

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/knowledge
The agent's documents, newest first, with whether each is ready to be cited. Files uploaded in the console are listed here too.

# Get Member
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/members/get-member

/api-reference/openapi.json get /members/{id}
One person in the workspace, with their role.

# List Members
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/members/list-members

/api-reference/openapi.json get /members
Everybody in the workspace, with their role — so a conversation can be assigned by email, or a role changed or a person removed by `id`. Not paged: every member is in one answer, and `nextCursor` is always null. Pending invitations are listed by List Invitations.

# Remove Member
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/members/remove-member

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /members/{id}
Removes a person from the workspace. Conversations assigned to them go back to the unassigned pool. The workspace's last owner cannot be removed. Needs a **full** key.

# Update Member
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/members/update-member

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /members/{id}
Changes a member's role to `admin` or `member`. A key cannot make anybody an owner — do that in the console, signed in as one — and the workspace's last owner cannot be demoted. Needs a **full** key.

# Send Message
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/messages/send-message

/api-reference/openapi.json post /messages
Sends one approved template to one number and records it in that customer's conversation. Marketing templates are refused for a customer who opted out; utility and authentication templates are not, since an order confirmation is not something a customer opts out of. Each send is charged like any WhatsApp template from your number, and the Free plan stops at its included messages. At most 60 sends a minute per workspace; send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry never sends twice. Needs a **full** key.

# List Models
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/models/list-models

/api-reference/openapi.json get /models
Every model an agent may answer with, by the name the console shows. `available` says whether your plan may pick it — the rest are listed so you can see what an upgrade adds — and `voice` whether it is quick enough to answer a call (an agent's model must be). On a workspace that brings its own keys there is also `byok`: your LLM provider, your key's own model and every model the key reaches, which is what agents run on while your own keys are on. `voiceOnlyByok` marks the models a call may run on while you bring only your own voice. `callTier` and `callPricePerMinuteMicro` are the per-minute call price the console shows beside each model, for your workspace, in `currency` micro-units. `callTier` is always `premium`: since standard voices were retired (23 October 2026) every call bills at the premium rate, or the studio rate with a studio voice, and the model never changes it. These cover the model only, with a premium voice. On a workspace using its own keys, a call bills at the BYOK per-minute rate whatever the model (all three keys, or voice key only — see Bring your own keys), so these prices apply only to an agent whose `byok` is `"off"`. Typical latency is not published.

# Get Notification Preferences
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/notifications/get-notification-preferences

/api-reference/openapi.json get /notification-preferences
Every notification category, with whether it is muted and what of it is emailed. A category never changed is shown, not muted and not emailed. Not paged: `nextCursor` is always null.

# Update Notification Preferences
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/notifications/update-notification-preferences

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /notification-preferences
Changes any categories at once, keyed by category: `muted` hides it from the feed and the bell (a critical notice shows regardless), `email` chooses what is emailed. A field you leave out keeps its value. Emails go only through the email sender connected in the console's notification settings; until one is connected nothing is emailed, whatever this says, and that connection is not available by API. Answers with every category. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Code Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/create-code-template

/api-reference/openapi.json post /codes/templates
Saves an authentication template as a **draft**. WhatsApp writes the words; you choose how long the code lasts, whether to add "For your security, do not share this code.", and the button — `copy_code` (works everywhere) or `one_tap` (hands the code to your Android app, which needs `apps`). Nothing is sent to WhatsApp until Submit Code Template. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Code Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/delete-code-template

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /codes/templates/{id}
Deletes the template — at WhatsApp first when it was submitted, then here. WhatsApp keeps a deleted template's name reserved for 30 days, so a replacement needs a different name. Codes stop sending at once if this was your only approved one. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Code Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/get-code-template

/api-reference/openapi.json get /codes/templates/{id}
One authentication template, with its review status and WhatsApp's reason when it was rejected.

# List Code Templates
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/list-code-templates

/api-reference/openapi.json get /codes/templates
Your workspace's authentication templates — drafts, those in review and approved ones — newest first.

# Send One-Time Code
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/send-one-time-code

/api-reference/openapi.json post /codes
Sends a code you generated to a WhatsApp number, using your approved authentication template — the code goes into the message **and** the copy-code button. We do not generate, store, expire or check the code; that stays yours. One number may be sent at most 5 codes in 10 minutes, and the workspace at most 120 sends a minute (codes keep the top of the budget it shares with Send Message). Each code is charged at WhatsApp's authentication rate, which is far higher for numbers abroad. Needs a **full** key.

# Submit Code Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/submit-code-template

/api-reference/openapi.json post /codes/templates/{id}/submit
Sends a draft to WhatsApp for review, on your workspace's own WhatsApp Business Account — so a connected number is needed first. The status moves to `pending` only when WhatsApp took it. Review usually takes minutes; a `template.*` webhook and Get Code Template tell you how it went. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Code Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/one-time-codes/update-code-template

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /codes/templates/{id}
Changes any of a **draft**'s fields; the ones you leave out keep their values. Once a template has been submitted, WhatsApp has the text and it can no longer be edited — make a new one instead. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Business Details
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/get-business-details

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers/business-details
Where this workspace's business details stand. India issues a number only to a business it has approved, in the business's own name, so there is one application per workspace — a platform with a workspace per customer sends and reads each customer's own (with the `Thinnest-Workspace` header). Returns `{ "status": "none" }` until details are sent. `canRent` is true once the details are approved (`accepted`) — the point from which an Indian number can be rented. `reviewNote` appears when the application was `rejected` and says what to correct. `businessName` is null if the application's name could not be read just now. The document itself is never returned. Any key can read this; the status is checked live, so it is current. Checks usually finish in minutes.

# Get Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/get-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers/{number}
One number this workspace holds: who answers it, who calls out on it, and its name. A number held by another workspace is `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

# Import Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/import-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json post /phone-numbers/import
Brings a number you own on your own carrier account. It stays on your account and you keep paying your carrier for it; we never bill it. For carriers that sign their calls with your account's secret, save the account's keys first (Save Carrier Account) — we also use them to check the number is really on that account. `setup` says what is left to do: where the number must send its calls, and whether we pointed it there ourselves. Bringing the same number again is not an error; it corrects `provider`. The number arrives answered by nobody — Update Phone Number points it at an agent. Needs a paid plan and a **full** key.

# List Available Cities
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/list-available-cities

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers/available/cities
The cities (India) or states (United States) Search Available Phone Numbers accepts as `city`, with how many numbers each has. Use these spellings exactly: "Bangalore" finds numbers where "Bengaluru" finds none, and a state is its full name ("California"). Empty on the Free plan or when the stock cannot be reached. Not paged.

# List Carrier Accounts
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/list-carrier-accounts

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers/carrier-accounts
Your own carrier accounts we hold verified keys for — the accounts your brought numbers live on — each by the last four characters of its account id, never any part of the secret. A carrier missing from the list has no keys saved: its brought numbers can answer calls (where the carrier allows) but not call out. Not paged.

# List Phone Numbers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/list-phone-numbers

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers
Every number this workspace can call from or be called on — rented and brought — with the agent that answers each. Not paged. `label` is always `null` here for a brought number; Get Phone Number reads it.

# Move Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/move-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json post /phone-numbers/{number}/move
In the console, developers do this from the Numbers page: open the number's menu and choose **Move to another workspace…**.

Moves a number, **keeping its digits**, from the workspace the request runs in to another workspace of the same developer: the developer's own, or any of its customers. Send it from the developer's own workspace, or as the customer that holds the number with `Thinnest-Workspace`; a key made for one customer cannot. The number leaves every agent and calling pool where it was and arrives **answered by nobody** — point it with `PATCH /phone-numbers/{number}` (as the target workspace) once it is there.

**Rent** continues from the next period on the target. The month already paid is not charged again, and inside one developer both workspaces bill the developer, so no money moves.

**An Indian number** is held in the name of the business using it: the target workspace's business details must be approved first (`PUT /phone-numbers/business-details` as that workspace), and the move re-registers the number to that business.

**A brought number** (on your own carrier account) moves only when both workspaces have that same account's keys saved. Refused while the number is on a call. **Safe to retry:** repeating a move that already succeeded to the same workspace answers the same `200` (for a day). Needs a **full** key.

# Release Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/release-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /phone-numbers/{number}
Gives a number up; either way it stops being any agent's line and leaves every agent's calling pool. A **brought** number is simply forgotten: it stays yours on your own carrier account, and calls to it are declined until you repoint it. A **rented** number is **released, permanently**: it goes back to the pool, anybody may rent it next, and this month's rent is not refunded — so it is refused unless you add `?confirm=release`. Needs a **full** key.

# Rent Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/rent-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json post /phone-numbers
Rents a number from Search Available Phone Numbers. **This costs money:** the first month's rent (the `monthlyPrice` the search showed) is charged from your balance at once, and again every month on the same day until you release the number. Every refusal happens before anything is bought or charged. An Indian number also needs your business details sent and approved first (Send Business Details, or the console's Phone Numbers page). The number arrives answered by nobody — Update Phone Number points it at an agent. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry cannot rent twice: a repeat returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and a request that failed lets the same key try again. Needs a **full** key.

# Save Carrier Account
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/save-carrier-account

/api-reference/openapi.json put /phone-numbers/carrier-accounts/{provider}
Saves the keys of your own account with a carrier, which lets its brought numbers be confirmed, answered and called out from. The keys are checked with the carrier before anything is stored, stored sealed, and never returned. One account per carrier: switching to a different account while numbers are still brought on the first is refused. `telnyx` takes its API key as `token` alone. Needs a **full** key — a carrier credential can spend money on your account.

# Search Available Phone Numbers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/search-available-phone-numbers

/api-reference/openapi.json get /phone-numbers/available
Local numbers you can rent in your workspace's region (Indian numbers for a workspace billed in India, United States numbers for one billed anywhere else), each with its monthly rent at your plan's rate in your balance's currency. Numbers somebody already holds are left out, so a page (up to twenty) can hold fewer and still have more after it: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Needs a paid plan.

# Send Business Details
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/send-business-details

/api-reference/openapi.json put /phone-numbers/business-details
Sends the business's details for approval, as multipart/form-data: the legal name, whether it is registered for GST, and **one** document — the GST certificate if it is, otherwise its Certificate of Incorporation or its Udyam certificate (say which in `documentKind`; incorporation is assumed). PDF, JPG or PNG, at most 5 MB, filename at most 99 characters. This is the Business details form in the console, run by the same code. The details go to India's numbering authority in the business's name, so this needs a **full** key. There is one live application per workspace: sending while one is being checked, or after it was approved, is `409`; sending after a `rejected` one corrects that application in place (`200`), and a first or expired one creates a new application (`201`). Approval usually takes a few minutes — read it with Get Business Details, then rent the number. Needs a paid plan.

# Update Phone Number
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/phone-numbers/update-phone-number

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /phone-numbers/{number}
Points a number at an agent, lends it to one for calling out, names it, or forwards its calls — any of the four. `agent` makes the number that agent's line (it stops being any other agent's; the agent must have voice switched on); `callingAgent` lets an agent call out on it without answering it (a brought number needs its carrier account's keys saved first); `forwardTo` sends every call to another phone, and works whether or not an agent answers the number (in the console: Numbers page, the number's menu, **Forward calls**). They are applied in the order `label`, `agent`, `callingAgent`, `forwardTo`, and a refusal stops there with the earlier changes kept. Needs a **full** key.

# Delete Call Content
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/post-call/delete-call-content

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /calls/{id}/content
Deletes ONE call's recording and transcript, and keeps its billing record. Gone: the recording (ours, the phone provider's copy of a call on a number we rent, and any copy made for model training), this call's own turns in its conversation (other calls and chats with the same person stay), its summary, its collected fields, and the summary handed on with a warm hand-off. Kept: the call itself — when it happened, who it was with, how long it lasted, what it cost and `billing`. Afterwards Get Call answers with `recording: null`, an empty `transcript`, `contentDeleted: true` and `contentDeletedAt`. A recording that cannot be deleted at that moment is queued and retried every night until it is gone, and counted in `recordingsPending`. For a call you placed that was retried, every attempt's content goes. This cannot be undone.

This is not Cancel Call: `DELETE /calls/{id}` still calls a call off. Safe to repeat — again answers 200 with the first deletion's time. Needs a **full** key; a developer reaches a customer's call with `Thinnest-Workspace`.

# Get Call Analysis
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/post-call/get-call-analysis

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/{id}/analysis
What one call came to, without the transcript: the outcome as the console's call log shows it ("Answered", "Line busy", "Answering machine"), the summary and the collected fields. `outcome` is null until the call has ended; `analysedAt` null means the summary and fields may still arrive, and `call.analysed` is sent the moment they do. Any id List Calls hands out works.

# Get Post-call Settings
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/post-call/get-post-call-settings

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/post-call
What an agent does after each call: whether it summarises and records calls, how long your plan keeps a recording, and the details it collects. These are the agent's own settings — the same values Get Agent shows under `voice` and `collectFields` — and `followUp`, the WhatsApp and/or SMS the agent sends the caller when a call ends.

# Update Post-call Settings
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/post-call/update-post-call-settings

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}/post-call
Changes what an agent does after each call; send only what you are changing. `collectFields` replaces the whole list, and an empty list stops collecting (details already collected are kept). Any other key is refused — the rest of the agent belongs to Update Agent. `followUp` sets the WhatsApp and/or SMS sent to the caller when a call ends, and is partial: what it leaves out keeps what is saved. A WhatsApp template must be an approved Utility one; an SMS needs a connected SMS provider. Answers with the settings as they now stand. A **build** key may do this, except `followUp`: it messages customers, so it needs a **full** key.

# Create Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/projects/create-project

/api-reference/openapi.json post /projects
Adds a project. Every workspace starts with its default project; a second one needs a plan with teams and projects, and is refused with `402` otherwise. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/projects/delete-project

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /projects/{id}
Deletes a project and its team grants. Refused for the default project, and while any agent is still in the project — move them first. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/projects/get-project

/api-reference/openapi.json get /projects/{id}
One project, with how many agents are in it.

# List Projects
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/projects/list-projects

/api-reference/openapi.json get /projects
The workspace's projects, newest first, each with how many agents are in it.

# Update Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/projects/update-project

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /projects/{id}
Renames a project. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Call Recording
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/recordings/get-call-recording

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/{id}/recording
One call's audio as MP3, streamed — it plays inline, or with `download=1` saves as `call-{id}.mp3`. `Range` requests are honoured so a player can seek, and nothing is cached. A recording lands about a minute after the call ends (`404` with `Retry-After` until then) and is deleted when your plan's retention runs out (`410`): 30 days on Free and pay-as-you-go, 49 on Pro, 75 on Scale, 365 on Enterprise. Any id List Calls hands out works.

# Get Recording By Signed Link
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/recordings/get-recording-by-signed-link

/api-reference/openapi.json get /recordings/{callId}
The signed link a call report hands out as `recording.url`, for a CRM user to click: it needs **no API key**, because the signature is the permission. Use the URL exactly as the report gives it; add `&download=1` to save rather than play. The link stops working at its `expiresAt`, which is when your plan deletes the recording. A forged link and an unknown call get the same `404`. Answers are plain text, not JSON.

# Create Saved Reply
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/saved-replies/create-saved-reply

/api-reference/openapi.json post /saved-replies
Adds a saved reply, offered in the inbox composer as `/shortcut`. A leading `/` on the shortcut is dropped. A shortcut already used — in any capitalisation — is `409`. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Saved Reply
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/saved-replies/delete-saved-reply

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /saved-replies/{id}
Deletes a saved reply. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Saved Reply
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/saved-replies/get-saved-reply

/api-reference/openapi.json get /saved-replies/{id}
One saved reply.

# List Saved Replies
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/saved-replies/list-saved-replies

/api-reference/openapi.json get /saved-replies
The workspace's saved replies, newest first.

# Update Saved Reply
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/saved-replies/update-saved-reply

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /saved-replies/{id}
Changes a saved reply's `shortcut`, `body`, or both. A **build** key may do this.

# SDKs
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sdks

Typed TypeScript and Python clients for every endpoint, with retries, idempotency and pagination built in.

Two small clients are generated from the same OpenAPI document as this reference, so every
endpoint here has a method, with typed request bodies and responses.

| | TypeScript | Python |
| - | - | - |
| Package | `@thinnestai/sdk` | `thinnestai` |
| Runtime | Node 18.17+, Deno, Bun, browsers — the global `fetch`, no dependencies | Python 3.9+, `httpx` only |
| Clients | `Client` | `Client` and `AsyncClient`, the same shape |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The packages are **not yet published to npm or PyPI**. Until they are, install them from a copy of
> the repository:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> npm install ./sdks/typescript      # TypeScript
> pip install ./sdks/python          # Python
> ```
>
> The compiled `dist/` is not committed, so installing from a path builds it: the package's
> `prepare` script fetches the TypeScript compiler with `npx` (the machine needs network access
> the first time) and compiles `src/`. If your npm blocks install scripts, or you copied the
> folder instead of installing it, run `npm install && npm run build` inside it once.

## Quickstart

```ts TypeScript theme={null}
import { Client, ApiError } from "@thinnestai/sdk";

const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY! });

// Create an agent
const agent = await client.agents.create({ name: "Skyline Sales" });

// Place a call
const call = await client.calls.place({
  to: "+91 98765 43210",
  purpose: "I'm calling from Skyline Homes about your enquiry.",
  agent: agent.id,
});

// Act in one of your customers' workspaces
const customer = await client.customers.create({ name: "Sunrise Dental Clinic" });
const sunrise = client.withWorkspace(customer.id);
await sunrise.agents.list();
```

```python Python theme={null}
import os
from thinnestai import Client, ApiError

client = Client(os.environ["API_KEY"])

# Create an agent
agent = client.agents.create({"name": "Skyline Sales"})

# Place a call
call = client.calls.place({
    "to": "+91 98765 43210",
    "purpose": "I'm calling from Skyline Homes about your enquiry.",
    "agent": agent["id"],
})

# Act in one of your customers' workspaces
customer = client.customers.create({"name": "Sunrise Dental Clinic"})
sunrise = client.with_workspace(customer["id"])
sunrise.agents.list()
```

`withWorkspace` / `with_workspace` sends the `Thinnest-Workspace` header on every request (see
[Customers](/api-reference/customers)). The `customers.*` methods and `usage.getCustomers` ignore it, because those endpoints are always
called as you, never as one of your customers. To fix one workspace for a whole client, pass
`workspace: "org_…"` (TypeScript) or `workspace="org_…"` (Python) when you create it.

## How methods are named

One namespace per group in this reference — `agents`, `calls`, `customers`, `phoneNumbers`
(`phone_numbers` in Python), `webhooks`, … — and a method per endpoint, named for what it does:
`client.agents.list()`, `client.calls.place(…)`, `client.customers.restore(id)`.

* Path parameters come first, then the request body.
* TypeScript takes query parameters as an object after the body, then `RequestOptions`
  (`idempotencyKey`, `headers`, `signal`, `timeoutMs`, `maxRetries`).
* Python takes query parameters as keyword arguments (`client.calls.list(status="completed")`),
  plus `extra_headers=`, `timeout=` and, where the endpoint accepts one, `idempotency_key=`.
* Binary answers (call recordings, voice previews) come back as a `Blob` / `bytes`; text answers
  (a transcript as text, a CSV export) as a string.

## Pagination

List endpoints answer one page, `{ items, nextCursor }`. Each has a companion that walks every page:

```ts TypeScript theme={null}
for await (const agent of client.agents.listAll({ limit: 100 })) {
  console.log(agent.name);
}
```

```python Python theme={null}
for agent in client.agents.list_all(limit=100):
    print(agent["name"])

# AsyncClient
async for agent in client.agents.list_all():
    print(agent["name"])
```

## Errors

Any answer outside `2xx` raises `ApiError`, carrying `status`, `message` (the `error` sentence
from [the error body](/api-reference/errors)), the response `headers` and the parsed `body`. No
answer at all — the network failed or the request timed out — raises `ApiConnectionError`.

## Retries and idempotency

The clients follow the [retry policy](/api-reference/errors) for you:

* `429` is retried for every method, waiting for `Retry-After` (up to 120 seconds; a longer wait is
  thrown rather than retried early).
* `408`, `500`, `502`, `503`, `504` and network errors are retried only for `GET` and `HEAD`, and for
  any request sent with an `Idempotency-Key`. A `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` without one is
  never replayed, because replaying it could act twice.
* Backoff is exponential with jitter, capped at 8 seconds; two retries by default (`maxRetries` /
  `max_retries`).
* These get an `Idempotency-Key` generated when you give none: `calls.place`, `calls.placeBatch`,
  `conversations.reply`, `messages.send`, `codes.send`, `customers.create` and
  `phoneNumbers.rent`. **The same key is
  sent on every retry**, so a retry never places a second call. A key you pass — as the
  `idempotencyKey` option or the `idempotencyKey` body field — is the one sent.
* `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` and `409` are never retried.


# Activate Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/activate-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sequences/{sequenceId}/activate
Turns a draft or paused sequence on: messages that fall due start going out, and its tags and events start enrolling people. Refused for a sequence with no steps, which would take people in and send nothing. Needs a **full** key.

# Add Sequence Step
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/add-sequence-step

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sequences/{sequenceId}/steps
Appends a message at the **end** of the sequence: an approved template, sent `delayHours` after the step before (or after the person joined, for the first step). Steps cannot be edited, reordered or removed — someone partway through a live sequence would skip a message or get one twice — so to change the messages, delete the sequence and make another. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/create-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sequences
Creates a sequence as a **draft**: it sends nothing until you add a step with Add Sequence Step and turn it on with Activate Sequence. Tags are stored lower-case and hyphenated, and event names lower-case with dots, as the console stores them. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/delete-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /sequences/{sequenceId}
Archives the sequence, which is how the console deletes one: it sends nothing more and leaves every list, while the record of who was sent what stays. There is no undo. A **build** key may do this.

# Enrol in Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/enrol-in-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sequences/{sequenceId}/enrolments
Puts one existing contact into a sequence, with values its messages can use — an order number your system knows and the console does not. The person must already be a contact; this never creates one. `enrolled: false` is a `200`, not an error: they are already in it, the number is not a contact, they opted out, or the sequence has no first message yet. Prefer Report Event unless your system must choose the sequence itself, since this puts a sequence id in your code. Only enrol people who agreed to hear from you. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/get-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json get /sequences/{sequenceId}
One sequence with its steps in order, the events that start and stop it, and how many people are in it, finished it or left it.

# List Sequences
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/list-sequences

/api-reference/openapi.json get /sequences
Your workspace's sequences, newest first. Deleted (archived) ones are left out. Get Sequence adds the steps, events and how many people are in each.

# Pause Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/pause-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sequences/{sequenceId}/pause
