Pauses an active sequence: nothing more is sent until it is activated again. The people in it keep their place. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Sequence
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sequences/update-sequence

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /sequences/{sequenceId}
Changes any of `name`, `exitOnReply`, `triggerTags`, `exitOnTags`, `startOn` and `stopOn`. A list you send **replaces** the old one; a list you leave out is kept. Works while the sequence runs, and applies to the people already in it — add a stop tag and they stop when they get it. Steps cannot be changed here. A **build** key may do this.

# Add SMS Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/add-sms-template

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sms/templates
Adds a template exactly as it was approved on your DLT portal, with `{#var#}` wherever the text changes. Each `{#var#}` takes at most 30 characters when sent. Promotional templates are not accepted: an agent may only send transactional or service messages. MSG91 and Fast2SMS send by their own template id, so with them `providerTemplateId` is required. Needs a **full** key.

# Connect SMS Provider
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/connect-sms-provider

/api-reference/openapi.json put /sms/provider
Connects your SMS provider, or replaces the one connected. A secret you leave out keeps the one saved, for the same provider; switching provider needs every field. The connection's `status` goes back to `untested` until Send Test SMS succeeds. Needs a **full** key.

What each provider asks for in `credentials`:

- `msg91`: `authKey`
- `exotel`: `accountSid`, `apiKey`, `apiToken`, `region` (`in` or `sg`)
- `gupshup`: `userId`, `password`
- `infobip`: `baseUrl` (your own, like `xxxxx.api.infobip.com`), `apiKey`
- `vonage`: `apiKey`, `apiSecret`
- `fast2sms`: `apiKey`

# Delete SMS Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/delete-sms-template

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /sms/templates/{id}
Deletes a template. An agent that sent it after its calls stops sending an SMS then. Needs a **full** key.

# Disconnect SMS Provider
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/disconnect-sms-provider

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /sms/provider
Forgets the provider and its credentials, and switches `send_sms` off on every agent. Your templates are kept. Needs a **full** key.

# Get SMS Provider
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/get-sms-provider

/api-reference/openapi.json get /sms/provider
The workspace's SMS provider, sender header and DLT entity id. Secrets are never returned: `secretsSaved` names the ones held.

# List SMS Templates
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/list-sms-templates

/api-reference/openapi.json get /sms/templates
The workspace's DLT templates, by name.

# Send Test SMS
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/send-test-sms

/api-reference/openapi.json post /sms/test
Sends one template to one Indian mobile number through your provider — a real SMS, billed by your provider — to prove the provider, header and DLT ids work together. Success sets the connection's `status` to `working`; a provider's refusal sets it to `failing` with the reason. Needs a **full** key.

# Update SMS Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/sms/update-sms-template

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /sms/templates/{id}
Changes any of a template's fields; what you leave out stays. If an agent sends this template after its calls, a body with a different number of `{#var#}` is refused until that agent's follow-up is changed. Needs a **full** key.

# Add Team Member
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/add-team-member

/api-reference/openapi.json put /teams/{id}/members/{memberId}
Puts a member of the workspace in the team, so they can reach the team's projects. Repeating it changes nothing. Answers with the team. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Team
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/create-team

/api-reference/openapi.json post /teams
Adds an empty team; put members in it and grant it projects with the team's sub-resources. Teams need a plan with teams and projects, and are refused with `402` otherwise. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Team
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/delete-team

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /teams/{id}
Deletes a team and its grants. A project only this team could reach opens to the whole workspace. The people stay in the workspace. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Team
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/get-team

/api-reference/openapi.json get /teams/{id}
One team, with its members' ids and the projects it can reach.

# Grant Team Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/grant-team-project

/api-reference/openapi.json put /teams/{id}/projects/{projectId}
Lets the team reach a project. A project's first grant **restricts** it: from then on only the teams granted it (plus owners and admins) can see its agents. Repeating it changes nothing. Answers with the team. A **build** key may do this.

# List Teams
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/list-teams

/api-reference/openapi.json get /teams
The workspace's teams, newest first, each with its members' ids and the projects it can reach.

# Remove Team Member
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/remove-team-member

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /teams/{id}/members/{memberId}
Takes a member out of the team; they stay in the workspace. Taking out somebody who is not in the team changes nothing. Answers with the team. A **build** key may do this.

# Revoke Team Project
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/revoke-team-project

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /teams/{id}/projects/{projectId}
Takes a project out of the team's reach. When that was the project's last grant, the project opens to the whole workspace again. Answers with the team. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Team
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/teams/update-team

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /teams/{id}
Renames a team. A **build** key may do this.

# Create Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/create-template

/api-reference/openapi.json post /templates
Saves a WhatsApp template as a draft, after the console's own checks of WhatsApp's rules for the body, header, footer, buttons and an authentication template's code. Review is a separate, deliberate step — Submit Template, or `submit: true` here — because once a name is approved it can never be reused for different words; if that submission is refused, the draft is kept and `message` says why. Limited-time offers, carousels and buttons that open a WhatsApp form are made in the console. Needs a **full** key.

# Delete Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/delete-template

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /templates/{name}
Deletes a WhatsApp template. One that was sent for review is deleted from WhatsApp first — only that language — and from your workspace only once that works, so a refusal leaves everything as it was. This cannot be undone, and WhatsApp may keep a deleted name reserved for a while, so it may not be reusable straight away. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/get-template

/api-reference/openapi.json get /templates/{name}
Returns one WhatsApp template by name, with its parts — header text, footer, buttons — and, when WhatsApp refused it, the reason in `reviewNote`. Poll it after Submit Template to follow the review: `status` moves from `pending` to `approved` or `rejected`. Pass `language` when the name exists in more than one.

# List Templates
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/list-templates

/api-reference/openapi.json get /templates
Lists your workspace's WhatsApp templates, newest first, with what a send needs from each: how many body values (`variableCount`), how many link-button values (`buttonVariableCount`) and whether the header needs a media link (`headerKind`). Only `approved` templates can be sent.

# Submit Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/submit-template

/api-reference/openapi.json post /templates/{name}/submit
Sends a **draft** template to your own WhatsApp Business Account for review, after the same last checks as the console's Submit. The template moves to `pending` only if WhatsApp accepted it. Review usually takes minutes, occasionally days; follow it with Get Template, whose `status` becomes `approved` or `rejected` (with the reason in `reviewNote`). A workspace with no connected WhatsApp number has no account to submit to. Needs a **full** key.

# Update Template
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/templates/update-template

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /templates/{name}
Edits a **draft** template. Send only the fields that change; the result is checked against the same rules as Create Template. Once a template has been sent for review WhatsApp has its text, so it can no longer be edited — create a new template instead. Changing `name` or `language` renames it. A **build** key may do this. The one exception is `agentMaySend` (whether an agent may send the template in a call or chat): it goes alone and needs a **full** key.

# Configure Connection
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/configure-connection

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}/connections/{kind}
Pin a connection to its target, say how a lead's row is found, choose when it saves, and switch its tools. The account must be connected first (records excepted). Changes apply in a fixed order and stop at the first refusal, keeping what came before it. Helpdesks have nothing to configure. A **build** key may do this.

# Connect Account
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/connect-account

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/connections/{kind}
Connect (or re-key) an account. Every key, token and secret is sealed and never returned. Connecting grants nothing: tools start off and are switched with `PATCH` `tools`. `googlesheets`, `zoho`, `zoho_bigin`, `hubspot` and `calendly` sign in on the provider's own consent screen — connect them once in the console (this answers `409`), then configure them here. A helpdesk connect opens one test ticket or case and answers with `inbound` **once**; a records connect that makes the first link answers with `link.passcode` **once**. A **build** key may do this.

# Connect Tool Server
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/connect-tool-server

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/mcp-servers
Connect an MCP tool server that takes a token (or none). It is asked for its tools at once and every tool arrives **off** — switch each on with `PATCH …/tools/{toolId}`. A server that cannot be reached is still saved and answers `201` with `status: "failed"` and the reason in `message`, so you can fix it and sync. A server that signs in through a browser must be connected in the console. A **build** key may do this.

# Disconnect Account
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/disconnect-account

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}/connections/{kind}
Disconnect the account; its tools leave the agent and its credential is deleted. A browser sign-in still pending is cancelled too. What already happened in the account (meetings booked, rows written) is untouched, and records already collected are kept. A **build** key may do this.

# Disconnect Tool Server
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/disconnect-tool-server

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /agents/{id}/mcp-servers/{serverId}
Disconnect the server; its tools leave the agent at once and its token is deleted. This works for servers connected in the console too. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Connection
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/get-connection

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/connections/{kind}
One connection, connected or not, with the shared tool budget.

# Get Tool Server
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/get-tool-server

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/mcp-servers/{serverId}
One tool server and its tools.

# List Built-in Tools
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/list-built-in-tools

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/tools
The agent's built-in tools — the Actions page's switches — with the recall, verification and hand-over settings. The three tools that reach a customer on another channel also say whether they are `ready` (on, and what they need exists) and what they `needs`.

# List Connection Options
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/list-connection-options

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/connections/{kind}/options
What a connected account can reach, read live each time, so you can choose a `target` for `PATCH …/connections/{kind}`: a Grist document's tables and columns (`?doc=`), a spreadsheet's sheets (`?spreadsheet=`), the modules a Zoho account can write to, HubSpot's one module (`contacts`), or a Calendly account's meeting types. Other kinds have nothing to choose.

# List Connections
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/list-connections

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/connections
Every account the agent can work in, connected or not — a calendar, two spreadsheets, two CRMs, records kept here and two helpdesks — each with its state, what it is pinned to and its tools. `toolsInUse` / `maxTools` is the one budget every connection's switches share. Credentials never appear.

# List Tool Servers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/list-tool-servers

/api-reference/openapi.json get /agents/{id}/mcp-servers
Every tool server the agent is connected to, oldest first, each with its tools. All come in one page. Tokens never appear; `hasSecret` says one is held.

# Replace Records Link
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/replace-records-link

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/connections/records/link
Make a new link to read the records the agent collects, with a new passcode — shown in this response and never again. The old link stops working at once, which is also how a link shared too widely is revoked. A **build** key may do this.

# Sync Tool Server
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/sync-tool-server

/api-reference/openapi.json post /agents/{id}/mcp-servers/{serverId}/sync
Ask the server what it offers, again — the console's Refresh, and the closest thing to a test. New tools arrive off; tools it no longer lists leave the agent. A store connection has a fixed list and is refused. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Built-in Tools
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/update-built-in-tools

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}/tools
Switch built-in tools on or off and set recall, code verification and the hand-over. `search_knowledge` is not a switch and web search cannot be switched on; both are refused. Changes apply in order and stop at the first refusal, keeping what came before. Needs a **full** key. — it can arm tools that call or message customers.

# Update Tool Server Tool
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/tools/update-tool-server-tool

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /agents/{id}/mcp-servers/{serverId}/tools/{toolId}
Switch one of a server's tools on or off. On, it is callable from every conversation the agent has. Answers with the server and all its tools. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Calls Summary
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/get-calls-summary

/api-reference/openapi.json get /calls/summary
Call totals for the last `days` — calls, inbound, outbound, answered, missed, failed, seconds, what they cost, by surface — and a series by hour (`days=1`) or by day, bucketed in your workspace's time zone. The dashboard's calls figures. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Get Customers Usage
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/get-customers-usage

/api-reference/openapi.json get /customers/usage
Developers: what each of your customers cost you over a range, in one call — spend net of refunds, how many charges, and spend by kind. Customers with no charges in the range are left out (list them with `GET /customers`). Without `from`/`to` it is this month so far; days are UTC and a range covers at most 366 days. Call it from your own workspace: the `Thinnest-Workspace` header is refused. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Get Daily Usage
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/get-daily-usage

/api-reference/openapi.json get /usage/daily
Replies, calls and call minutes for every UTC day in the window — the Usage page's chart, quiet days as zeros. Give a rolling `days`, or a `from`/`to` range of up to 366 days reaching back at most 730 days; a `to` past today is cut to today. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Get Usage
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/get-usage

/api-reference/openapi.json get /usage
Your plan, this calendar month's (UTC) replies against its allowance, the wallet, and replies per UTC day for the last `days` — the figures on the console's Usage page. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Get WhatsApp Summary
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/get-whatsapp-summary

/api-reference/openapi.json get /whatsapp/summary
WhatsApp messages sent and received, how many were delivered, read or failed (with failure codes), a series, and what they cost you — the WhatsApp dashboard's figures. Either a rolling `days` or a `from`/`to` range (inclusive, up to 366 days), in your workspace's time zone; `from`/`to` wins when both are given. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# List Call Log
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/list-call-log

/api-reference/openapi.json get /usage/calls
The Usage page's call log: every call made or taken, newest first, with how it ended and what it was charged. `format=csv` returns the console's export instead — the same calls, up to 10,000, as a `calls.csv` attachment (columns Started, Direction, Surface, Agent, Number, From, Outcome, Status, Seconds, Cost, then Summary, then one column for each detail the agent collected, named as your agent names it, in the order they first appear: up to 20; a call that did not collect one has an empty cell); `limit` and `cursor` do not apply to it. `GET /calls` is the integration view of the same calls; this is the billing view. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# List Invoices
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/list-invoices

/api-reference/openapi.json get /invoices
One invoice for every payment taken, newest first — the rows under Settings → Billing → History → Invoices. Amounts are integer **minor** units (paise, cents) of `currency`, as issued — not micro-units. `from`/`to` filter on the issue date. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# List Wallet Ledger
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/usage/list-wallet-ledger

/api-reference/openapi.json get /wallet/ledger
The balance history — every top-up, reply, call, WhatsApp message, number rental, refund and adjustment, newest first, with the balance after each (Settings → Billing → History). A developer's charges for its customers land on its own ledger, each naming the customer; `customer` narrows to one (read with your own key, no `Thinnest-Workspace` header). Reads only: money is added in the console. Any key may call this, a **read-only** key included.

# Create Voice Clone
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voice-clones/create-voice-clone

/api-reference/openapi.json post /voice-clones
Clones a voice from a 5–30 second recording, sent as multipart/form-data with the audio as `sample`. Both consent fields must be `true` — the two promises the console shows — or nothing is stored or sent anywhere; the refusal carries the two sentences so you can show your own user the same words. Cloning is on the Pro plan and above, up to your plan's number of voices (10 on Pro, 20 on Scale). Needs a **full** key.

# Delete Voice Clone
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voice-clones/delete-voice-clone

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /voice-clones/{id}
Forgets the voice everywhere — the voice, its recording and its preview — and moves every agent that spoke with it to a Premium voice; `movedAgents` says how many. It cannot be undone. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Voice Clone
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voice-clones/get-voice-clone

/api-reference/openapi.json get /voice-clones/{id}
One cloned voice, with a preview link that works for sixty seconds — long enough to play, too short to share.

# List Voice Clones
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voice-clones/list-voice-clones

/api-reference/openapi.json get /voice-clones
Your workspace's cloned voices, newest first, with a short-lived link to each one's preview and the consent it was made under.

# Update Voice Clone
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voice-clones/update-voice-clone

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /voice-clones/{id}
Renames, re-describes or re-tags a cloned voice. Its language, recording and consent are what it was made from and cannot be changed; sending any other field is refused. A **build** key may do this.

# List Voices
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/voices/list-voices

/api-reference/openapi.json get /voices
Every voice your agents may speak with, in the picker's order: premium, then Studio. `tier` is the price band a call is billed at: `premium` or `studio`. Standard voices were retired on 23 October 2026 and are no longer listed. Studio voices — the shared Studio catalogue and your own clones (`mine: true`) and, in a developer's customer workspace, the developer's clones (`sharedFromDeveloper: true`) — are listed only on the Pro plan and above, so every id here is one you can set. Every voice speaks every supported language; the agent's language decides which.

# Webhooks
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks

Add, list, change and remove the endpoints an agent's events are sent to.

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/webhooks
Authorization: Bearer ta_live_…
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "agent": "ag_5c4a5f93-…",
  "url": "https://crm.example.com/hooks/thinnest",
  "events": ["call.analysed", "call.completed"]
}
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "wh_e1c5…",
  "agent": "ag_5c4a5f93-…",
  "url": "https://crm.example.com/hooks/thinnest",
  "events": ["call.analysed", "call.completed"],
  "enabled": true,
  "delivery": { "failuresInARow": 0, "lastStatus": null, "lastError": null, "lastSentAt": null },
  "createdAt": "2026-09-17T09:41:00Z",
  "signingSecret": "s3cr3t…"
}
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> **`signingSecret` is in the create response and nowhere else.** Store it.
> Every delivery carries `x-thinnest-signature: sha256=…`, an HMAC of the raw
> body under this secret, and `x-thinnest-signature-v2`, which also signs the
> delivery time — see [Delivery](#delivery).

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What |
| - | - | - |
| `GET` | `/webhooks` | List, newest first. `agent` filters |
| `POST` | `/webhooks` | Add one. `url`, and `agent` — or `includeCustomers: true` |
| `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}` | One endpoint, with its delivery state |
| `PATCH` | `/webhooks/{id}` | `url`, `events`, `enabled` |
| `DELETE` | `/webhooks/{id}` | Remove it |
| `POST` | `/webhooks/{id}/test` | Send a sample event and say whether it arrived |
| `GET` | `/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` | Recent deliveries, newest first, with attempts and the next retry |
| `POST` | `/webhooks/{id}/redeliver` | Send one delivery again, or everything that failed since a time |

## Fields

**agent** `string` *required*

Whose events. Required on create — unless `includeCustomers` is `true`.

**includeCustomers** `boolean`

For a workspace with [customers](/api-reference/customers): one endpoint for the events of every
agent in every one of your customers. It has no `agent` (send one or the other, not both). Each
delivery's `data` carries `workspaceId` — the customer it is about — inside the signed body.

**url** `string` *required*

An `https://` address, or an email address — a helpdesk that opens tickets by
mail gets one email per event. Addresses inside our own network are refused.

**events** `string[]`

Which events to send. Leave it out for every event, now and as new ones are
added; the response then reads `["*"]`.

| Event | When |
| - | - |
| `lead.captured` | The agent collected a name, email or phone from somebody interested |
| `conversation.escalated` | It handed a conversation to a person |
| `conversation.resolved` | A teammate marked one done |
| `call.completed` | A call ended — outcome and duration, the moment it ends |
| `call.analysed` | A call's [results are ready](/api-reference/calls/get-call) — summary, fields, transcript, recording link, and what the call cost (`costMicro` in millionths of `currency`; your reseller's price if you are a white-label client; `costMicro` is `null` if the call has not settled yet — read [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) later) |
| `campaign.finished` | A broadcast or calling campaign finished |
| `contact.opted_out` | During a call, somebody asked not to be called again and the agent put their number on your [do-not-call list](/channels/voice#dont-call-me-again) — `data.phone`, `data.callId`, `data.source` (always `"call"`), `data.optedOutAt`, `data.reason` (their words, or `null`) |
| `call.problem` | During a call that is [still going on](#problems-on-a-live-call): the agent could not answer, your own model key failed, a reply was very slow, or the voice connection failed. At most once per kind per call |
| `contact.erased` | A contact you deleted is [gone completely](#workspace-events), recordings included. Sent once |
| `byok.changed` | Your [own keys](#workspace-events) changed: one was added, replaced, removed or failed its check, or they were switched on or off or set to cover different jobs |

**enabled** `boolean`

Switching an endpoint back on forgives its past failures.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `call.started` is not a webhook event you subscribe to. It is the request your own system receives
> from an agent's [Who-is-calling lookup](/channels/voice#who-is-calling-lookup), signed the same
> way, which you answer with values for the agent to use.

## Problems on a live call

`call.problem` is sent **while the call is still going on**, so you can alert
somebody or flag the call before it ends. Each kind is sent at most once per
call, and a burst across many calls is held to about 20 events a minute per
agent. An event held back by that limit is not queued: it is sent if that kind
happens again on the same call once the agent is back under the limit, and
otherwise it is not sent at all. The same problems are also on the call itself,
under **Problems on this call** in [Usage](/workspace/usage#how-a-call-went).

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_4d8b2f6a-…",
  "event": "call.problem",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:31:02.715Z",
  "data": {
    "callId": "out_9f2c1a44-…",
    "agentId": "ag_5c4a5f93-…",
    "kind": "slow_reply",
    "detail": "A reply took 6.2 seconds to start.",
    "at": "2026-10-06T04:31:02.702Z"
  }
}
```

| `kind` | What happened |
| - | - |
| `no_answer_from_model` | The agent could not get an answer — even from its backup — and apologised to the caller |
| `byok_failed` | Your [own model key](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys) failed, so the agent apologised instead of answering |
| `slow_reply` | A reply took more than 5 seconds to start |
| `voice_failed` | The call's voice connection failed — the caller may have heard silence or been cut off. It also rings the workspace's notification bell |

`callId` is the id [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) takes. `detail` is
a sentence you can show a person.

## Call quality

Every call the agent ran carries `quality`, written once when the call ends —
on [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) and in `data.quality` on
`call.completed` and `call.analysed`:

```json theme={null}
"quality": {
  "turns": 14,
  "responseMs": { "median": 1180, "p90": 1920, "max": 3410 },
  "answerMs": { "median": 1650, "p90": 2840, "max": 4120 },
  "firstTokenMs": { "median": 610, "p90": 940, "max": 1730 },
  "longSilences": 1,
  "longSilenceSeconds": 10,
  "longestSilenceSeconds": 12.4,
  "interruptions": 2,
  "knowledgeTurns": 3,
  "modelErrors": 0,
  "rescues": 1
}
```

| Field | What it is |
| - | - |
| `turns` | Caller turns the agent answered — noises that got no reply, such as an echo of the agent's own voice, are not counted |
| `responseMs` | How long the caller waited: from when they stopped speaking to the agent's first audio — median, 90th percentile and slowest, in milliseconds. A thinking line or an acknowledgement that plays first ends it |
| `answerMs` | The same wait, to the first word of the actual answer being heard. A thinking line that plays first does not end it, so a fast answer and a thinking line covering a slow one look different. `null` when it was not measured. [Get Call Timeline](/api-reference/calls/get-call-timeline) gives it for every turn |
| `firstTokenMs` | Our side of that wait: from the turn reaching the model to its first word |
| `longSilences` | Silences on either side at least `longSilenceSeconds` long — the agent's "are you still there?" time, or 10 seconds if it has none |
| `longestSilenceSeconds` | The longest stretch where nobody spoke |
| `interruptions` | Times the caller started speaking while the agent was talking |
| `knowledgeTurns` | Turns where the agent looked something up in its knowledge. `null` when the count was not available for the call |
| `modelErrors` | Turns the agent apologised for because it could not get an answer. `null` when the count was not available for the call |
| `rescues` | Turns where the agent's first choice failed and a backup answered, so the caller still got a reply. `null` when the count was not available for the call |

`quality` is `null` for a call that was not measured (a call from before these
figures were recorded, or one that never connected), and a figure inside it is
`null` when it could not be measured on that call. On `call.completed` it can
also be `null` when the call ended before its figures were ready;
`call.analysed` and Get Call have them by then. In the console the same
figures are under **How the call went** when you open the call in
[Usage](/workspace/usage#how-a-call-went).

## Calls handed to another agent

When an agent passes a live call to another of your agents
([how](/channels/voice)), `call.analysed` and Get Call list it in `handedTo`,
oldest first — empty when the call stayed with `agent`, which is always the
agent the call was placed or answered as:

```json theme={null}
"handedTo": [
  {
    "agent": { "id": "ag_7b1d4e90-2c3a-4f6e-8d15-9a0b3c2e4f71", "name": "Support" },
    "from": { "id": "ag_3f6a9c21-7d4e-4b58-9a1f-0c2e8b7d5a34", "name": "Sales" },
    "at": "2026-10-09T10:04:12Z"
  }
]
```

A hand-off to another agent is not a hand-over to a person, so it does not
send `conversation.escalated`.

**Which agent an event names.** The call-level events — `call.completed`,
`call.analysed` and `call.problem` — stay with the agent the call started
with, which is also the one the call is billed and summarised under. Events
the agents themselves raise mid-call — `lead.captured`,
`conversation.escalated` — name the agent that ran the tool in `data.agentId`
and carry `data.callId`, so on a handed call you can join them to the call
report and to `handedTo`.

**Webhooks belong to an agent.** An event raised by the agent a call was handed
to goes to *that* agent's webhooks, not to the agent that took the call first.
If you only subscribe the first agent, you will get `call.completed` and
`call.analysed` for the whole call but miss any `lead.captured` or
`conversation.escalated` the second agent raises. Add the same endpoint to every
agent a call can be handed to.

## Delivery

Each event is a `POST` of JSON:

```json theme={null}
{ "id": "evt_9d1c…", "event": "lead.captured", "sentAt": "2026-10-07T09:12:03.551Z", "data": { … } }
```

with these headers on every attempt (an email destination gets the ticket email only, without them):

| Header | What it is |
| - | - |
| `x-thinnest-signature` | `sha256=` + hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under your signing secret |
| `x-thinnest-signature-v2` | `sha256=` + hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<x-thinnest-delivered-at>.<raw body>` — the delivery time, signed |
| `x-thinnest-delivered-at` | When this attempt left (ISO 8601) |
| `x-thinnest-event-id` | `evt_…`, the same as the body's `id` — the same on every retry and re-send |
| `x-thinnest-attempt` | `1`, then `2`, `3`, … |

Each header is also sent under a neutral name with the same value: `x-webhook-signature`,
`x-webhook-signature-v2`, `x-webhook-delivered-at`, `x-webhook-event-id` and `x-webhook-attempt`.
Verify either. A white-label reseller's clients receive the neutral names only, so code you ship to
them should read those.

### Retries

Anything other than a 2xx answer — an error, a timeout after 10 seconds, an
address we cannot reach — is tried again after **1 minute, 5 minutes, 30
minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours**: six attempts over about 8½ hours. Every attempt
sends the **same bytes**, so `sentAt` is when the event happened, not when the
attempt left. Payloads are kept for **7 days**, so anything that still did not
arrive can be [sent again](#re-send-what-failed) within that week.

Re-sending a delivery starts its retry schedule afresh. Retries and re-sends
go to the endpoint's **current** address — change the URL and pending retries
follow it. A Slack or helpdesk destination that accepted a post but answered
after the 10-second timeout can receive it twice, since neither can dedupe on
the event id.

### What your receiver should do

1. **Verify** `x-thinnest-signature-v2` (or `x-thinnest-signature`) with a
   constant-time compare.
2. **Check freshness on `x-thinnest-delivered-at`** — reject one more than five
   minutes from your clock. Not on `sentAt`: a retry's `sentAt` is hours old by
   design. The delivery time is covered by the v2 signature, so it cannot be
   moved without breaking it.
3. **Dedupe on `x-thinnest-event-id`.** A retry after a timeout can reach you
   after you already handled the first attempt.
4. **Answer 2xx quickly**, then do the work.

```js theme={null}
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

function verify(secret, rawBody, headers) {
  const at = headers["x-thinnest-delivered-at"];
  const expected = "sha256=" + createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${at}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex");
  const given = headers["x-thinnest-signature-v2"] ?? "";
  const fresh = Math.abs(Date.now() - Date.parse(at)) < 5 * 60_000;
  return fresh && given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(given), Buffer.from(expected));
}
```

### Switched off

An endpoint is switched off — `enabled: false`, `delivery.lastError` says why —
after **five events in a row that each failed every attempt**. A failed attempt
that a retry then delivers does not count. Events that happen while it is off
are recorded as not sent; fix the endpoint, `PATCH { "enabled": true }`, and
re-send them — nothing within the last 7 days is lost.

## Event payloads

Every delivery is the same envelope. What changes is `data`, shown here in full for each event.
Ids in `data` are the same prefixed ids the API returns and takes: `conv_…` for a conversation
(pass it to [List Conversation Messages](/api-reference/conversations/list-conversation-messages)), `cmp_…` for a
campaign, and `out_…`, `sch_…` or the call reference for a call (pass it to
[Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call)). `conversationId` and `campaignId`
always carry their `conv_` and `cmp_` prefix, so a value from a webhook can be
passed straight to the API. If your receiver stored these ids as bare
identifiers before, store the prefixed value from now on.

An endpoint created with `includeCustomers: true` also gets `data.workspaceId` (`org_…`), the
customer the event is about.

### `lead.captured`

The agent collected contact details. `name`, `email` and `phone` are each `null` when not given; `note` is what the customer wants, written for whoever follows up. `agentId` is the agent that captured it and `callId` the call it was on (the id [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) takes; `null` off a call).

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_9d1c4b2a-7e3f-4a6b-8c1d-2e5f7a9b0c13",
  "event": "lead.captured",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:31:55.204Z",
  "data": {
    "conversationId": "conv_3f6b2d1e-8a4c-4f7b-9e21-6c0d5a7b8e94",
    "agentId": "ag_3f6a9c21-7d4e-4b58-9a1f-0c2e8b7d5a34",
    "callId": "out_6d1c2e84-3b7a-4f95-8e10-5a9b7c3d2f41",
    "name": "Asha Rao",
    "email": "asha@example.com",
    "phone": "+919876543210",
    "note": "Wants a 2 BHK at Sky Towers, budget around 80 lakh, and a site visit on Saturday."
  }
}
```

### `conversation.escalated`

The agent handed the conversation to a person. `reason` is the agent's own words. `agentId` is the agent that handed over and `callId` the call it was on (`null` off a call).

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_1a7f3c9e-5b2d-4e8a-9f6c-0d3b7e1a4c25",
  "event": "conversation.escalated",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:32:12.880Z",
  "data": {
    "conversationId": "conv_3f6b2d1e-8a4c-4f7b-9e21-6c0d5a7b8e94",
    "agentId": "ag_3f6a9c21-7d4e-4b58-9a1f-0c2e8b7d5a34",
    "callId": null,
    "reason": "The customer asked to speak to someone about a refund."
  }
}
```

### `conversation.resolved`

A teammate marked the conversation done. Sent once, when the status actually changes.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_6e2b8d4f-1c7a-4f3e-a9b5-8d0c2e6f1a37",
  "event": "conversation.resolved",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T05:10:03.551Z",
  "data": {
    "conversationId": "conv_3f6b2d1e-8a4c-4f7b-9e21-6c0d5a7b8e94"
  }
}
```

### `call.completed`

The moment a call ends, before it has been read. `outcome` is `completed`, `missed` or `failed`; `hangup` is `answered`, `no_answer`, `busy`, `rejected`, `unreachable`, `cancelled`, `voicemail`, `before_agent` or `failed`; `phone` is null on a web call. `campaignId` is present only for a campaign's call, and `id`, `reference` and `metadata` only for a call placed through the API.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_3c9a5e1b-7d4f-4b2a-8e6c-1f0d9a3b5c49",
  "event": "call.completed",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:33:12.020Z",
  "data": {
    "callRef": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "conversationId": "conv_3f6b2d1e-8a4c-4f7b-9e21-6c0d5a7b8e94",
    "outcome": "completed",
    "hangup": "answered",
    "seconds": 182,
    "direction": "outbound",
    "surface": "phone",
    "phone": "919876543210",
    "campaignId": "cmp_7a1e9c3b-2d4f-4b8a-a6e0-1f5c8d2b9e47",
    "id": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "reference": "LSQ-42",
    "metadata": {
      "deal_id": "D-19",
      "owner": "Ravi"
    },
    "quality": {
      "turns": 14,
      "responseMs": { "median": 1180, "p90": 1920, "max": 3410 },
      "answerMs": { "median": 1650, "p90": 2840, "max": 4120 },
      "firstTokenMs": { "median": 610, "p90": 940, "max": 1730 },
      "longSilences": 1,
      "longSilenceSeconds": 10,
      "longestSilenceSeconds": 12.4,
      "interruptions": 2,
      "knowledgeTurns": 3,
      "modelErrors": 0,
      "rescues": 1
    },
    "endedAt": "2026-10-06T04:33:11.902Z"
  }
}
```

`quality` is how the call went in numbers (see [Call quality](#call-quality)); it
can be `null` when the call ended before its figures were ready. `forwardedTo`
appears only on a call your number forwarded to a phone, and is that phone's
number; it is left out of every other call.

It is a short record of how the call ended. It never carries the transcript, the
recording, the summary or the details collected: those are in
[`call.analysed`](#call-analysed) and Get Call. There is no `status` or
`analysedAt` field; `outcome` and `endedAt` are the ones to use.

**Order.** On one call `call.completed` is sent first, and the analysis waits up
to five seconds for it, so `call.analysed` normally follows. That is not a
guarantee: a delivery retried after a failure, or a restart in the middle of a
call, can swap them. Join the two on `callRef` and treat `call.analysed` as the
fuller record whichever arrives first.

### `call.analysed`

The call once it has been read: exactly the object [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) returns. `quality` can be `null` (see [Call quality](#call-quality)), `handedTo` is empty unless the call was [handed to another agent](#calls-handed-to-another-agent), `forwardedTo` is `null` unless the call was forwarded to a phone, and `insights` is `null` unless the agent's [Call insights](/agent/insights) is on.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_8f4d2a6c-3e9b-4c1f-b7a5-6d2e0f8c4a51",
  "event": "call.analysed",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:33:20.402Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "callRef": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "reference": "LSQ-42",
    "metadata": {
      "deal_id": "D-19",
      "owner": "Ravi"
    },
    "attempt": 1,
    "status": "completed",
    "direction": "outbound",
    "phone": "919876543210",
    "from": "918045678901",
    "agent": {
      "id": "ag_5c4a5f93-2b1e-4d7a-9f60-8e2d1c3b4a71",
      "name": "Skyline Sales"
    },
    "scheduledFor": null,
    "startedAt": "2026-10-06T04:30:02.118Z",
    "answeredAt": "2026-10-06T04:30:09.540Z",
    "endedAt": "2026-10-06T04:33:11.902Z",
    "seconds": 182,
    "hangup": "answered",
    "variables": {
      "lead_name": "Asha",
      "project": "Sky Towers"
    },
    "summary": "Asha is keen on a 2 BHK at Sky Towers with a budget around 80 lakh. She asked to visit the site on Saturday.",
    "fields": {
      "budget": 8000000,
      "interest": "Hot",
      "site_visit": true
    },
    "insights": {
      "outcome": "interested",
      "noReason": null,
      "objections": [{ "text": "Budget is tight", "kind": "price" }],
      "issues": [],
      "nextStep": {
        "kind": "visit",
        "at": "2026-10-31T04:30:00.000Z",
        "note": "Site visit on Saturday",
        "status": "open",
        "followedUpAt": null
      }
    },
    "transcript": [
      {
        "speaker": "agent",
        "text": "Hello Asha, I'm calling from Skyline Homes about your enquiry for Sky Towers.",
        "at": "2026-10-06T04:30:10.204Z"
      },
      {
        "speaker": "customer",
        "text": "Haan, boliye. I wanted a 2 BHK.",
        "at": "2026-10-06T04:30:16.880Z"
      }
    ],
    "recording": {
      "url": "https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1/recordings/3b7e1c90-5a2d-4e8f-9c61-0d4b7a2e8f13?expires=1762403402&sig=8c1f0e7a92b4d3c6e5f1a0b9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1",
      "expiresAt": "2026-11-05T04:30:02.118Z",
      "ready": true
    },
    "analysedAt": "2026-10-06T04:33:20.311Z",
    "retryScheduledFor": null,

      "firstTokenMs": { "median": 610, "p90": 940, "max": 1730 },
      "longSilences": 1,

        "agent": { "id": "ag_7b1d4e90-2c3a-4f6e-8d15-9a0b3c2e4f71", "name": "Site Visits" },
        "from": { "id": "ag_5c4a5f93-2b1e-4d7a-9f60-8e2d1c3b4a71", "name": "Skyline Sales" },
        "at": "2026-10-06T04:31:40.000Z"
      }
    ],
    "forwardedTo": null,
    "error": null
  }
}
```

### `campaign.finished`

Everyone on a broadcast (`kind: "whatsapp"`) or a calling campaign (`kind: "voice"`) has been reached or given up on. `skipped` is people who withdrew consent before their turn.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_2b6e0c8a-9f3d-4a7e-8c4b-5e1f3d7a9b63",
  "event": "campaign.finished",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T13:02:44.311Z",
  "data": {
    "campaignId": "cmp_7a1e9c3b-2d4f-4b8a-a6e0-1f5c8d2b9e47",
    "name": "Diwali site visits",
    "kind": "voice",
    "recipients": 120,
    "sent": 104,
    "failed": 9,
    "skipped": 7,
    "finishedAt": "2026-10-06T13:02:44.180Z"
  }
}
```

### `contact.opted_out`

During a call, somebody asked not to be called again and their number went on the do-not-call list. `callId` is the call's id; `source` is always `"call"`; `reason` is what the caller said, as recorded (up to 160 characters, in the language they spoke), or `null` when the agent did not record their words.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_5a3f7d1e-2c8b-4e6a-9d0f-7b4c1e5a3d75",
  "event": "contact.opted_out",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:32:40.640Z",
  "data": {
    "phone": "+919876543210",
    "callId": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "source": "call",
    "optedOutAt": "2026-10-06T04:32:40.511Z",
    "reason": "please don't call me again"
  }
}
```

### `call.problem`

Something went wrong while a call was live. `kind` is `no_answer_from_model`, `byok_failed`, `slow_reply` or `voice_failed`; `detail` says what happened in a sentence; `callId` is the id [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) takes. Sent at most once per kind per call.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_4d8b2f6a-1e3c-4a9d-b5f7-0c6e2a8d4b87",
  "event": "call.problem",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T04:31:02.715Z",
  "data": {
    "callId": "out_9f2c1a44-6b0e-4c1d-8a7f-2e5b3c9d1f60",
    "agentId": "ag_5c4a5f93-2b1e-4d7a-9f60-8e2d1c3b4a71",
    "kind": "slow_reply",
    "detail": "A reply took 6.2 seconds to start.",
    "at": "2026-10-06T04:31:02.702Z"
  }
}
```

## Workspace events

`contact.erased` and `byok.changed` are about your whole workspace rather than one agent. They go to
**every endpoint in the workspace that subscribed to them**, whichever agent you added it on, and
**once per address**: if three agents post to the same URL, that URL still gets one delivery. If you
are a developer, an endpoint that receives every customer's events (`includeCustomers`) gets them for
your customers too, with `workspaceId`. An endpoint subscribed to every event (`["*"]`) receives them
as well. Neither event carries personal details or any part of a key.

### `contact.erased`

A contact you deleted with [Delete Contact](/workspace/data-and-erasure) is gone completely, recordings
included. It is sent **once**: straight away when Delete Contact answered `204`, or — when it answered
`recordingsPending` because a recording could not be deleted at that moment — from the nightly retry,
once the last of those recordings is gone. A recording that was still being written when you deleted
the contact can take up to three nights to be confirmed gone. `contactId` is the id you deleted.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_7c2e9a41-5d3b-4f8e-a6c0-1b9d4e7f2a58",
  "event": "contact.erased",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-07T02:30:11.402Z",
  "data": {
    "contactId": "cust_2b7e4c19-8a3d-4f60-b1e5-9c0d6a3f7e24",
    "erasedAt": "2026-10-06T11:42:05.118Z"
  }
}
```

### `byok.changed`

Your [own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys) changed. `change` is one of:

| `change` | What happened |
| - | - |
| `key_added` | A key was added for a job that had none |
| `key_replaced` | A key was saved over the one you had for that job |
| `key_removed` | A key was removed |
| `key_failed_verification` | You tried to save a key and the provider refused it. Nothing was saved |
| `byok_enabled` | Your own keys were switched on |
| `byok_disabled` | Your own keys were switched off; calls and replies run on ours |
| `scope_changed` | Your own keys were set to cover different jobs |

`kind` (`stt`, `llm` or `tts`) and `provider` name the key for the four key changes, and are `null`
for the others. `byokEnabled` and `scope` say where your workspace stands **after** the change.
Choosing a different model for a key is not sent. Saved keys are not re-checked on a schedule: a model
key that stops working on a call shows up as [`call.problem`](#problems-on-a-live-call) (`byok_failed`).

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_1f6b3d8e-9a2c-4e75-b0d4-6c8a2e5f9b13",
  "event": "byok.changed",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-06T09:15:40.226Z",
  "data": {
    "change": "key_replaced",
    "kind": "tts",
    "provider": "cartesia",
    "byokEnabled": true,
    "scope": "voice"
  }
}
```

## Re-send what failed

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/redeliver
```

One delivery, now — the answer says whether it arrived:

```json theme={null}
{ "deliveryId": "whd_2b6f…" }
```

```json theme={null}
{ "delivered": true, "status": 200, "error": null, "attempts": 4 }
```

Or everything that has not succeeded since a time, at most 7 days back — queued
and sent within a minute:

```json theme={null}
{ "since": "2026-10-06T00:00:00Z" }
```

```json theme={null}
{ "queued": 12 }
```

The same body, event id and `sentAt` as the first attempt, with
`x-thinnest-attempt` one higher. The endpoint must be switched on. The console's
**Re-send failed** button on the endpoint does the same for the last 7 days. A
build key may do this.

## Test an endpoint

```http theme={null}
POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test
```

```json theme={null}
{ "delivered": true, "status": 200, "error": null }
```

Sends one sample `lead.captured` — marked `"test": true`, with obviously fake
details — the same way a real event goes: signed JSON, Slack's own format for
a Slack URL, or a ticket email for an email address. A failed test counts
towards the five failures that switch an endpoint off.

## Delivery history

```http theme={null}
GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "whd_2b6f…", "eventId": "evt_9d1c…", "event": "call.analysed",
      "status": 500, "delivered": false, "error": "Internal Server Error",
      "attempts": 2, "nextRetryAt": "2026-10-05T09:18:04Z",
      "at": "2026-10-05T09:12:03Z", "lastAttemptAt": "2026-10-05T09:13:04Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "whd_7c3e…", "eventId": null, "event": "test",
      "status": 200, "delivered": true, "error": null,
      "attempts": 1, "nextRetryAt": null,
      "at": "2026-10-05T08:58:41Z", "lastAttemptAt": "2026-10-05T08:58:41Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

One row per event, however many attempts it took, newest first — the last 7
days (or the last 50, whichever is more). The answer to "why did leads stop
reaching our CRM on Tuesday?". `status` and `error` are from the latest
attempt; `0` means we could not reach it. `nextRetryAt` is when the next
automatic attempt is due — null once it arrived or ran out of retries. The
payloads themselves are not returned: they carry your customers' details.


# Create Webhook
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/create-webhook

/api-reference/openapi.json post /webhooks
Adds an endpoint for one agent's events — or, from a developer workspace, with `includeCustomers: true`, one endpoint for every agent in every one of your customers, each delivery's `data` carrying the `workspaceId` it is about. The response carries `signingSecret` **once**: store it to verify `x-thinnest-signature` on every delivery, because it is never shown again. `url` is an `https://` address or an email address (a helpdesk that opens tickets by mail gets one email per event); addresses inside our own network are refused. A **build** key may do this.

# Delete Webhook
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/delete-webhook

/api-reference/openapi.json delete /webhooks/{id}
Removes the endpoint. Nothing more is sent to it, and its delivery history goes with it. A **build** key may do this.

# Get Webhook
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook

/api-reference/openapi.json get /webhooks/{id}
One endpoint, with its delivery state: how many deliveries in a row have failed, and the last status, error and time. Never the signing secret.

# List Webhook Deliveries
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhook-deliveries

/api-reference/openapi.json get /webhooks/{id}/deliveries
The endpoint's recent deliveries, newest first — one row per event, however many attempts it took; 7 days (or the last 50, whichever is more) are kept. `status` and `error` are from the latest attempt, `0` when your endpoint could not be reached. `attempts` counts them, and `nextRetryAt` says when the next automatic one is due (null once delivered or out of retries). Test sends are listed as `test` with no `eventId`. Payloads are not returned: they carry your customers' details. Returns at most 50 rows and has no cursor: `nextCursor` is always null. A delivery counts toward switching the endpoint off only when it used up all six attempts: five such events in a row switch it off, and since each takes about 8½ hours to give up, a dead endpoint can take up to about two days to be switched off.

# List Webhooks
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhooks

/api-reference/openapi.json get /webhooks
The workspace's webhook endpoints, newest first — those added by API and those added in the console alike — each with its delivery state. Filter to one agent's with `agent`.

# Redeliver Webhook Events
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/redeliver-webhook-events

/api-reference/openapi.json post /webhooks/{id}/redeliver
Sends events to this endpoint again — the same body, event id and `sentAt` they first had, with `x-thinnest-attempt` one higher. Either `{ "deliveryId": "whd_…" }` for one delivery, sent now (the answer says whether it arrived; if it fails it joins the retry schedule), or `{ "since": "<ISO time>" }` for every delivery that has not succeeded since then — at most 7 days back, when payloads are dropped — queued and sent within a minute (`202 { queued }`). The endpoint must be switched on. A **build** key may do this: it reaches only your own endpoint.

# Test Webhook
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/test-webhook

/api-reference/openapi.json post /webhooks/{id}/test
Sends one sample `lead.captured` event to the endpoint — its `data` marked `"test": true`, with obviously fake details — the same way a real event goes: signed JSON, Slack's own message format for a Slack URL, or a ticket email for an email address. It is recorded in the delivery history as `test`, and a failed test counts towards the five failures in a row that switch an endpoint off. The answer says whether it arrived; a failure to deliver is still a `200` here. A **build** key may do this.

# Update Webhook
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/webhooks/update-webhook

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /webhooks/{id}
Changes an endpoint's `url`, `events` or `enabled`; fields you leave out are kept. Switching an endpoint back on (`enabled: true`) forgives its past failures, so after an outage: fix the receiver, catch up from the API on what it missed, then `PATCH { "enabled": true }`. The agent an endpoint belongs to cannot be changed. A **build** key may do this.

# Get a Workflow
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workflows/get-a-workflow

/api-reference/openapi.json get /workflows/{workflowId}
One workflow: what starts it and its blocks, as PUBLISHED (the draft only for a workflow never published), and — when your system starts it — the address to send runs to. Any key.

# List Workflows
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workflows/list-workflows

/api-reference/openapi.json get /workflows
The workspace's workflows, newest first, with each one's id — what Start a Workflow Run takes — its status, the version new runs start on, and what starts it. Read-only: workflows are built and published in the console. Any key.

# Send a Workflow Event
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workflows/send-a-workflow-event

/api-reference/openapi.json post /workflows/events
Tells your workflows that something happened to a contact, such as a payment landing or a booking being made. Every run of that contact whose **Await** block waits for *Your system sends an event* with this name moves on through its **Arrived** path at the next check; only events sent after the run began waiting count. The contact is found by phone number. Needs a **full** key.

# Start a Workflow Run
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workflows/start-a-workflow-run

/api-reference/openapi.json post /workflows/{workflowId}/runs
Starts one contact through a workflow whose published **Start when** is *Your system asks*. A number this workspace has never seen gets a contact made for it, so a brand-new lead from your CRM can go straight in. `variables` are this run's own values: a blank written `{{contact.order}}` fills from `variables.order`. `started: false` is a `200`, not an error: the contact is already going through it, or the workflow's settings do not let them go through it again. Calls and messages the workflow sends are billed as usual. Needs a **full** key.

# Get Workspace
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workspace/get-workspace

/api-reference/openapi.json get /workspace
The workspace's id, name, console address (`slug`), time zone and when it was made. Plan and billing are not settings and are not here.

# Update Workspace
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/api-reference/workspace/update-workspace

/api-reference/openapi.json patch /workspace
Renames the workspace, changes its time zone, or sets how many days calls are kept (`callRetentionDays`) — any of them. The name appears in invitation emails, so it follows the rules for a person's name: 2 to 80 characters (a longer one is refused with a 400), no web or email address, no markup. Every date in the console is shown in the time zone. The `slug` never changes. Needs a **full** key.

# Calling rules by country (US TCPA, UK PECR, India TRAI)
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/channels/calling-rules

What ThinnestAI does for you when your agent calls people, and what the law in the US, the UK and India leaves to you.

When your agent calls or messages people, **you** are the caller in the eyes of
the law. ThinnestAI gives you tools that help you keep to the rules, but it does
not decide whether you may call someone, and it does not check for you. This
page sets out which part is which, country by country.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **This is not legal advice.** It is a short guide to rules that change, and
> that apply differently to marketing calls, service calls and calls a customer
> asked for. Check with a lawyer who knows your market before you run outbound
> calls, and read the regulator's own guidance linked below.

## What the platform does for you

* **A do-not-contact list.** Numbers on the list on the **Contacts** page under
  *Do not contact* are never reached by a campaign or an API call, on any
  channel. It is checked as each call is placed, so adding a number stops a
  campaign that is already running. See [Calling
  campaigns](/channels/voice-campaigns#who-gets-called).
* **"Don't call me again."** When a caller clearly asks not to be called again,
  your agent puts their number on that list itself, unless you switch this off
  for the agent. See ["Don't call me again"](/channels/voice#dont-call-me-again).
* **Opt-outs.** Anybody who has asked you to stop is left out of a campaign
  even when they are in the file you upload.
* **Calling hours you set.** A campaign calls only in the hours you give it,
  and an API call only in the `callingHours` you send. Hours are read on the
  **called person's clock**, worked out from their number: 9am on a London
  number means 9am in London. For a country with several time zones, such as
  the United States, a campaign keeps inside your hours at both ends of the
  country. See [When it calls, and when it
  stops](/channels/voice-campaigns#when-it-calls-and-when-it-stops).
* **Pacing.** A cap on calls per hour, and retries that keep to your hours.
* **Honest about being an AI.** If someone asks whether they are talking to an
  AI, a bot or a real person, the agent says it is an AI assistant, on every
  channel and whatever your instructions say. See [Behaviour](/agent/behaviour).

## What the platform does not do

> [!WARNING]
>
> * **There are no calling hours of our own.** A campaign with no hours set, or
>   an API call with no `callingHours`, may ring at any hour. Set hours that
>   keep to the law where the person you are calling lives.
> * **No register screening.** We do not check your lists against the US
>   National Do Not Call Registry, the UK's TPS or CTPS, India's DND register or
>   any other register.
> * **No consent check.** Ticking "these people agreed to be called" when you
>   upload a list is a claim you make and we record. We do not verify it.
> * **No automatic announcements on phone calls.** An agent does not say on its
>   own that the call is recorded or that it is an AI. If the law requires
>   either, put it in your agent's first words. (Website calls show *This call
>   is recorded* when recording is on, and an agent always answers truthfully
>   if a caller asks whether the call is recorded.)

## United States: TCPA

The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) and the Federal Communications
Commission's (FCC) rules decide most of what an outbound AI call needs.

| You are responsible for | What it means in practice |
| - | - |
| **Consent** | The FCC treats AI-generated voices as "artificial" voices under the TCPA. Calls using one generally need the called person's prior express consent, and marketing calls need prior express **written** consent. Keep the proof. |
| **Do Not Call** | Do not make telemarketing calls to numbers on the National Do Not Call Registry without a valid exception, and keep your own internal do-not-call list. |
| **Calling hours** | Telemarketing calls only between **8am and 9pm** in the called person's local time. Set your campaign hours to match. |
| **Identification and opt-out** | Say who is calling at the start of the call, and give people a way to opt out. |
| **State rules** | Several states have their own calling laws, some stricter than the TCPA on hours, consent or call frequency. |
| **Recording** | Some states, California among them, require every party's consent to record a call. |

Read: [FCC: Telemarketing and robocalls](https://www.fcc.gov/general/telemarketing-and-robocalls)
and the [National Do Not Call Registry](https://www.donotcall.gov/).

## United Kingdom: PECR

Marketing calls in the UK are governed by the Privacy and Electronic
Communications Regulations (PECR), enforced by the Information Commissioner's
Office (ICO), alongside UK GDPR for the personal data itself.

| You are responsible for | What it means in practice |
| - | - |
| **TPS and CTPS** | Do not make live marketing calls to numbers registered with the Telephone Preference Service (TPS) or the Corporate TPS, unless that person has told you they are happy to get your calls. |
| **Automated calls** | Automated marketing calls need the person's specific prior consent. Whether a given AI call counts as automated is a question to settle with your adviser before you call. |
| **Identification** | Say who is calling, show a number the person can call back, and give an address or freephone number if they ask. |
| **Opt-outs** | Stop calling anybody who asks you to. |
| **Calling hours** | PECR sets no fixed hours. The platform sets none either: choose hours your customers would think reasonable, and set them on the campaign. |
| **Recording** | Tell people a call is recorded and why, as UK GDPR's transparency rules expect. |

Read: [ICO: direct marketing and PECR](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/)
and the [Telephone Preference Service](https://www.tpsonline.org.uk/).

## India: TRAI

Commercial calls in India are governed by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of
India's (TRAI) rules on unsolicited commercial communication, alongside the
Digital Personal Data Protection Act for the personal data.

| You are responsible for | What it means in practice |
| - | - |
| **Registration** | Register as a sender or telemarketer where TRAI's rules require it, and place promotional calls from the number series assigned for them (140). |
| **DND preferences** | Do not make promotional calls to people who have blocked them on the National Customer Preference Register (DND), unless you hold their recorded consent. |
| **Calling hours** | Keep promotional calls to daytime hours, for example 9am to 9pm. Set the hours on the campaign: the platform does not. |
| **Consent and notice** | Hold consent for the purpose you are calling about, and give people the notice the data protection law requires. |
| **Complaints** | Complaints about unwanted calls go against the number that called. Repeated complaints can get a number disconnected. |

Read: [TRAI](https://www.trai.gov.in/), where the regulations on unsolicited
commercial communication and the DND register are published.

## The UAE and other countries

Every country has its own rules on telemarketing, consent, Do Not Call
registers and calling hours. The UAE, for example, has its own telemarketing
regulations and a Do Not Call Registry. For anywhere not covered above, the
hours you set on your campaign are the only hours the platform keeps to, so
check the local rules before you call.

## Where this is written down

Our [Terms of Service](https://thinnest.ai/legal/terms) (section 6) put consent,
Do Not Call screening, calling hours and disclosures on the business that
places the calls, and the [Acceptable Use
Policy](https://thinnest.ai/legal/acceptable-use) lists what may never be done.
If you resell ThinnestAI under your own brand, your clients' calls are yours to
answer for too.


# Instagram
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/channels/instagram

Your agent answers Instagram DMs and comments, and every conversation lands in your Inbox.

Connect an Instagram professional account and your agent answers its Direct
messages with the same knowledge and instructions it uses everywhere else. Every
conversation appears in the shared **Inbox**, where your team can read along and
reply.

You sign in with Meta's own login, using Facebook or Instagram. Nobody shares
a password, no Facebook Page is needed, and you can remove access at any time
from your Instagram or Meta business settings.

## Connect

**1. Open Connect Instagram**

In the sidebar, open **Instagram** and then **Connect Instagram**.

**2. Choose the agent that answers**

Pick the agent, then press **Connect with Instagram**.

**3. Sign in and choose your account**

Log in with Facebook or Instagram and choose the professional account to
connect. It must be a **Business** or **Creator** account.

**4. Send it a DM**

From another Instagram account, message yours. The agent replies within
seconds, and the conversation shows in the Inbox.

Each Instagram account is answered by one agent. To hand an account to a
different agent, change it on **Connect Instagram**. New conversations go to the
new agent, and open ones keep the agent they started with.

## What the agent handles

* **Text and links.** A long answer is split into several messages at a
  paragraph or sentence, because Instagram refuses a message over 1,000
  characters.
* **Photos customers send**, such as a reference image or a screenshot. They are
  kept with the conversation, so they are still there weeks later even though
  Instagram's own links expire.
* **Photos the agent sends.**
* Buttons and lists of choices are sent as plain text.

## Replying yourself

Open the conversation in the **Inbox** and reply. Your message goes out on
Instagram, and the agent stops answering that conversation while a person has
it.

You can also reply from the Instagram app on the business account. Your reply
shows in the Inbox as a message from your team, and the agent stops answering
that conversation, just as if you had replied from the Inbox.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Instagram lets a business reply for **24 hours** after the customer's last
> message, and a person up to **7 days**. After that, a reply is saved in the
> Inbox but not sent until the customer writes again. There are no templates on
> Instagram for reaching someone after the window closes.

## Ice breakers

Under **Instagram > Ice breakers**, set up to four questions people can tap when
they open a new chat with you, such as "What are your prices?" or "How do I
book?". They appear in Instagram as soon as you save, and the agent answers
whichever one a person taps.

## Comment automation

Under **Instagram > Comment automation**, add keyword rules for comments on your
posts. When a comment contains a keyword, the commenter gets a **private DM**,
and you can also post a **public reply** under the comment.

* Leave the private DM empty and your agent writes the answer itself.
* Rules are checked top to bottom, and the first match wins.
* Keywords match whole words, ignoring capitals and accents, so "price" matches
  "What's the PRICE?" but not "priceless".
* **Every other comment** decides what happens to comments no rule matches: the
  agent answers them by DM, or they are left alone.

Instagram allows **one** private DM per comment, within 7 days of it. When the
commenter replies to that DM, the conversation continues in the Inbox like any
other.

## IG Dashboard

**Instagram > IG Dashboard** shows the last 30 days for all your accounts or one
of them:

* DMs received, and from how many people
* the agent's replies
* your team's replies
* comments answered
* conversations a person has taken over
* replies Instagram refused

## Opting out

A customer who writes STOP is recorded as opted out, exactly as on WhatsApp,
and the agent stops replying to them.

## What it does not do

> [!WARNING]
>
> **No broadcasts or campaigns on Instagram.** Instagram does not allow a
> business to message people who have not written first, so Broadcasts,
> Sequences and Send Message work on WhatsApp only.
>
> **Instagram does not join a customer's identity.** Instagram gives a name or
> handle, never a phone number, so an Instagram conversation is not merged with
> the same person's WhatsApp or phone history.
>
> **Voice notes, videos and shared posts** are noted in the conversation, but
> the agent does not watch or listen to them.


# Channels overview
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/channels/overview

Where customers talk to your agent, and what each channel can carry.

A channel is a place a customer **talks to you**. There are five.

| Channel | Inbound | Agent replies | Broadcasts | Recognises signed-in customers |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| [Website widget](/channels/website) | Yes | Yes | Never — a campaign reaches somebody who is not there | Yes, [with signing](/install/signed-in-customers) |
| [WhatsApp](/channels/whatsapp) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, by phone number |
| [Telegram](/channels/telegram) | Yes | Yes | Not built | No |
| [Instagram](/channels/instagram) | Yes, DMs and comments | Yes | No: Instagram does not allow messaging people who have not written first | No |
| [Voice](/channels/voice) | Yes, by phone | Yes, out loud | No — a call is not a broadcast | Yes, by phone number |

An agent has at most one channel of each kind.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Shopify, WordPress and PrestaShop are not channels.** They are doors onto
> the website widget — ways to get it onto your pages without editing theme
> code. See [Put it on your site](/install/shopify).

## One agent across all of them

The same knowledge, the same instructions, the same tools. You do not configure
a separate WhatsApp bot.

Each channel renders what it can. A card that appears as a rich card in the
website widget arrives as a native WhatsApp card, and where a channel cannot
render something it degrades to text rather than to a blank message.

## One customer across all of them

A person who asks on your website and then messages on WhatsApp is one contact
with one history — provided the two can be joined on evidence they did not
supply themselves. [How that works](/concepts#how-two-channels-become-one-person).

## What is not built

> [!WARNING]
>
> * **Messenger.** Not available. [Instagram](/channels/instagram) is.
> * **Campaigns on Instagram.** Instagram does not allow messaging people outside
>   the 24-hour window, so there is no campaign lane there.
> * **Multi-channel campaigns.** The picker is real and only WhatsApp can send.
> * **WhatsApp calling.** Not yet. [Voice](/channels/voice) answers on a phone
>   number and in the website widget today.


# Phone numbers
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/channels/phone-numbers

Get a number your customers ring, or point one you already own at your agent.

Your agent answers on a phone number. You can get one from us — searched,
bought and ready on the same screen — or use a number you already own.

Numbers belong to the **workspace**, not to one agent. They live on the **Phone
Numbers** page in the main sidebar, which lists every number you hold, where it
came from, and two things for each: the **Inbound** agent, which answers it, and
the **Outbound** agent, which calls out on it. They can be the same agent or
different ones, or either can be empty — see [Inbound and
outbound](#inbound-and-outbound-are-separate). A **Dial-out ready** column says
whether the number can place calls as well as answer them. You can search the
list and move any number to another agent.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You do not need a number to try voice. The website call button works without
> one, on any plan, and it is the same agent with the same voice. A number is
> what lets somebody ring you from a phone — and if you already own one, you can
> point it at your agent on any plan, free included.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Which numbers you can buy from us depends on where your workspace is
> billed.** A workspace billed in India buys Indian numbers; a workspace billed
> anywhere else buys **United States** local numbers (see [United States
> numbers](#united-states-numbers)). Either can bring a number it already owns
> from any country. See [Where you are billed](/workspace/regions).

## Country codes

Every phone number carries its country code — the `+44`, `+1`, `+971` or `+91`
at the front.

* **In the console**, wherever you type or upload numbers (importing a number,
  adding or importing contacts, the do-not-contact list, a calling campaign's
  list, sending a WhatsApp message, a test call), a country list with flags sits
  beside the box. It starts on your workspace's country and you can change it.
  A number you type without a code takes the country picked there; a number
  that already starts with `+` or `00` keeps its own.
* **Through the API**, send every number with its country code, like
  `+44 7700 900123` or `+91 98765 43210`. Spaces and dashes are fine, and full
  international digits without the `+` (`447700900123`) work too. A number
  without its country code is **refused** with a message saying how to write
  it; nothing is assumed to be Indian or anywhere else.

## Getting a number from us

**1. Open Phone Numbers**

In the main sidebar choose **Phone Numbers**, then **Buy / Import number**.

**2. Search**

Pick a city (India) or a state (United States) if you want a local code,
or type an area code. You will see the numbers available now, each with
what it costs a month.

**3. Take one**

Choose a number. Before anything is charged you get a summary — the number,
what it costs a month, what leaves your wallet today and what is left in it —
and the number is yours the moment you confirm. There is nothing to configure
with a phone company and no settings to copy anywhere.

**4. Say which agent answers it**

A new number is not pointed anywhere yet. On the **Phone Numbers** page,
choose the agent under **Inbound**. That agent starts answering immediately.

**5. Ring it**

Call the number. You should hear your greeting, then the agent.

### What it costs

Each number has a monthly price, shown before you take it, and it repeats every
month until you give the number up. The price is the same on every plan.

**Buying a number needs a paid plan**, because we rent it for you every month.
Pay as you go has no monthly fee of its own and can hold numbers. Through the API,
send an `Idempotency-Key` on [Rent Phone
Number](/api-reference/phone-numbers/rent-phone-number): a retry returns the first
answer instead of renting a second number.

**Pointing a number you already own at your agent works on every plan,
including the free one.** It costs us nothing to answer it — you are already
paying your own provider for the number — and a phone call is usually the thing
you want to hear before you decide to pay for anything. Free-plan calls come out
of the same trial minutes as calls from your website.

That covers calls in **both directions**. On the free plan your agent can answer
a number you brought and, once you have added that account's credentials, ring
people from it — your own provider bills you for the line either way. Buying a
number from us is the part that needs a paid plan.

### United States numbers

A workspace billed outside India buys **United States local numbers**: ordinary
numbers with a US area code, which your customers ring like any other. Toll-free
numbers are not offered yet; if you need one, tell us.

* **Search by state or area code.** Pick a state from the list, or type a
  three-digit area code such as `415`. A leading `1` is ignored, so `1415`
  finds the same numbers.
* **Nothing to verify.** No business documents are needed. The number is yours
  the moment you confirm.
* **They call the United States and Canada only.** A call from one of these
  numbers can go to any US or Canadian number (`+1`), including US toll-free
  numbers. It cannot go anywhere else, and that includes the parts of the `+1`
  code outside the US and Canada: Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, Guam and
  the other US territories, and the Caribbean countries that dial `+1`
  (Jamaica, the Dominican Republic, the Bahamas and the rest).

What happens when a call would go further:

| What | What happens |
| - | - |
| A campaign, a test call or the call API rings a number outside the US and Canada | That call is not placed. In a campaign only that person fails, with "We cannot call that country from your calling number", and the rest go ahead |
| Your agent tries to put a caller through to a person outside the US and Canada | The transfer is not made and the caller stays with your agent |
| You set a forward to a number outside the US and Canada | The forward is not saved: "US numbers can call US and Canada numbers only." |

The Buy list says this too, under the numbers. A number you **bring** from your
own carrier account is not limited this way: your carrier decides where it can
call.

### India needs your business verified first

An Indian number is only issued to a registered business, and the check is in
**your** name rather than ours. It has its own tab — **KYC**, beside Imported on
the Phone Numbers page — because it takes a little time to clear and it is worth
being able to come back and see where it got to.

This is not our rule and we cannot shortcut it. Numbers in most other countries
need nothing beyond choosing one.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is not the same as [business verification for
> WhatsApp](/meta/verification), which Meta runs and which unlocks a different
> set of things. Passing one does nothing for the other, and you may well need
> both.

#### What it asks for

Your registered business name, and **one** document. Which one depends on a
single question:

| Registered for GST? | The document to send |
| - | - |
