> Rejected as low quality, particularly where it makes the sender look
> fraudulent.

> [accordion] Content the language does not match
>
> A template declared `en` whose body is Hindi. Declare the language you
> actually wrote.

## Choosing the right category

| Category | For | Charged | Reaches an opted-out contact | Needs verification |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| **Marketing** | Offers, announcements, re-engagement, anything promotional | Yes | **No** | No |
| **Utility** | Order confirmations, delivery updates, receipts, appointment reminders — tied to a specific transaction the customer initiated | Yes | Yes, and must | No |
| **Authentication** | One-time passwords only | Yes | Yes | **Yes** |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The test for utility is "did the customer do something that makes this
> message expected?"** An order confirmation follows an order. A "we miss you"
> message follows nothing, and is marketing however you label it.

## Authentication templates are special

Meta writes and localises the wording for one-time passwords itself. The editor
copies Meta's text exactly rather than letting you write your own — rewording it
gets the template rejected.

Authentication templates are also gated behind [business
verification](/meta/verification).

## Limits on templates themselves

| | Limit | Whose |
| - | - | - |
| Template name | 512 characters, lowercase letters, numbers and underscores | Meta |
| Templates created per hour | 100 per WhatsApp account | Meta |
| Review time | Minutes, up to 24–48 hours for human review | Meta |

## Editing an approved template

Editing sends it back through review. The previous version keeps working until
the new one is decided, so an edit does not take a working template offline —
but a rejected edit means you are still on the old wording.

> [!TIP]
>
> For anything you send often, treat an approved template as immutable and
> create `..._v2` instead. That way a rejected change never blocks a working
> message, and you can compare how the two perform.

## After approval, it can still be taken away

Approval is not permanent. Meta keeps scoring how customers react, and a
template that gets blocked or reported can be paused and eventually disabled.
See [Quality and limits](/meta/quality-and-limits).


# Business verification
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/meta/verification

What it unlocks, what it costs you in time, and what stays locked without it.

Meta verifies that your business is a real, registered entity. Several things
you will want are gated behind it, and the wait is measured in days rather than
minutes — so start it early.

## What it unlocks

| | Without verification | With |
| - | - | - |
| Messaging limit | 250 unique customers / 24h | **2,000**, then automatic increases |
| One-time password templates | **Blocked** | Available |
| Publishing a form | **Blocked** — it builds and previews, but reaches nobody | Available |
| Display name on your number | Limited | Your verified business name |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Forms are the one that surprises people.** You can build a form, store it and
> preview it perfectly. Meta will not *publish* a flow for an unverified
> business, and an unpublished form reaches no customer — so the feature looks
> finished and does nothing.

## What Meta asks for

Broadly: a legal business name that matches official documents, a business
address, a phone number or website that can be checked, and a document proving
the entity exists — in India typically a GST certificate, Certificate of
Incorporation, or a utility bill in the business name.

The single most common cause of rejection is a **mismatch**: the name on your
Meta business portfolio differing, even slightly, from the name on the document.
Match them exactly, including the `Pvt Ltd` or `LLP` suffix.

## How long

Days, occasionally longer. Meta may ask for more documents, which restarts the
clock.

> [!TIP]
>
> Start verification on day one, before you need any of what it unlocks. It runs
> in the background while you build everything else, and nothing about it gets
> faster by waiting.

## Connecting your number

**Connect WhatsApp**, in the sidebar, is self-serve — it opens Meta's own signup,
you sign in with your own Facebook account, and it never touches us. See
[Connecting](/channels/whatsapp#connecting) for the two ways in and which
number to use.

## While you wait

None of this blocks the parts of the product that matter most:

> [card] [Telegram, in two minutes](/channels/telegram)
>
> No verification, no approvals, no templates. A real external channel to test
> against today.

> [card] [The website widget](/channels/website)
>
> Nothing here involves Meta at all.

Get the agent answering well on those first. A verified WhatsApp number attached
to an agent that cannot answer your customers' questions is the wrong order to
do this in.


# Windows and what gets charged
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/meta/windows-and-pricing

The 24-hour window, the 72-hour free entry point, and why answering costs far less than starting.

WhatsApp charges **per message**. Every template you send is its own charge, at
a rate that depends on the recipient's country and the kind of message.

The 24-hour window is a separate thing, and the two are easy to confuse: the
window decides **what you are allowed to send**, not how a charge is counted.

## The 24-hour customer service window

When a customer messages you, a 24-hour window opens.

**Inside it**, the agent replies freely, in its own words, as many times as the
conversation needs. Cards, buttons, images — anything.

**Outside it**, nothing but an [approved template](/meta/template-review)
reaches that customer. Not a short message, not a follow-up question. Nothing.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Every customer message **resets** the window to a fresh 24 hours. A
> conversation that goes back and forth over three days never leaves the window.

## What gets charged

| Category | When you use it | Cost |
| - | - | - |
| **Marketing** | Offers, launches, re-engagement | The most expensive by a wide margin |
| **Utility** | Order updates, reminders, receipts | Far cheaper than marketing — and **free inside an open window**, until 1 October 2026 |
| **Authentication** | One-time passcodes | Priced separately per country, in or out of the window |
| **Service** | The agent's own replies, inside the window | Free until 1 October 2026 — see below |

Messages your customers send you are never charged.

> [!TIP]
>
> **An open window makes two things free, not one.** Until 1 October 2026 it
> covers the agent's own replies *and* any utility template you send while the
> window is open. So an order update sent to somebody who is mid-conversation
> with you costs nothing, where the same template sent a day later is charged.
>
> Authentication is the exception: a one-time passcode is charged whether or not
> a window is open.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This is why answering is cheap and starting is expensive.** An agent handling
> forty inbound questions costs a fraction of forty marketing sends. Support
> automation pays for itself long before outbound does.

Rates vary by country and change from time to time — India differs from the US
by a large multiple. Your [usage page](/workspace/usage) itemises what you were
actually charged, by category and country.

## Who bills you, and for what

Two things are being paid for and they arrive from different places, which is the
single most common question about a WhatsApp bill.

**Meta charges for the message.** The rates above are Meta's, they vary by
country, and they are the bulk of the cost.

**ThinnestAI charges 10% of Meta's rate**, per message — the platform fee. It
pays for the console, the shared inbox, templates, forms, delivery reporting and
keeping your conversations.

Which of us Meta invoices depends on whose WhatsApp Business Account the message
went out on.

| | Meta's fee | Our 10% |
| - | - | - |
| **Your own WhatsApp Business Account** | Meta bills the payment method on your Meta account, directly | From your ThinnestAI balance |
| **A number we provide** | Meta bills us | From your ThinnestAI balance, included in the per-message price |

Either way our share is the same 10% of the same rate. On your own account you
will see two charges for one message — Meta's on your Meta bill, ours on your
usage page — and that is expected rather than a duplicate.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Money added in one place does not cover the other.** A balance topped up here
> cannot pay Meta's message fees, and a payment method added on Meta does not pay
> our platform fee. If sending stops, check which of the two is empty: a Meta
> payment problem stops messages being delivered at all and
> [says so on your WhatsApp page](/channels/whatsapp), where an empty balance
> here stops campaigns before they start.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Your agent's own replies are charged separately from messages — what the model
> costs us, plus the same 10% — and are itemised on your
> [usage page](/workspace/usage). Calls are priced per minute. Neither has
> anything to do with Meta's message rates.

## In-window messages become chargeable on 1 October 2026

> [!WARNING]
>
> **This one is worth planning for.** Two things that are free today stop being
> free on **1 October 2026**:
>
> * **The agent's own free-form replies** inside the 24-hour window, which is
>   most of what it sends.
> * **Utility templates** sent while a window is open.
>
> Both are then charged at the ordinary utility rate for that country. A
> WhatsApp conversation gets more expensive on that date, and if you run
> pay-as-you-go your balance will drain faster than it does now.

You will not have to remember this. A notice appears on your
[usage page](/workspace/usage) in the run-up, and you get a notification before
the date — so the first you hear of it is not a smaller balance than you
expected.

Nothing about how the agent works changes, and nothing you have built needs
rebuilding. What changes is the arithmetic: today a long back-and-forth costs
almost nothing, and after that date each of the agent's replies carries a
charge.

## The free entry point

> [card] 72 hours free
>
> When a customer arrives from a **click-to-WhatsApp ad** or a Facebook page
> call-to-action, and you reply within 24 hours, nothing in that conversation is
> charged — **for 72 hours**. Marketing templates included.

Three times the normal window, at no cost, and it covers the most expensive
category on the rate card. If you run WhatsApp ads at all, this changes the
economics of answering quickly: a reply inside 24 hours turns a paid
conversation into a free one.

Free entry point conversations show in your usage.

## What this means in practice

> [accordion] Answer fast, especially from ads
>
> A reply within 24 hours of a click-to-WhatsApp ad buys 72 free hours. A reply
> on day two buys nothing.

> [accordion] Batch your outbound
>
> Every template is charged. Two separate utility messages an hour apart cost
> twice what one message covering both would.

> [accordion] Send the utility template while the window is open
>
> Until October 2026 an order update, a reminder or a receipt costs nothing if
> the customer is still inside their 24-hour window, and the ordinary rate the
> moment it closes. The same message, the same template, two different prices
> — so timing it with the conversation is worth real money on any volume.

> [accordion] Do not reach for a template when free-form will do
>
> Inside the window the agent can simply answer, in its own words, for nothing.
> Check the inbox before sending a template to somebody you are already talking
> to.

> [accordion] Prefer utility where it is honestly utility
>
> Far cheaper than marketing, and it reaches customers who opted out of
> marketing. Only where it genuinely is utility — see
> [the categories](/meta/template-review#choosing-the-right-category).

## What you cannot do, at any price

> [!WARNING]
>
> * **Send free-form text outside the window.** No amount of paying unlocks this.
> * **Send marketing to somebody who opted out.** Refused, and correctly.
> * **Open a window by sending yourself a message.** The window is opened by the
>   customer, or by a template you pay for.


# Partner referrals
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/partners/referrals

Refer a business to ThinnestAI, and earn a share of what they spend on voice and on subscriptions.

If you introduce a business to ThinnestAI, you earn a share of what that
business spends — for as long as the agreement says, paid monthly, visible to
you in your own panel.

This page describes the **referral** track: we bill your client, they are a
ThinnestAI customer, and you take commission. Reselling under your own brand is
a separate arrangement — talk to us.

## Becoming a partner

Signed in? Click **Become a Partner** in the sidebar. Otherwise apply at
**`/partner/apply`** — company, website, the markets you sell into, and how you
would sell this.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Every application is read by a person.** There is no automatic approval: being
> a partner means a referral code, agreed commission rates and a claim on future
> revenue, so somebody here decides. We come back to you by email.

If we cannot take one forward we say why, and you are welcome to apply again if
that changes.

## Getting set up

Once approved, you have two things:

* **A referral link**, like `https://app.thinnest.ai/?ref=yourcode`
* **A partner code**, the `yourcode` part, for anyone you introduce by phone

Then sign in at **`/partner`** to see everything below.

## How a referral is counted

**1. Someone opens your link**

We remember your code in their browser for **30 days**. If they click two
partners' links, the **first** one counts — whoever introduced them.

**2. They sign up**

The code is applied to their new workspace. There is also a **Partner code**
box on the signup form, so someone you introduced over a call can type
`yourcode` and still be counted.

**3. It is fixed from then on**

A workspace belongs to the partner who introduced it and cannot be moved to
another one later.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The 30-day window starts at the **first** click, not the most recent one. If
> someone you introduced signs up 31 days later without using the link again, ask
> them to enter your code on the signup form instead.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Use the exact link from your panel.** A link you build yourself pointing at our
> marketing site will not carry your code — only the app link does. If you would
> rather send someone to the marketing site first, give them your **partner code**
> as well and ask them to enter it at signup.

## Demo workspaces

You can create up to **three demo workspaces** from your panel — somewhere to
show the product to a prospect without touching a client's account.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **A demo is funded by you, not by us.** It is a real workspace with a real
> balance that starts at zero. Top it up before you try a call or a message, or
> the demo will not connect. Calls and messages cost the usual rates.

Because the spending is your own, a demo workspace **earns you no commission**,
and it is not counted among your referred accounts or in your conversion rate.

## What earns commission

> [card] Voice minutes
>
> A share of what a referred workspace is charged for calls.

> [card] Subscriptions
>
> A share of the monthly or yearly Pro or Scale fee.

**Nothing else earns commission.** In particular:

| | |
| - | - |
| WhatsApp messages | **No.** These are charged at Meta's own rates and passed straight through, so there is no margin to share. |
| Wallet top-up fees | No. |
| Phone number rental | No. |
| Website and chat replies | No. |

Your exact rates are on your panel, including any that change after a set number
of months.

## When the rate changes

Commission rates can step down over the life of an account — for example a
higher rate for the first year and a lower one after.

**Those months are counted from the day the workspace signs up**, not from their
first invoice. Your panel shows the referral date for every account so you can
work out where each one sits.

A rate that is renegotiated applies to what you earn **from then on**. Commission
already earned is never recalculated.

## Your panel

Sign in at `/partner`. It shows:

* **How many people opened your link** in the last 90 days, and how many of them
  signed up — so you can tell a traffic problem from a pitch problem
* **Earned, all time** and **this month**
* **Accounts referred**, with each one's plan, referral date and what it has earned
* **Every earning line** — the call or charge, what the client was charged, your
  rate, and your share
* **Payouts**, with period, status and reference

Every figure comes from the same ledger, so the summary, the per-account column
and the lines always agree.

## Getting paid

* Commission is calculated on money we have **actually collected**, after tax and
  payment fees.
* Payouts are raised **monthly, in arrears**, for the previous period.
* If a client is refunded or a payment is reversed, the matching commission is
  reversed — it appears as a **negative line**, so your total always matches what
  a payout will actually contain.
* Small balances roll forward rather than being paid — a transfer costs the same
  whatever it carries. Ask us what your minimum payout is.

### Why the amount paid differs from the amount earned

Your payout row shows four figures, and the difference between the first and the
last is not a deduction we keep:

| | |
| - | - |
| **Earned** | Commission for the period, from the ledger |
| **GST** | Added, if you are GST-registered — this is what you invoice us |
| **TDS** | Withheld under **section 194H** and deposited against your PAN |
| **Paid to you** | Earned + GST − TDS |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **TDS is your money, not ours.** It is deposited with the government against your
> PAN and you claim it on your return. We issue the certificate quarterly.

> [accordion] When does TDS start being deducted?
>
> Once your commission for the financial year (1 April to 31 March) passes
> **₹20,000 in total**. It is an annual threshold, not a per-payout one — so
> the payout that takes you over it also covers the earlier ones that were
> under it. That payout will carry more TDS than you expect, and the ones
> after it will be back to normal.
>
> If that catch-up is more than the payout itself — a small period that
> happens to cross the line — we withhold the whole payout and deduct the rest
> from your next one. A payout never goes below zero, and across the year the
> total withheld is the same.

> [accordion] Why is 20% being deducted instead of 2%?
>
> Because we do not have your **PAN** on file. Section 206AA requires 20%
> without one. Send it to us and it drops to 2% on your next payout — we
> cannot reverse deductions already made and deposited, so do it early.

> [accordion] Do I add GST to my commission?
>
> Only if you are GST-registered. If you are, give us your GSTIN and your
> payouts will include 18% on top of your commission, which you account for in
> your own return. TDS is calculated on the commission only, never on the GST.

> [accordion] I am outside India
>
> Payouts to non-residents fall under a different regime (section 195) that
> depends on your country's tax treaty with India. We handle those
> individually rather than automatically — talk to us before your first payout.

## Things worth knowing

> [accordion] A client of mine signed up but nothing is showing
>
> Check the referral date on your panel. A workspace only appears once it has
> signed up — not when someone opens your link. If they signed up without the
> link and without typing your code, get in touch with the workspace name and
> we can look into it.

> [accordion] An account is listed but has earned nothing
>
> Commission is earned on voice minutes and Pro and Scale subscriptions. A workspace on
> the free plan, or one using only WhatsApp and website chat, will show as
> referred and earn nothing. That is expected.

> [accordion] My account says suspended
>
> New signups stop being attributed to you and no further commission accrues.
> **Everything you have already earned is unaffected** and is paid on the
> normal schedule. Get in touch to sort it out.

> [accordion] Can I set my own prices?
>
> Not on the referral track — your client buys from us at our published prices
> and you earn a share. To set your own prices and bill your own clients under
> your own brand, use [White label](/white-label/overview), which comes with
> the Scale plan.


# Quickstart
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/quickstart

An agent answering on your website, from your own pages, in about ten minutes.

This gets you to a working agent on your own site. WhatsApp and Telegram come
after, and neither is required to start.

**1. Create an agent**

In the console, create a workspace and then an agent inside it. The agent's
name is what customers see in the widget header, so use the name you would
want a customer to read.

**2. Give it something to answer from**

Open **Knowledge** and add your material. The fastest start is a site crawl:
paste your homepage, choose a depth of 1 to 3 levels, and pick the pages you
actually want indexed before anything is ingested.

```
https://example.com
```

A crawl only follows links. If you have unlinked pages — a pricing page
reachable only from an email, say — add your `sitemap.xml` instead, which
reaches them.

> [!TIP]
>
> Add fewer, better pages first. Ten pages that answer real questions beat
> four hundred that mostly repeat your navigation.

**3. Tell it how to behave**

On **Settings**, write a business description — the facts the agent falls
back on when a search finds nothing — and your instructions for tone.

Set the reply language, or leave it on **match the customer** so it answers
in whatever language the customer wrote in.

**4. Try it in the Playground**

Ask it the three questions your customers actually ask. This is where you
tune instructions against a live reply rather than guessing.

Ask it something your material does **not** cover, too. It should say it
does not know. If it invents an answer instead, your business description is
doing too much work.

**5. Put it on your site**

Open **Channels** and copy your public key.

```html theme={null}
<script
  src="https://thinnest.ai/widget.js"
  data-key="pk_your_public_key"
  async
></script>
```

Paste it before the closing `</body>` tag on every page you want the agent
on. On Shopify, WordPress or PrestaShop, use the plugin instead — no code,
and it can recognise signed-in customers.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The public key identifies which agent answers. It authorises nothing and
> is meant to be visible in your page source.

**6. Watch the first real conversation**

**Inbox** shows every thread as it happens, and **Contacts** shows the
people behind them. When a conversation needs a person, anyone on your team
can take it over and the agent steps out of the way.

## Next

> [card] [Recognise signed-in customers](/install/signed-in-customers)
>
> Four lines on your server, and a logged-in customer stops being a stranger.

> [card] [Add WhatsApp](/channels/whatsapp)
>
> The same agent, answering on WhatsApp.

> [card] [Let it do things](/agent/actions)
>
> Look up an order, call your API, hand off to your helpdesk.

> [card] [Send a broadcast](/whatsapp/broadcasts)
>
> An approved template to people who opted in.


# Early October 2026
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/whats-new/early-october

What changed in ThinnestAI from October 1 to 5, 2026.

These are earlier changes. The newest are on [What's New](/whats-new), and the
weeks before this are on [Late September](/whats-new/late-september).

**Oct 5, 2026**

The MCP server, Telnyx numbers, WhatsApp carousels

**New**

* **Run your workspace from Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code.** ThinnestAI is now an
  MCP server: an AI assistant can work with your agents, actions, contacts, calls
  and analytics. Anything that would reach a customer waits for your approval, and
  a test chat contacts nobody. There is a new **MCP** tab in these docs.
  [MCP overview](/mcp/overview) and [Connect](/mcp/connect)
* **Choose what each API key can do.** Full access, Build or Read-only, and the
  same level applies to the MCP server. [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication)
* **Run the inbox and campaigns from the API or an assistant.** Resolve,
  hand back, take over and assign conversations, pause or cancel a campaign, see
  WhatsApp cost by category, send a test webhook and read its delivery history.
  [MCP tools](/mcp/tools)
* **See what an assistant did.** A list of the latest changes an AI assistant
  made in your workspace, with reads and test chats left out.
  [MCP tools](/mcp/tools)
* **Import Telnyx numbers.** Bring a number you already own on Telnyx, and your
  agent can answer it, detect voicemail and transfer calls.
  [Numbers from Telnyx](/channels/phone-numbers#numbers-from-telnyx)
* **Finish setting up WhatsApp.** A checklist on Connect WhatsApp shows what is
  left, and the payment step turns red if Meta blocks the account.
  [Finish setting up](/channels/whatsapp#finish-setting-up)

**Improved**

* **WhatsApp carousels are easier to get approved.** End the message with STOP,
  put buttons on the cards, and keep each card to 160 characters. The form checks
  all of it as you type. [Carousels](/whatsapp/templates#carousels)
* **A transfer on a line you brought no longer costs you our per-minute charge.**
  [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers)
* **Erasing a contact also deletes recordings of their calls** on numbers you
  brought. [Data and erasure](/workspace/data-and-erasure)

**Oct 4, 2026**

Several phone companies for one agent, quiet calls end

**New**

* **One agent can call out from numbers with different phone companies.** Each
  call dials, hangs up and transfers through its own number's provider.
  [Spare numbers for calling out](/channels/phone-numbers#spare-numbers-for-calling-out)
* **Test calls from the Playground can ring any country,** and the card is laid
  out as **Call from** and **Call to**. [Voice](/channels/voice)

**Improved**

* **A call where nobody speaks for five minutes is ended,** instead of holding
  the line open. An agent with no "end after" set now hangs up when its last
  "are you still there?" goes unanswered.
  [Ending the call](/channels/voice#ending-the-call)
* **Connecting your own WhatsApp account tells you that Meta bills your card,**
  not the balance here, before the first send.
  [Add a payment method in Meta](/whatsapp/payment-method)

**Oct 3, 2026**

Twilio numbers, separate inbound and outbound, better inbox search

**New**

* **Import Twilio numbers.** Connect your Twilio account and we set the number
  up there for you. Importing replaces what the number was set to before, so a
  number that already runs a menu or a forwarding rule loses it, and the page
  tells you before you do it.
  [Using a number you already own](/channels/phone-numbers#using-a-number-you-already-own)
* **Inbound and outbound are chosen separately for each number.** They can be
  different agents, and either can be empty. An agent that only calls out needs
  no number of its own.
  [Inbound and outbound are separate](/channels/phone-numbers#inbound-and-outbound-are-separate)
* **Export who a broadcast reached.** Download every recipient's status as a CSV.
  [Broadcasts](/whatsapp/broadcasts)
* **See who WhatsApp's marketing limit applies to.** Contacts and the Inbox show
  **Marketing paused until** for anyone WhatsApp is holding marketing messages
  for. [Not delivered](/whatsapp/not-delivered)

**Improved**

* **Inbox search finds every conversation,** not only the ones already loaded,
  and looks inside every message. Filters also look through all conversations.
  [Finding a conversation](/workspace/inbox#finding-a-conversation)
* **Carousel link buttons send,** and button labels can be up to 25 characters.
  [Buttons](/whatsapp/templates#buttons)

**Fixed**

* **Calls out from an imported number on another phone company now connect.**
  [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers)

**Oct 2, 2026**

WhatsApp Dashboard, blue tick, Marketing Messages

**New**

* **A WhatsApp Dashboard** with a date range and campaign-style tiles, and
  account cards on Connect WhatsApp.
  [The WhatsApp Dashboard](/channels/whatsapp#the-whatsapp-dashboard)
* **See your blue tick status.** Connect WhatsApp shows whether each number is
  eligible, with Meta's five checks.
  [The blue tick](/channels/whatsapp#the-blue-tick)
* **Set up Marketing Messages, two-step verification and display-name changes
  from the platform.** [Marketing Messages API](/channels/whatsapp#marketing-messages-api)
* **Filter Contacts by what became of their last message,** and export the
  filtered list to CSV. [Contacts](/agent/leads)

**Improved**

* **The daily limit is explained.** WhatsApp's limit counts different people you
  start conversations with in a rolling 24 hours, across the whole business. The
  Calls window states the real figure.
  [Quality and limits](/meta/quality-and-limits)
* **"Connect Your CRM" is now "Connect External Agent/CRM",** so the name says
  what it does. [External agents](/whatsapp/external-agents)

**Oct 1, 2026**

WhatsApp calls, one-time codes, delivery reasons

**New**

* **Customers can call you from WhatsApp and your agent answers.** One switch on
  Connect WhatsApp controls it. [WhatsApp calling](/whatsapp/calls)
* **Save and submit a one-time-code template in one step,** and open a window
  with the code to paste into your website in cURL, Node.js, Python or PHP.
  [One-time codes](/whatsapp/one-time-codes)

**Changed**

* **Your agent's replies inside the 24-hour window are charged from October 1,**
  and so are utility templates sent while a window is open, at the utility rate
  for the country. Messages your customers send you stay free.
  [In-window messages](/meta/windows-and-pricing#in-window-messages-become-chargeable-on-1-october-2026)

**Improved**

* **A message that was not delivered says why,** in WhatsApp's words first and
  ours second. [When a message isn't delivered](/whatsapp/not-delivered)
* **Marketing broadcasts go through Meta's marketing API,** at the same price,
  with nothing to switch on. [Broadcasts](/whatsapp/broadcasts#how-marketing-broadcasts-are-sent)
* **The email test goes to every address** and says "accepted" rather than
  "delivered", because that is all we can know.
  [Notifications](/workspace/notifications)


# What's New
Source: https://docs.thinnest.ai/whats-new/index

The latest changes to ThinnestAI, newest first: October 6 to November 14, 2026.

This is what changed in ThinnestAI, in plain words, with a link to the page that
explains each thing. Earlier changes are on [Early October](/whats-new/early-october)
and [Late September](/whats-new/late-september).

**Nov 14, 2026**

Studio voices on every plan; one Studio catalogue in every market

**Changed**

* **Studio voices on every plan**, including the free trial. Only cloning your own voice needs the Pro plan or
  above. [Voice](/channels/voice#voice)
* **One Studio catalogue in every market.** Every Studio voice speaks all 63 Studio languages, shows its accent and
  flag, and choosing a language puts its native voices first. Studio voices have no sample to play; use **Test a
  call**. An agent whose Studio voice is no longer listed answers in a voice of the same gender until you choose a
  new one. [Studio voices and languages](/channels/voice#studio-voices-and-languages)
* **Voice clone languages** are now the languages Studio speaks on a call, in every market. [Languages](/channels/voice-clone#languages)
* **Browse voices**: search and filters sit on one line, and **Select voice** is above the language list.

**Nov 10, 2026**

Standard voices; see every tool the agent ran; reset or delete a conversation

**New**

* **Standard voices.** A new tab in every voice picker, first in the list, with twenty natural voices that read all
  eleven Indian languages. Standard costs less per minute than Premium, and less again on a number you imported and on
  web calls, since no line of ours is used. For workspaces billed in rupees. [Voice](/channels/voice)
* **See what the agent did.** Every tool the agent runs (checking a calendar, booking, saving a lead, your own
  actions) is now logged, with what it sent, what came back, and why it failed when it did. Open **Tools** at the top
  of a conversation in the Inbox, or the **Tools** tab of a call in Usage. [Inbox](/workspace/inbox#what-the-agent-did)
* **Reset the agent's memory**, for one conversation or for everything about a number, so a test from your own phone
  starts clean. Nothing is deleted. [Inbox](/workspace/inbox#resetting-the-agents-memory)
* **Delete a conversation** for good, with its calls and recordings. Owners and admins.
  [Inbox](/workspace/inbox#deleting-a-conversation)

**Nov 4, 2026**

Several agents call out from one number; a ring-back reaches the agent that called; no daily limit per number

**New**

* **Several agents can call out from one number at once.** [Place Call](/api-reference) now accepts, as `from`, any
  number your workspace holds and can call from — lent to that agent or not. One agent can answer the number while
  others call out from it, with no lending. [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers#inbound-and-outbound-are-separate)
* **A ring-back can reach the agent that called.** Set a number's `ringBack` to `last_caller` and a person ringing it
  back reaches the agent that called them from it in the last 30 days, not the number's answering agent. Off unless
  you turn it on. [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers#inbound-and-outbound-are-separate)

**Changed**

* **No daily limit per number.** A number is no longer stopped at 200 calls a day, and the `number_daily_limit` error
  is gone. Campaigns still spread their calls across an agent's numbers and keep each person on one number.
  [Voice campaigns](/channels/voice-campaigns)
* **A waiting call keeps its number.** A call waiting to be placed that named a number rings from it as long as the
  workspace still holds it, even if the number was lent to another agent meanwhile.

**Oct 29, 2026**

Insights: what your calls came to, and a follow-up list; workflows start from a webhook or a schedule, and save to your CRM

**New**

* **Insights.** Switch on **Call insights** for an agent and every answered call is noted: how it ended, the objections
  in the customer's words, why a no was a no, what is broken on the customer's side, and the next step with its day.
  **Insights** in the sidebar adds it up for 7, 30 or 90 days, keeps a follow-up list for the team, and downloads as a
  CSV. Each call in **Usage** shows its own. [Insights](/agent/insights)
* **Insights in the API.** `insights` comes on `call.analysed`, Get Call and Get Call Analysis.
  [Webhooks](/api-reference/webhooks)
* **Review decisions.** Mark whether AI decides got recent calls right, and it finds the lowest confidence bar that
  keeps the answers above it right as often as you need. [Workflows](/agent/workflows)
* **Workflows start more ways.** From a webhook your system or a form tool posts to, on a schedule, or on a date a
  contact holds (a birthday, a renewal), in the contact's own clock. **Await** waits for a reply, a form, a call or an
  event your system sends. [Workflows](/agent/workflows)
* **Workflows reach your tools.** **Send to CRM** saves the contact to the agent's CRM (Zoho, Bigin or HubSpot), and
  **Book on calendar** books on its Cal.com or Calendly. **Tell the team** and **Assign to a team** hand a contact to
  people. [CRM](/agent/crm) · [Calendar](/agent/calendar)
* **Contacts keep their own details**, imported from any column, and agent calls read them.
* **Conversation budget.** Set what one conversation may cost you in a day; past it the agent answers on a lighter
  model, and never goes quiet. **Agents** → the agent → **Settings**. [Agent behaviour](/agent/behaviour#conversation-budget)

**Oct 28, 2026**

Workflows: call, message and follow up with each contact over days, with AI reading every call

**New**

* **Workflows.** Draw a journey that takes each contact through on their own: Agent calls them, AI reads the call and
  decides how it went, the workflow waits, sends a WhatsApp or an SMS, calls again. Start it for a contact group or a
  tag, or let a tag being added, a call ending or a form being sent start it. Test it on your own phone, follow every
  contact under **Runs**, and see the last 30 days on the canvas with **Results**. Six ready-made workflows to start
  from. [Workflows](/agent/workflows)
* **Describe it, and AI builds it.** Say what the workflow should do in a few sentences and AI draws it, with your
  agents and templates chosen by name — a draft to look over and publish.
* **AI decides.** Name the answers — *Interested*, *Call back later*, *Not interested* — and AI reads the call and picks
  one, with how sure it is. Below the confidence you set, it takes **Unsure**, which you connect like any other path.
* **Your agents don't change.** A call a workflow places is the agent's call in every way; on those calls the agent's
  own After the call messages are left to the workflow, so nobody gets both.
* **API.** [Start a Workflow Run](/api-reference/workflows/start-a-workflow-run) starts one contact through a workflow
  published with *Start when: Your system asks*; a new number becomes a contact. Also the MCP tool `start_workflow_run`
  and `workflows.startRun` in the SDKs. [List Workflows](/api-reference/workflows/list-workflows) and
  [Get a Workflow](/api-reference/workflows/get-a-workflow) find a workflow's id (MCP `list_workflows`).

**Oct 27, 2026**

Voices for more languages outside India; the call settings move to the Playground, with one Save for everything; help text in (i) tooltips across the agent pages; several WhatsApp and SMS messages after a call; where the time went in each turn of a call

**New**

* **Voices for more languages.** If your business is billed outside India, the Studio catalogue speaks fifteen
  languages best. For the others, a call now answers in a voice of the same gender from a second set made for them,
  and **Browse voices** lists that set under each of those languages. These voices have no sample to play.
  [Studio voices and languages](/channels/voice#studio-voices-and-languages)
* **Clone a voice in more languages.** Bosnian and Sundanese join the list outside India, and a clone in any language
  outside those fifteen is made with the second set, at the same rate. [Languages](/channels/voice-clone#languages)
* **API.** [`GET /voices`](/api-reference/voices/list-voices) lists the second set with `languages`, the languages each is
  offered for, and an empty `accent`.
* **Several messages after a call.** The **After the call** card on an agent's Actions page now sends up to 3 WhatsApp
  templates and up to 3 SMS templates when a call ends, in the order you tick them, each with its own blanks. They go
  out as one set: once per call, never to your do-not-contact list, at most once a day to the same number.
  [After the call](/agent/after-the-call)
* **Choose what Agent may send during a call.** A **During the call** card on the Actions page's **On calls** tab holds
  the WhatsApp and SMS switches, with a list to tick the templates Agent may pick from while it talks to a customer.
* **API.** [Update Post-call Settings](/api-reference/post-call/update-post-call-settings) takes `followUp.whatsappTemplates`
  and `followUp.smsTemplates`, lists of up to 3. `whatsapp` and `sms` still work and mean the first of the list.
* **Where the time went in each turn.** Open a call in Usage and, under **How the call went**, open **Where the time went
  in each turn**. For every turn it shows when the first word of the actual answer was heard, when the first sound of any
  kind was (a thinking line or an acknowledgement that plays first no longer passes for the answer), how long the turn took
  to be decided, Ear's check, the model's first sentence and the voice. It is recorded for calls made from now on, and not
  for speech-to-speech calls; an older call says nothing was recorded. [Usage](/workspace/usage#how-a-call-went)
* **The time to the answer, in the API.** [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call) and the `call.completed` and
  `call.analysed` webhooks carry `quality.answerMs`, the wait to the first word of the actual answer (`responseMs` still
  stops at the first sound of any kind), and `quality.knowledgeTurns`, the turns that looked something up in the agent's
  knowledge. [Get Call Timeline](/api-reference/calls/get-call-timeline) returns every turn's timing.
* **Knowledge on calls from the API.** [Update Built-in Tools](/api-reference/tools/update-built-in-tools) takes
  `knowledgeOnCalls` to switch the agent's knowledge search on or off during calls; chat is not affected.

**Changed**

* **Call settings are on the Playground.** How the agent speaks, listening and turn detection, sound and recording, ending calls, memory, and call length and silence are now cards on the agent's Playground, under the model, voice and instructions. One **Save changes** saves the whole page, and **Test a call** saves any unsaved change before it dials. The **Voice** page keeps whether the agent answers and where. [Where the call settings are](/channels/voice#where-the-call-settings-are)
* **Help text in (i) tooltips.** On the agent pages, the grey line that explained a card or a field is now an (i) beside its title. Hover it, tab to it, or tap it on a phone. Warnings, live counts and empty states stay on the page.
* **Send after** on the After the call card is a list you tick: calls somebody answered, missed calls, or both.
* **Save appears only when there is something to save** on the After the call and Hand calls to another agent cards.

**Oct 26, 2026**

One app for every country: sign up at app.thinnest.ai and pick the country your business is billed in

**Changed**

* **One app, one address.** ThinnestAI is now a single app at `app.thinnest.ai` for every country. The sign-up page asks which country your business is billed in: India is billed in rupees, everywhere else in US dollars. The API is at `https://app.thinnest.ai/api/v1` for every workspace. `dashboard.thinnest.ai` now sends you to `app.thinnest.ai`, and its API address keeps working. [Where you are billed](/workspace/regions)

**Oct 24, 2026**

Every phone number carries its country code, with a country list in the console; the API refuses a number without one; an international site; resellers paid through their own Dodo Payments account

**Changed**

* **The API refuses a phone number without its country code.** Send every number with its code, like
  `+44 7700 900123` or `+91 98765 43210` (full international digits without the `+` work too). A
  number like `9876543210` used to be read as Indian; it is now refused with a message saying how to
  write it. This covers placing calls, batch calls, contacts, the do-not-call list, WhatsApp messages
  and one-time codes, and importing a phone number. [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers#country-codes)
* **A country list beside every number box in the console.** Importing a number, adding or importing
  contacts, the do-not-contact list, a calling campaign's list, sending a WhatsApp message and the
  Playground's test call each have a country list with flags, starting on your workspace's country.
  A number typed without a code takes the country picked there.
  [Phone numbers](/channels/phone-numbers#country-codes)

**New**

* **An international site** at `dashboard.thinnest.ai`, with billing in US dollars,
  ten British voices, and WhatsApp priced from Meta's own published rates for every country. Buying a number there is coming soon; bring one you already own. The sign-up and
  log-in pages name the region you are on, with a link to the other. [Regions](/workspace/regions)
* **Resellers on the international site are paid through their own Dodo Payments account**, under
  their own business name. A reseller with no payment account has its clients' usage charged to its
  own balance, so a client is never stopped for its own balance. [Your prices](/white-label/prices#paid-through-dodo-international)

**Oct 23, 2026**

Speech-to-speech calls with OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini; speech-to-speech on the Enterprise plan only for now; unused Pro and Scale credit rolls over for up to 3 months; standard voices retired

**New**

* **Speech-to-speech calls with OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini.** A second model that hears and speaks,
  at a lower rate a minute than GPT-Live-1, with the phone line included (per second on web,
  30-second blocks on phone), on the Enterprise plan. It takes turns: callers can cut in, but it does not
  listen while it speaks. It answers simple things itself and uses your agent's knowledge and
  actions for the rest, and never states a fact your agent has not given it.
  Its ten voices speak every language. Its own call settings, **Realtime session** on the
  Playground, set its noise reduction, how it knows the caller has finished, an idle timeout,
  interruptions, the caller transcript, reply length, speaking speed and what a long call keeps;
  on this model they replace the Voice page's fillers and listening settings.
  Through the API: the model `openai-gpt-realtime-mini`, `voice.realtimeVoice` and
  `voice.realtimeSession`. [Voice](/channels/voice#speech-to-speech-openai-gpt-realtime-mini)

**Changed**

* **Speech-to-speech models are on the Enterprise plan only, for now.** OpenAI GPT-Live-1 and
  OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini have left the Model picker and List Models while they are tested
  further; we set them up on Enterprise agents. An agent already on one keeps it, and its calls
  run and bill as before. Through the API, a realtime model is refused as a new choice with
  "… is not available yet." [Voice](/channels/voice#speech-to-speech-openai-gpt-live-1)

* **Unused plan credit rolls over.** The usage credit that Pro and Scale give each period
  used to expire at the end of that period. Now unused credit rolls over for up to 3 months
  while your paid subscription remains active, and each period's credit expires at the end of
  its own 3-month window. A renewal adds the new credit on top of what is left, the oldest
  credit is spent first, and money you topped up is never touched. If you cancel, what is left
  lasts until the end of the period you have paid for. Through the API, `creditExpiresAt` on
  [Get Usage](/api-reference/usage/get-usage) is the earliest date any of your credit
  expires. [Usage](/workspace/usage#plan-credit)

* **Standard voices are retired.** Every voice call is now billed at the Premium or the Studio
  rate — see Pricing. An agent that spoke with a standard voice has been moved to a similar Premium
  voice automatically. The model no longer changes a call's rate: only a Studio voice (one of ours
  or your own clone) makes a call Studio. The Scale plan pays the same voice rates as every other
  plan. Through the API, [List Models](/api-reference/models/list-models) returns `callTier` as
  `premium` for every model, with the Premium price, and
  [List Voices](/api-reference/voices/list-voices) lists only `premium` and `studio` voices; `tier`
  is never `standard`. [Voice](/channels/voice#voice)

**Oct 22, 2026**

Speech-to-speech calls with OpenAI GPT-Live-1; early answers can be switched off; no limit on the Playground's instructions

**New**

* **Speech-to-speech calls with OpenAI GPT-Live-1.** An agent can answer
  calls with one model that hears and speaks, listens while it talks, and still uses your
  agent's instructions, knowledge and actions. It speaks in its own voices, Indian voices
  first, and is billed at one flat rate a minute with the phone line included (per second on web,
  30-second blocks on phone). On the Enterprise plan only for now (see Oct 23). Fillers, speaking
  speed, Ear mode, early answers, digit hold, the interruption and silence settings and end phrases
  are shown greyed out on it, with the reason.
  Through the API: the model `openai-gpt-live-1`, `voice.realtimeVoice`, and `billing.billedOn`
  and `billing.chargedMicro` on a call. [Voice](/channels/voice#speech-to-speech-openai-gpt-live-1)
* **Early answers, on or off.** The agent starts its reply on what it has heard so far and
  throws it away if the caller goes on; the tokens of a thrown-away reply are billed to your
  own model key on an agent that uses one, and are not in the call's `usage`. Switch **Early
  answers** off on the Voice page, or send `voice.earlyAnswers: false`, to start a reply only
  once the caller has finished. On by default. [Voice](/channels/voice#early-answers)
* **What each call was about, in the export.** The call export from Usage (and
  `GET /v1/usage/calls?format=csv`) now ends with the call's summary and a column for each
  detail the agent collected, such as the caller's name or the reason they called. The
  columns before them are unchanged. [Usage](/workspace/usage)
* **Billing details in Settings.** A billing name, so invoices can carry your company's
  legal name rather than the workspace name, and your GST number, both in Settings →
  General before the billing address. [Usage](/workspace/usage)
* **No character limit on the Playground's instructions.** Saving from the agent page no longer
  refuses long instructions, and the box shows only the count. The API still accepts up to
  20,000 characters. [Behaviour](/agent/behaviour)

**Oct 21, 2026**

Your own lead and hand-over rules, Test Chat as a call, the number a caller rang

**New**

* **`ownRules`: leave our lead and hand-over sentences out.** If you write those rules
  yourself, set `ownRules: true` on Create Agent or Update Agent and the agent is no
  longer told to refuse names and numbers, to never promise a follow-up or when to hand
  over. The boundary, the AI disclosure, the reply language and the date stay. Off by
  default. [Behaviour](/agent/behaviour#writing-your-own-lead-and-hand-over-rules)
* **Test Chat as a call.** `mode: "call"` runs a test turn with the agent's call prompt
  and the thinking level a call uses, so you can try wording the way a caller will get
  it. [Test chat](/agent/custom-api#during-a-test-chat)
* **The number a caller rang.** Get Call and List Calls now carry `to`: your number a
  call came in on, so a workspace with several numbers can tell which line it was.
  Calls from before today have it empty.

**Improved**

* **A forward under your own keys** is billed at the flat price of those keys, not the
  agent's voice plan. [Forwarding a whole line](/channels/phone-numbers#forwarding-a-whole-line)

**Oct 19, 2026**

Webhooks, forwarded calls and Test Chat

**Fixed**

* **Choosing `contact.erased` or `byok.changed` on a webhook.** Create Webhook and Update
  Webhook answered `500` when an endpoint named either event. Both are saved now.
  [Webhooks](/api-reference/webhooks)

**Improved**

* **What a forwarded call costs is spelled out.** A call forwarded to a phone on a number
  we rent is billed for every connected second at the voice plan of the agent attached to
  the number, or the Standard plan when none is (the flat own-key price where your own
  keys apply); it is not the carrier-only charge, and it is not recorded. [Forwarding a whole line](/channels/phone-numbers#forwarding-a-whole-line)
* **Rent Phone Number takes an `Idempotency-Key`,** so a retry returns the first answer
  instead of renting a second number.
* **A shared voice clone keeps your own voice `id`** inside every customer.
  [Voice cloning](/channels/voice-clone#your-customers-can-use-your-voices)
* **Lending a number to a second agent ends no call.** A call waiting to be placed that
  named that number fails with a clear message. [Numbers](/channels/phone-numbers)
* **Test Chat** says that it runs the agent as saved, and what a reply costs on your own
  model key.

**Oct 17, 2026**

Languages and re-ask on the API, clearer billing notes

**New**

* **Reply languages on the API.** `languages` on Create Agent and Update Agent sets the
  console's "one, or up to four": `[]` for auto, one name for that language, two to
  four for the languages the agent expects, the first being its fallback. Get Agent
  returns it. [Behaviour](/agent/behaviour#reply-language)
* **`billing` on List Calls.** Every call in the list now carries what it was billed as
  (the key choice, the voice plan, the per-minute rate, the billed seconds and the
  currency), the same object as Get Call, so reconciling a page of calls needs no
  call per row.
* **`voice.reaskAfterSeconds` is in the API reference.** It could already be set; it was
  missing from the schema. [Voice](/channels/voice)

**Improved**

* **What a call was billed as is clearer.** A call that ended before the agent spoke is
  charged the carrier's fee only, in 30-second blocks. A free trial call is one paid
  from a free-plan workspace's trial minutes.

**Fixed**

* **Update Agent's own-model response.** The `409` for the agent's own model said the
  workspace was "not using its own voice key". It now says the language-model key
  is the one that is missing.

**Oct 15, 2026**

Find leads: describe the businesses you want and your agent finds them

**New**

* **Find leads.** Describe the businesses you want to reach — "real-estate
  developers in Pune" — and an agent finds them and brings back their phone numbers
  and emails, with a link to where each came from. Save them to Contacts and a group, then call them with an agent
  or send them a WhatsApp broadcast. The first 50 are free in your first month;
  after that ₹1 a lead, and you only pay for leads that have a phone number or
  email. [Find leads](/agent/find-leads)
* **Save a search and run it again.** Name a search to keep it on the start screen;
  running it again charges only for businesses you do not already have.
  [Find leads](/agent/find-leads#save-a-search-run-it-again)

**Improved**

* **Leads has two tabs.** **Find leads** is first; the people who came to your
  agents are on **Inbound leads**. [Leads and contacts](/agent/leads)

**Oct 15, 2026**

What each call was billed as; delete one call's content; shorter retention; developers' voices for their customers; two new webhooks

**New**

* **What each call was billed as.** Get Call and the `call.analysed` webhook now
  carry `billing`: whose keys the call ran on (`keys`: `off` for ours, or `all`,
  `voice`, `llm`, `llm_voice`), the voice plan it was priced on (`voicePlan`;
  null on the flat own-key prices), its per-minute rate fixed when it started
  (`ratePerMinuteMicro`) and the seconds it was charged for (`billedSeconds`).
  [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call)
* **Characters sent to the voice, per call.** `usage.ttsCharacters` counts the
  text sent to the voice to be spoken — replies, the greeting and fixed lines —
  on your own voice key too. It includes sentences sent before the caller
  interrupted, which is what voice providers charge for.
  [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call)
* **Estimated token counts are marked.** `usage.inputTokensEstimated` is `true`
  when part of a call's input token count was estimated because the model's
  provider reported none. [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call)
* **`contact.erased` webhook.** Sent once a contact you deleted is gone
  completely, recordings included — straight away, or after the nightly retry
  when a recording could not be deleted at once. Only the contact's id and when.
  [Webhooks](/api-reference/webhooks#workspace-events)
* **`byok.changed` webhook.** Sent when one of your own keys is added, replaced,
  removed or refused by its provider, and when your own keys are switched on or
  off or set to cover different jobs. Never carries a key.
  [Webhooks](/api-reference/webhooks#workspace-events)
* **Delete one call's recording and transcript.** `DELETE /calls/{id}/content`
  removes a call's recording, its turns, its summary and the details collected
  from it, and keeps the call's billing record. Get Call then shows
  `contentDeleted: true`. [Your data](/workspace/data-and-erasure#deleting-one-calls-recording-and-transcript)
* **Keep calls for less time.** Set `callRetentionDays` on your workspace to
  delete calls' recordings and transcripts sooner than your plan does, from
  1 day up to your plan's limit. [How long calls are kept](/workspace/data-and-erasure#how-long-calls-are-kept)
* **Your customers can use your cloned voices.** Every voice a developer clones
  can now be used by all its customer workspaces, marked
  `sharedFromDeveloper` in `GET /voices`. Only the developer can rename or
  delete it. [Voice Clone](/channels/voice-clone#your-customers-can-use-your-voices)
* **Your own voices are marked.** Each voice in `GET /byok/voices` now says
  `own`: `true` for a voice you cloned or designed on your provider account
  (Cartesia, ElevenLabs, Soniox), `false` for the provider's library.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys#voices)

**Oct 14, 2026**

Speaking speed; the agent stops sooner, and at once, when a caller talks over it

**New**

* **Over two hundred more Premium voices.** Named for the voice and its style, with the accent (Hindi, Indian English,
  Hindi–English mix and seven more Indian languages) in the hover text beside what it is for: conversational, customer
  care, sales, banking, narrator, news and more. Search the Premium tab by accent or style. Voices you already use are unchanged.
  [Voices](/guides/how-your-agent-sounds#pick-the-voice-by-listening)
* **A question with no answer is asked again.** When the agent asks something
  on a call and hears nothing, it asks the same question again after 2.5
  seconds, once — instead of waiting in silence for your "Are you still there?".
  Change the wait, or turn it off, on the Voice page. Through the API,
  `voice.reaskAfterSeconds`. [Voice](/channels/voice#your-own-limits)
* **An agent can speak a few languages.** The language picker on the Playground
  and Settings now takes up to four. The agent answers in whichever of them the
  customer speaks, and falls back to the first; on a call the speech recogniser
  listens only for those, so a short reply is no longer written down in a
  language nobody on the call speaks. [Reply language](/agent/behaviour#reply-language)
* **Speaking speed.** Set how fast your agent talks on calls with a slider, from
  slower to faster, on the Playground, right under the voice. Most Standard and
  Premium voices follow it. Through the API,
  `voice.speakingSpeed`. [Voice](/channels/voice#speaking-speed)

**Improved**

* **"Are you still there?" in the call's language.** On a call where the caller
  had not yet said anything the agent could read the language from, it used to
  ask in English; it now asks in the language of its own opening line.
  [Voice](/channels/voice#your-own-limits)
* **The agent stops while a website caller is still talking over it.** It used to
  finish its sentence and stop only once the caller had finished theirs. Now it
  stops once they have talked over it for about as long as your **Words needed to
  cut the agent off** — a hum or a quick "okay" still changes nothing — and if it
  was stopped by something that was not words, it asks the caller to go on.
  [Interrupting](/channels/voice#interrupting)
* **Ear mode listens in real time, and phone callers can stop the agent
  mid-sentence too.** An agent set to **Ear** under **How agent knows the caller
  has finished** stops as soon as it has heard enough of the caller's words, or a
  "wait", usually a second or two in, instead of once they have finished. It
  ignores its own voice coming back down the line, lets a listener's "haan ji,
  bilkul" pass without stopping, and waits through a pause mid-thought instead of
  answering half a sentence — saying a short "haan ji" while it waits. Ear is
  billed at the rate of the voice, like any other call. Both behaviours have a switch and a box for your own words —
  **Backchannel detection** with **Caller backchannel words**, and **Agent speaks
  backchannel / acknowledgement while the caller explains** with **Agent
  backchannel phrases** — and API fields to match.
  [Ear: real-time speech recognition](/channels/voice#ear-real-time-speech-recognition)
* **The agent goes quiet the instant it is interrupted.** On some voices it used
  to carry on for up to half a second before stopping.
* **The agent's "haan ji" now comes while the caller is still talking.** With
  **Agent speaks backchannel / acknowledgement while the caller explains** on, it
  used to wait for a long pause that someone explaining something rarely makes,
  so it almost never spoke. On website calls it now says its word in the short
  gaps between a caller's sentences, once they have been talking for a few
  seconds, at most twice in a turn; it does not count as the caller being
  interrupted. On a phone call it still waits for a longer pause.
  [Ear: real-time speech recognition](/channels/voice#ear-real-time-speech-recognition)
* **Replies start sooner.** The agent now starts working on its answer the
  moment it has heard what the caller said, while it is still making sure they
  have finished, so the first words come a fifth of a second or so earlier on
  every turn, whichever model your agent uses. If the caller was not finished,
  that early answer is dropped and never spoken or recorded. The short silence
  some voices put in front of each reply is no longer played, which saves up to
  most of a second on those voices.

**Oct 13, 2026**

Warm and cold hand-offs; Actions, Voice and Playground, redesigned

**New**

* **Bring your own language model and voice together.** A new set for bring your own
  keys: your LLM account answers and your voice account speaks, while we keep the
  speech recogniser. A call is a flat ₹1 a minute, as with all three keys, on any
  model your key offers. Choose **My voice and my language model** in **Settings →
  Your keys**, or `scope: "llm_voice"` on the API.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **Each agent chooses how it uses your keys.** The scope you pick for the
  workspace is the default; an agent can follow it, be switched off your keys, or
  use a different set your saved keys allow, so one agent can run on your language
  model while another uses your language model and your voice. In the console it
  is **How Agent uses your keys** on the agent's pages; in the API, the agent's
  `byok` is `null` (follow the workspace), `"off"`, or a scope, and a scope your
  keys cannot serve is refused with the missing key named.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **Tokens used on every call.** Get Call and the `call.analysed` webhook now carry
  `usage`: the `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` and `cachedInputTokens` the call's
  replies used, including on your own model key, each null when not recorded.
  [Get Call](/api-reference/calls/get-call)
* **Warm or cold, when a call is handed on.** Each agent a call can be handed to
  is **warm** (it gets a short summary and the conversation, and opens by saying
  who it is and why the caller is there) or **cold** (it starts fresh and greets
  the caller as on a new call). [Voice](/channels/voice#handing-a-call-on)
* **Warm transfers to a person.** With **Call transfer**, the person who answers
  can first hear a short spoken summary of the call before the caller is
  connected, and with **Press 1 to accept** the caller is connected only once
  they press 1, so a voicemail never takes the call. Cold, as before, stays the
  default. [Escalation](/agent/escalation#on-a-phone-call-putting-the-caller-through)
* **In the API**, `handOver.transferMode`, `handOver.acceptKey` and each hand-off
  agent's `mode`; `handedTo` on calls now says each hand-off's `mode` and `summary`.
  [Update Built-in Tools](/api-reference/tools/update-built-in-tools)

**Improved**

* **The Actions page is in three tabs.** **Built in**, **On calls** and **Connect a
  service**, with the open tab kept in the address. A line under the title shows
  how many tools are on, how many services are connected and how many agents calls
  can be handed to, and a tool that is on but missing something it needs shows an
  amber **Not in use yet**. [Actions](/agent/actions)
* **The Voice page is in seven sections.** Calls, How Agent speaks, Listening, Sound
  and recording, Ending calls, Memory, and Call length and silence, with links
  along the top, **Save changes** always in view, and **Test a call** staying
  in view beside the settings on a wide screen (first, above them, on a narrower one). [Voice](/channels/voice)
* **The Playground is in four cards.** Language and model, Voice, What Agent says,
  and Reply length. The page used to say changes save immediately; they apply
  once you press **Save changes**. [Behaviour](/agent/behaviour)
* **More room inside an agent.** The workspace sidebar shrinks to icons while you
  are inside an agent, next to the agent's own menu. Open it any time with the
  toggle; the sidebar on every other page stays as you left it.
* **Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin sit side by side** under a **CRM** heading, like
  Calendar and Spreadsheet, instead of stretching across the page.
* **Labels name the agent** where they said "it": **How Agent should speak**,
  **What Agent says**, **Message when Agent is off**.

**Fixed**

* **The "How Agent should speak" box on the Voice page scrolls** once it is tall,
  as it was always meant to. It had grown to show every rule at once.

**Oct 12, 2026**

Calls that read better, an own-voice tuning panel, safer do-not-call

**New**

* **Bring only your own language model.** Use your own LLM account, such as Gemini
  or OpenAI, while we keep the speech recogniser and the voice. Calls stay on the
  same per-minute voice plan as any other call (Standard, Premium or Studio), whatever
  model your key runs, and chat replies cost ₹0.02. Choose it in **Settings → Your
  keys**, or with `scope: "llm"` on the API.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **Tune your own Cartesia voice for each agent.** Speed, volume, emotion, the
  Sonic model (including `sonic-3.6`) and a pronunciation dictionary can be set
  per agent in the console, through the API and in MCP, and heard in the console
  and the API before you save. [Tune a Cartesia voice](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **The who-is-calling lookup moved to the Actions page.** It is now a card of its
  own there, no longer on the Voice page; nothing about how it works changed.
  [Who-is-calling lookup](/channels/voice#who-is-calling-lookup)
* **Choose how the agent decides the caller has finished speaking.** `voice.turnDetection`
  (Smart, Timer or Ear) is now on the API next to the silence setting.
  [Voice](/channels/voice)
* **Switch off the do-not-call tool for an agent.** `voice.recordDoNotCall` and a
  switch on the Voice page. The `contact.opted_out` webhook now carries the words
  the caller used, so you can see why a number was added.
  [Voice](/channels/voice) and [Webhooks](/api-reference/webhooks)
* **A reply in your customer's language in chat.** With **Match the customer**,
  website chat, WhatsApp, Telegram, the Playground and test chat now answer in the
  language of a message written in an Indian script. Messages typed in English
  letters are left to the agent's judgement. [Reply language](/agent/behaviour#reply-language)

**Improved**

* **The agent asks before adding someone to the do-not-call list.** "That's all,
  you can hang up" no longer counts as "do not call me again", and the agent
  quotes the caller's words when it does add a number.
* **What was never heard is no longer treated as said.** When a caller talks over
  the agent, the agent now knows which part was cut off and the transcript is
  corrected to the part the caller heard where it can be.
  [Voice](/channels/voice)
* **Stage directions are not read aloud.** Text such as `[pause]` or
  "(waiting for your response)", and a model's visible "thinking", is removed
  before the agent speaks and before it is saved, while ordinary brackets such as
  "(Monday to Friday)" and "\[1]" stay.
* **Goodbyes in more languages.** Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali and
  Marathi closings now end a call properly. The short fixed lines the agent
  falls back on ("I am having trouble", a goodbye) are also written in Hindi and
  Telugu; if you hear a wording you would change, tell us.
* **Gemini on your own key** is asked to think less on a call, for the models
  where Google allows it.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)

**Fixed**

* **A reply that was retried on a backup model no longer runs together.** The same
  sentence could be said, and stored, twice with no space between the pieces.
* **"I'll take care of that" no longer ends a call** as if it were a goodbye.

**Oct 10-11, 2026**

Every Voice page setting on the API, a test-chat marker, model call prices

**New**

* **Every setting on the Voice page can now be read and changed through the API
  and the MCP server.** Fillers and their timing, how long a pause ends the
  caller's turn, how many words cut the agent off, never interrupt, the
  background sound and its volume, hanging up when the conversation ends,
  asking "are you still there?", ending a call on silence or on a phrase, and
  the call instructions. A read returns every value with its default filled in,
  and a number outside its range is refused with a message instead of being
  moved. [Voice](/channels/voice#the-settings) and
  [Update Agent](/api-reference/agents/update-agent)
* **Choose where an agent answers calls.** `voice.surfaces` sets phone, your
  website's call button and WhatsApp calls. Adding the phone to an agent that
  answers calls but has no number is refused with the code
  `phone_number_required`. [Where it answers](/channels/voice#turn-it-on) and
  [Errors](/api-reference/errors)
* **Your endpoint can tell a test chat from a real customer.** Every action
  request made during an API test chat carries an `X-Test-Chat: true` header, and
  `{{test.chat}}` fills as `true`, so you can answer without writing anything to
  your system. [During a test chat](/agent/custom-api#during-a-test-chat)
* **Each model shows what a call on it costs.** `GET /models` now returns
  `callTier`, `callPricePerMinuteMicro` and `currency` (the currency of the
  wallet your calls are charged to). A model marked premium puts every call on the
  premium rate. A workspace using its own keys is billed the BYOK rate whatever
  the model. [Model](/agent/behaviour#model)
* **Your own cloned voices on Cartesia.** The voice list starts with the voices
  you cloned and then reads the whole library, and a clone can be set on an
  agent. [Choose an agent's voice](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys#choose-an-agents-voice)

**Improved**

* **Agent instructions can be 20,000 characters in the console too.** The box
  used to stop at 8,000 while the API accepted more. Conversation steps are limited
  separately. [Instructions](/agent/behaviour#instructions)

* **A forwarded call on a number with no agent** appears in Usage, Get Call and
  the call list with no agent, and does not create an inbox conversation or a
  webhook. [Forwarding a whole line](/channels/phone-numbers#forwarding-a-whole-line)
  **Fixed**

* **Studio voices need the Pro plan or above,** not Scale as one guide said.
  [How your agent sounds](/guides/how-your-agent-sounds)

* **A cloned Cartesia voice that was missing from the list,** and so was refused
  when you set it on an agent, is listed and accepted.
  [Choose an agent's voice](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys#choose-an-agents-voice)

* **The background sound's volume now shows what callers actually hear.** The
  Voice page slider and the API report 15% (0.15) when you have not set one; the
  page used to show 18%. [Background sound](/channels/voice#background-sound)

**Oct 9, 2026**

Callers by name, call hand-offs, forwarding, contact groups

**New**

* **Your agent knows who is calling.** When someone rings from a number saved in
  your Contacts, the agent is told their name and can greet them with it. It is
  also told to confirm who it is talking to before discussing an account, because
  a caller's number can be faked. [Who is calling](/channels/voice#who-is-calling)
* **Look the caller up in your own system.** Give an agent a web address and we
  ask your system who is calling before the agent answers, so it can open with
  their last order or their plan. You have two seconds to reply, and the request
  is signed so you know it came from us.
  [Who-is-calling lookup](/channels/voice#who-is-calling-lookup)
* **Hand a call to another of your agents.** Sales can pass a caller to support
  in the middle of a call. It is the same line and the same conversation, and the
  other agent sees everything said so far.
  [Handing a call on](/channels/voice#handing-a-call-on)
* **Forward a whole phone line.** Choose **Forward calls** in a number's menu
  and every call to it rings a phone of your choice, with no agent speaking. It
  works whether or not an agent answers the number, so use it as a fallback while
  you fix or switch off an agent.
  [Forwarding a whole line](/channels/phone-numbers#forwarding-a-whole-line)
* **Set how long outbound calls ring.** Between 10 and 60 seconds, for an agent
  on the Voice page or for one call through the API. Calls now stop ringing
  after 30 seconds unless you set it; on some carriers they used to ring longer.
  [How long it rings](/channels/voice#how-long-it-rings)
* **Move a number between your customers.** If you build on the developer API, a
  number can move between your workspace and your customers' workspaces and keep
  its digits, from the number's menu or the API.
  [Moving a number](/channels/phone-numbers#moving-a-number-to-another-workspace)
* **See how each call went.** Open a call in Usage to see who it was handed to
  or forwarded to, how long the caller waited for each reply, long silences,
  interruptions and any replies that needed a backup. A new `call.problem` webhook tells you the moment something
  goes wrong on a live call.
  [How a call went](/workspace/usage#how-a-call-went)
* **Contact groups.** Build named lists of contacts, such as "Wholesale buyers",
  and aim a broadcast or a voice campaign at exactly those people.
  [Groups](/agent/leads#groups)

**Improved**

* **Every webhook event has a documented example,** and the ids in webhooks
  always carry their `conv_` or `cmp_` prefix, so a value from a webhook can go
  straight into the API. [Event payloads](/api-reference/webhooks#event-payloads)
* **An agent that is on a live call cannot be deleted,** so a call is never cut
  off by a clean-up. The API says why in a clear error.
  [Errors](/api-reference/errors)
* **The Buy tab on Phone Numbers stays visible on a plan that cannot buy,** and
  tells you why, instead of disappearing.
  [Getting a number from us](/channels/phone-numbers#getting-a-number-from-us)

**Fixed**

* **A call from your website that never connects now gives up after 45
  seconds** and frees the line, instead of showing "Connecting" forever.
  Reloading the page ends a live call, and the "line busy" message names the
  limit. [A call button in your chat](/channels/voice#a-call-button-in-your-chat)

**Oct 8, 2026**

One language per agent, per-agent keys, erasure and error codes

**New**

* **Pick a language for each agent.** An agent has one language: choose it when
  you create the agent, on the Playground or in Settings, or leave it on **Match
  the customer**. The old "second language" setting is retired. You can also
  rename an agent from the sidebar. [Reply language](/agent/behaviour#reply-language)
* **Keep one agent off your own keys.** If your workspace brings its own provider
  keys, an individual agent can choose to stay on ours.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **Erase a contact, and their recordings go too.** Erasing a contact now also
  removes the recordings of their calls on numbers you brought. On pay-as-you-go,
  you can ask us to exclude your workspace from model training.
  [Data and erasure](/workspace/data-and-erasure)
* **Say what a switched-off line tells the caller.** When Answer calls is off,
  the caller hears a sentence you wrote, where the phone provider allows it.
  [When Answer calls is off](/channels/voice#when-answer-calls-is-off)
* **Every API refusal carries a code you can act on.** Branch on `code` rather
  than on the wording of the message. [Errors](/api-reference/errors)
* **Business details (KYC) for rented Indian numbers, by API.** Submit and
  follow the business details an Indian number needs, without the console.
  [India needs your business verified first](/channels/phone-numbers#india-needs-your-business-verified-first)

**Improved**

* **A WhatsApp template you sent looks the same in the inbox as it did to the
  customer,** with its picture, cards and buttons.
  [Inbox](/workspace/inbox)
* **The agent speaks sooner while it looks something up,** with its own wording
  or a short one of ours, and it no longer says a generic "I see" just before the
  answer. A new setting sets the gap before a second line.
  [Fillers before tool run](/channels/voice#fillers-before-tool-run)
* **A shorter wait before the agent's first answer on a call.**
  [Voice](/channels/voice)

**Fixed**

* **The agent no longer answers its own echo** on calls where the speech
  recogniser used to hear the agent's own voice as the caller.
* **A caller repeating the agent's words is no longer ignored.** Someone who
  answers "I would like to see the pediatrician" in the agent's own words now
  gets a reply. [Interrupting](/channels/voice#interrupting)

**Oct 7, 2026**

A full API reference, SDKs, texting the caller, new default voice

**New**

* **An API reference with a page for every endpoint.** About 180 operations,
  each with typed fields, cURL, JavaScript and Python examples, a **Try it**
  panel and sample responses. [API reference](/api-reference/introduction)
* **TypeScript and Python SDKs.** Every operation is a typed method, with
  retries and pagination built in. [SDKs](/api-reference/sdks)
* **Text the caller.** Your agent can send an SMS during a call, and a WhatsApp
  message or SMS after it ends, through your own SMS provider and sender ID.
  [SMS](/channels/sms), [After the call](/agent/after-the-call) and
  [a worked guide](/guides/text-the-caller)
* **The MCP server covers the whole console.** An AI assistant such as Claude
  Code or Cursor can now do almost anything you can do in the console, with your
  approval for anything that reaches a customer, including drafting and
  launching campaigns. [MCP tools](/mcp/tools)
* **Bring only your own voice.** Use your own voice account while we supply
  speech recognition, the model and the phone line, at ₹1.50 a minute. Calls run
  on low-cost models in this mode.
  [Bring your own keys](/api-reference/bring-your-own-keys)
* **Webhooks are signed with their delivery time** and carry an `evt_` id that
  stays the same across retries. [Delivery](/api-reference/webhooks#delivery)
* **Failed webhooks are retried, and you can send them again** yourself.
  [Retries](/api-reference/webhooks#retries)

**Improved**

* **New agents start on the Premium voice Kavya,** because the standard voices
